# AxiomDynamics — Master Licensing & Liability

**Docket position:** D08. Executed under the Comprehensive Master Contract (D07). Conversion mechanics in D05. Rate schedule annexed as A2.

> **Drafting status:** Commercial grade. The pricing structure and the liability split are settled; the language is not yet contract-grade. Requires conversion to enforceable terms by counsel before execution.

**Positioning:** This is not a SaaS product. AxiomDynamics is an engineering-discipline, agentic (non-LLM) predictive maintenance platform sold against multi-million-dollar CapEx/OpEx exposure. Licensing is tied to **operational assets monitored** and **documented outcomes prevented** — not to user seats.

---

## 1. Why Not SaaS

SaaS pricing (per seat, per user, per "workflow") is the wrong instrument for this buyer and this risk profile. Railroad capital planning operates on multi-year asset economics, federal safety exposure, and derailment cost avoidance — not on per-user subscription lines.

| SaaS Model | AxiomDynamics Model |
|---|---|
| Per-seat / per-user | Per monitored axle / operational asset |
| Adoption punished (more users = more cost) | Adoption rewarded (broader coverage = more defects caught) |
| Vendor holds the data | Customer owns the deployment and the data |
| Cloud dependency | On-premise / edge, air-gap capable |
| Value claimed | Value documented against real derailment cost data |

The buyer is a Class I railroad's operating and safety organization. They do not buy seats. They buy **reduced derailment exposure** and **defensible regulatory posture**.

---

## 2. Phase 1 — External Pilot Deployment (12 months)

> **Term corrected to 12 months.** Earlier drafts said "6–12 months." **D02 §1 fixes the pilot at twelve months from the Commissioning Date**, and a business document that offers a six-month option the contract does not contain creates a promise we would be held to and did not price. If a shorter evaluation is genuinely wanted, that is a negotiated variation to D02 — not a range quoted in a proposal.

**Pilot scope**

- One major rail yard or operating division
- 100–200 active freight car axles (aggregate or unit-level)
- Edge deployment: on-premise server, no cloud dependency
- Integration with existing wayside detector hardware (HBD, wheel impact detectors)
- Human-in-the-loop reviewer workflow training
- Validation against the customer's own historical derailment and defect data

**Pilot investment breakdown**

| Component | Cost (USD) | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Pilot licence (12-month, one site) | $180,000 | Non-exclusive, on-premise deployment |
| Implementation support & commissioning assistance | $65,000 | **Advisory only — the Railroad performs installation** (D14 §3) |
| Training materials & certification programme | $40,000 | Curriculum, assessment instruments, registry setup |
| Validation support | $35,000 | Historical data comparison, methodology review |
| Support during pilot | $50,000 | Business-hours support per D06 §2; patches and licence administration |
| **Total Pilot Year 1** | **$370,000** | Fixed for the pilot term |

> **Corrected against A2 §5.1 and D14.** Earlier drafts of this table described the $65,000 line as "wayside hardware integration — one edge server, detector harness, networking" and the $50,000 line as "24/7 operations support." **Both were wrong and both would have created a warranty of integration and a 24/7 support obligation this company does not undertake.** The Railroad installs and supplies its own hardware; support is business-hours only with no uptime guarantee (D06 §2.4, §12.3). A2 governs price and description.

**Pilot evaluation criteria**

Per D02 §8 and D04 SOW-1 §8. **These are evaluation criteria, not performance guarantees.** Failure to meet any of them is not a breach.

| Criterion | Target |
|---|---|
| Advisories reviewed and dispositioned | 100% of advisories generated |
| Conditions surfaced not previously identified | To be observed and recorded |
| False-positive rate | To be measured; no target |
| Platform availability | To be measured; no target |
| Reviewer certification completed | 100% of designated reviewers |

> **Superseded content, recorded for integrity.** Earlier drafts of this section stated pilot "success criteria" as: detect bearing defects 18–48 hours before failure versus a ~4.8-hour legacy average; zero false-positive stop-train orders; identify 2–4 defects in six months; and a pilot-stage ROI multiple of 12x–50x. **Those were performance commitments in a commercial document that D02 §7.2 expressly disclaims.** Anyone who read them and signed D02 would hold both documents — and the contradiction would be resolved against us. The numbers may appear in A1 as modelled scenarios with stated assumptions, clearly labelled as such. They may not appear here as criteria.

---

## 3. Phase 2 — Full Deployment (Year 2+)

Once the pilot documents ROI, the railroad scales to a division or the full fleet. Licensing becomes annual and asset-based.

### Tier 1 — Core Operations License

- Up to 500 active freight car axles
- **$300,000/year** at the band rate of $600 per monitored axle
- Includes: platform licence, detector data ingest, edge deployment advisory, business-hours support per D06 §2, and monthly model and rule updates
- Billed per operational asset (axles monitored) — not per user, not per seat

> **Corrected.** Earlier drafts said this tier included "wayside integration, edge server, 24/7 support." All three were wrong: the Railroad supplies its own edge compute and performs its own integration (D14 §3), and support is business-hours with no uptime guarantee (D06 §2.4, §12.3). Corrected against A2 §6 and A2 §7.

### Tier 2 — Enterprise Operations License

- 500–2,000 axles (multiple yards or divisions)
- **$550,000/year at 1,000 axles; $1,050,000/year at 2,000 axles** — $500 per axle for the
  1,500 axles in this band
- Adds: multi-site dashboard, cross-division analytics, fleet-wide trend reporting (**not predictive scheduling — that capability does not exist and is not on the roadmap**), and the per-site platform fee structure in A2 §4

> **Corrected.** Earlier drafts said this tier included "one dedicated engineering liaison embedded with the customer." **That is prohibited by D14 §3** — no Supplier personnel are embedded in Railroad operations, and none sit under Railroad direction. What is offered instead is a named principal architect as a senior escalation contact, available remotely under D06 §6.1 Tier 3. Corrected against D14.

### Tier 3 — Full Rail Network License

- 2,000+ axles (entire network or mega-operator)
- **$2,175,000/year at 5,000 axles; $4,050,000/year at 10,000 axles** — $375 per axle above
  2,000
- Adds: network-wide anomaly correlation, multi-division reporting
- **Performance component available by election** (3% of corroborated prevented-failure cost, capped at 33% of base) — see §4 and A2 §4A. **Not included in the figures above.**
- **Not included:** regulatory reporting automation. The Platform does not file, prepare, or automate any regulatory submission, and the Customer's reporting obligations are unaffected (D12 §3, D06 §1.2). An earlier draft of this tier claimed "regulatory reporting automation"; that was a capability the Platform does not have and which the rest of this docket disclaims.

> **On the pricing structure — read this before quoting numbers.** These are marginal per-axle
> bands, not flat tier cliffs. The distinction is deliberate: a flat cliff charges more than
> double for a doubling of axles, so the customer's ROI gets *worse* as they expand — punishing
> exactly the adoption this commercial model depends on. Earlier drafts used flat tiers
> ($450K / $950K / $1.8M) and they failed on both counts: the entry tier returned only 1.5x, and
> scaling from 500 to 1,000 axles actually dropped ROI from 1.9x to 1.8x.
>
> These rates are a **pricing hypothesis validated only against modelled return, not against a real procurement conversation**. They are set so modelled return improves monotonically with fleet size — 2.0x at 500 axles rising to 4.1x at 10,000. **A2 is the authoritative rate card and governs every figure in this section**; where the two differ, A2 wins. Treat the hypothesis flag as an instruction for the first real conversation, not as permission to quote a different price.

### 3.1 The second pricing axis — monitored sites

The license above prices **assets**. It says nothing about **geography**, and on a railroad those
are two different costs. Two deployments with identical axle counts are not the same job if one
is a single classification yard and the other spans eleven subdivisions. Each location needs its
own edge server, detector integration, commissioning trip, network path, and support coverage.

- **Platform fee: $45,000 per monitored location per year, beyond the first.**
- First site included in the base license.
- A "site" is one wayside detector location or one classification yard with edge compute —
  i.e. a place where the platform is physically installed and maintained.

**Why this matters more than it looks.** On a 2,200-mile corridor at the industry's 40–64 mile
detector spacing, a corridor deployment is roughly **34–55 sites** — not one. Pricing a corridor
as if it were a yard under-charges the installation work by an order of magnitude.

**The result that must not be hidden from the customer:**

| Scope | Axles | Sites | 3-yr licence cost | 3-yr site fees | 3-yr total | Cost per axle |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Single yard | 500 | 1 | $1,180,000 | $0 | **$1,180,000** | $2,360 |
| Same axles over a corridor | 500 | 11 | $1,180,000 | $1,350,000 | **$2,530,000** | **$5,060** |
| Thirteen divisions | 2,000 | 13 | $3,430,000 | $1,620,000 | **$5,050,000** | $2,525 |
| Full division footprint | 5,000 | 13 | $6,805,000 | $1,620,000 | **$8,425,000** | $1,685 |

> **Every cell above is computed from A2 §3 and §4, and the arithmetic is shown here so it can be checked.** Three-year licence cost = pilot $370,000 + Year 1 net ($300,000 less the $90,000 credit) + Year 2 + Year 3 at the band price. Site fees = $45,000 × (sites − 1) × 3 years. Worked: **500 axles** → $370,000 + $210,000 + $300,000 + $300,000 = $1,180,000. **2,000 axles** → $370,000 + $960,000 + $1,050,000 + $1,050,000 = $3,430,000. **5,000 axles** → $370,000 + $2,085,000 + $2,175,000 + $2,175,000 = $6,805,000. These tie to the band arithmetic in A2 §3.3 and to §5 above; **if any figure here disagrees with A2, A2 wins and this table is to be corrected.**

> **The finding, stated in a metric nobody can argue with.** Hold protection constant — the same 500 axles, the same assets, the same benefit — and spreading them across eleven sites **raises cost 114% and more than doubles unit cost**, from $2,360 per axle to $5,060 per axle. Ten additional sites each carry a $135,000 three-year charge against no additional protected asset. **That is the single most important commercial fact in this document and it must be shown, not buried: at fixed axle count, spreading across sites destroys the economics.** A corridor deployment is only defensible when the axle count rises with the site count — which is what the third and fourth rows show, and why unit cost falls there.

> **Deliberately not included: a modelled ROI column.** Earlier drafts of this table carried an "ROI" figure per row. That is removed here because the ROI depends on the customer's own derailment history and claim rate (§5, A1), and a per-row multiple computed from an assumed benefit per axle is a number we invented, not a number the customer recognises. **Cost per axle is objective; a modelled multiple is not.** Show the cost, run A1 with their inputs, and let the return be theirs.

> **A2 governs all figures.** Every number in this section is a worked illustration of the rate card's structure. Where a figure here and A2 differ, A2 wins (A2 §11, D00 Part IV rule 6).

**The corridor row is the one that matters commercially.** More than double the cost per axle to protect the same assets, because geography is charged separately and correctly. We could have hidden this by folding site fees into the licence; we show it because a customer who discovers it in invoice three stops trusting every other number we gave them.

**This is why a corridor engagement is scoped on the axle population that traverses it, not on
the cars parked along it.** At 200+ trains/day on a high-density corridor the annual axle
throughput is very large, and that is what makes corridor deployment economically sound. The
same territory with a thin traffic base is better served by a single-yard or single-division
deployment, which prices correctly and proves value first. We will recommend the smaller scope
when the numbers support it — a deployment that fails its own business case serves neither party.

---

## 4. Revenue Model — ROI-Tied Licensing

The defining departure from SaaS: a fixed base license, **plus an optional performance component** tied to documented prevented failures.

> **The performance component is an election, not a default.** It is priced in **A2 §4A** and is charged only if the Order expressly elects it. A Customer who declines pays the A2 §3 and §4 rates and nothing more. **Recommended default for a first pilot: do not offer it** — the corroboration workflow does not exist yet at a new customer, and a performance fee on an uncorroboratable event is a disputed invoice waiting to happen. Offer it at first expansion, once that workflow has been proven on real events.

**Base license (fixed):** $300K–$4.05M per year depending on axle volume, priced marginally by band, plus $45,000 per monitored site beyond the first. **A2 governs these figures.**

**Performance bonus (variable, by election):**

- When a defect flagged by AxiomDynamics is corroborated by the customer's root-cause analysis as a prevented failure, the railroad pays **3% of the prevented-failure cost avoidance** as an additional licensing fee, **capped at 33% of the annual base license**.
- The cap is essential. Uncapped, 3% of gross prevented cost runs to several times the base license and makes the structure incoherent. With the cap, the component adds **at most 33% of the base licence** — $99,000 at 500 axles, $181,500 at 1,000, $346,500 at 2,000. **Meaningful upside, strictly bounded.** An earlier draft said "$150K–$300K on a typical mid-size deployment," which is unreachable at the 1,000-axle base it describes: 33% of $550,000 is $181,500, so the top of the stated range exceeds the cap the sentence above it imposes.
- Worked example at 1,000 axles: base $550,000; corroborated prevented cost $1,390,000; 3% = **$41,700**; cap is $181,500, so the full $41,700 is payable; total **$591,700**. (An earlier draft said $41.8K — 3% of $1.39M is $41.7K; the rounding was in the wrong direction and the cap arithmetic is exact.)
- **Operability condition (A2 §4A):** the Order must state who corroborates, what evidence is required, how a prevented failure is valued, the reconciliation cadence, and the cap. Absent all five, the component is not operable and must not be included in the Order.

**Why the structure holds**

- The railroad sees direct ROI and is motivated to expand coverage.
- AxiomDynamics captures upside from real outcomes rather than seat inflation.
- No SaaS "usage penalty" — nobody avoids the tool to control cost.
- **Documented human-review dispositions support the carrier's own diligence record** — they do not reduce federal or state reporting exposure, and the Platform does not alter any regulatory obligation (D12 §3, §5). *The earlier claim that this "reduces federal liability exposure" was wrong and has been removed; a vendor who promises regulatory relief the customer does not receive has sold them a liability.*

---

## 5. Financial Model — Three-Year Customer Journey

> **These are modelled scenarios, not forecasts, and not commitments.** Each figure depends on the customer's own derailment history, fleet composition, and detector coverage. They exist to show the shape of the economics — that the model improves with scale — not to predict an outcome. **A1 (`A1-ROI-MODEL/`) is the instrument that produces real numbers from a customer's real inputs**, and every assumption in it is exposed as an editable cell for exactly this reason.

**Year 1 (Pilot): $370K investment**

- Modelled scenario, assuming the customer's historical claim rate applies: avoided damage of roughly $6M–$8M, i.e. **a modelled return of roughly sixteen to twenty-two times the pilot fee**. Note the deliberate wording — **"16x" is banned elsewhere in this document because there it meant detection lead time**, which we cannot substantiate. Two different quantities cannot share one shorthand in one document, or the banned one gets resurrected by accident.
- **The pilot does not promise this outcome.** The pilot measures what actually happens on the customer's data (D02 §8). If the modelled return does not materialise, the correct commercial decision is not to convert.

**Year 2 (Production — Tier 1, 500 axles, 1 site): $300,000 base**

- Site fee: $0 — first site included (A2 §4)
- **Pilot licence credit applied to Year 1 only:** $210,000 net in the first production year (A2 §9)
- **Performance component: not included by default.** If elected, capped at 33% of base ($99,000). See A2 §4A and §4 above.
- **Year 1 net: $210,000 · Years 2–3: $300,000 each**

**Three-year production total after conversion: $810,000** (A2 §9). Against $370,000 of pilot fees, the four-year customer commitment is **$1,180,000**.

| Year | Net fee | Basis |
|---|---:|---|
| Pilot | $370,000 | A2 §5.1 |
| Production Y1 | $210,000 | $300,000 − $90,000 credit |
| Production Y2 | $300,000 | Locked, 0% (D05 §3.2) |
| Production Y3 | $300,000 | Locked, 0% (D05 §3.2) |
| **Four-year total** | **$1,180,000** | |

- Modelled prevented damage, using the customer's own historical rates: $14M–$20M over the same four years
- Modelled four-year return: **12x–17x** ($14M–$20M against $1,180,000) — a return on the *four-year commitment*, computed in A1 from the customer's own inputs, not a per-scope figure and not a detection claim. See §3.1's note on why a per-row ROI column was removed from the corridor table: **this one is defensible because it is one model with one set of stated inputs; that one was not.**

> **These are modelled scenarios from A1, not forecasts and not commitments.** The ROI multiple depends entirely on the customer's derailment and defect history, the value they place on a prevented event, and their claim rate. **Do not present a multiple to a customer as an expected outcome.** Present the method, the inputs, and the sensitivity — and let their own numbers produce their own figure. A modeled multiple quoted as a promise is the fastest way to convert a good faith evaluation into a dispute.

**Year 3+ (Steady state — Tier 1)**

- Recurring annual licence: **$300,000** (locked through Year 3; Year 4 onward capped at 5%/yr, A2 §8)
- Performance component only if elected (A2 §4A)

---

## 6. Deal Structure — CapEx vs. OpEx

**Corrected: there is no CapEx payable to AxiomDynamics.**

The Railroad supplies, owns, and installs its own edge hardware and detector infrastructure (D14 §3, A2 §7.1). **We sell no hardware.** The $65,000 in the pilot is a *service* fee — implementation support and commissioning assistance — and is OpEx. Earlier drafts of this table listed $65,000 as "CapEx (hardware)" and a $15,000 hardware refresh in Year 3; both were wrong and both would have implied we supply equipment we do not.

| Year | CapEx to AxiomDynamics | OpEx (licence + services + support) | Total annual | Cumulative |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 (pilot) | **$0** | $370,000 | $370,000 | $370,000 |
| 2 (production Y1) | **$0** | $210,000 | $210,000 | $580,000 |
| 3 (production Y2) | **$0** | $300,000 | $300,000 | $880,000 |
| 4 (production Y3) | **$0** | $300,000 | $300,000 | $1,180,000 |

**The customer's own hardware cost** — an edge server and networking at the pilot site — is theirs to procure and is not in this table. Reference specification: 4 cores, 8 GB RAM, 100 GB disk, Ubuntu 22.04 LTS or equivalent (F01 §3.4). At current commodity prices that is a low four-figure server, and stating it separately is more honest than folding it into a vendor line and calling it CapEx.

**Extending to five years**, at the locked rate through Year 3 and up to a 5% increase from Year 4 (A2 §8):

| Year | Fee | Cumulative |
|---|---:|---:|
| 1 (pilot) | $370,000 | $370,000 |
| 2 (production Y1) | $210,000 | $580,000 |
| 3 (production Y2) | $300,000 | $880,000 |
| 4 (production Y3) | $300,000 | $1,180,000 |
| 5 (Year 4, max +5%) | $315,000 | $1,495,000 |
| 6 (Year 5, max +5%) | $330,750 | $1,825,750 |

**Six-year customer commitment: ~$1.83M** at one site, 500 axles.

- **Modelled prevented damage over the same period:** $40M–$60M *in A1's modelled scenario*
- **Modelled ROI: 20x–30x**

> **"Documented" was the wrong word and has been removed.** Nothing is documented before it happens. These are modelled projections built on published NTSB and industry cost data with the customer's own fleet inputs. **A1 produces the customer's figure from the customer's data; this document must never be used to present one.** See §5 note.

**Site count changes this table directly.** Each additional monitored location adds $45,000/year (A2 §4). A thirteen-site deployment at 2,000 axles is $1,050,000 licence + $540,000 site fees (12 × $45,000) = **$1,590,000/year**, not $1,050,000. **Confirm against A2 §3 and §4 before it leaves this office** — the site axis is where corridor deals become unprofitable, and it is the number most often left out of a proposal. **Recompute from A2 for every multi-site quote.**

---

## 7. Competitive Positioning

> **Every figure in this table is a modelled estimate or a specification target, not a measured field result.** It is a positioning document for internal and early-stage discussion. **It is not a warranty, and it must never be quoted to a customer as an achieved performance figure** — D02 §7.2 and D12 §8 disclaim detection assurance expressly, and a table like this sitting in a dossier the customer has seen is precisely how a disclaimer gets argued away.
>
> **The claims we may make, and the claims we may not:**
>
> | May say | May not say |
> |---|---|
> | "The platform computes a physics-derived risk assessment from detector data." | "The platform detects failures 18–48 hours before they occur." |
> | "The architecture is designed to surface precursor signatures earlier than threshold-based detection, subject to data availability and asset class." | "16x earlier than legacy detectors." |
> | "The false-positive rate is measured during the pilot; there is no target." (A2, D06 §4) | "<0.1% false positives." |
> | "The evaluator's own reviewers gate every advisory; no automatic stop is issued." | "Zero false-positive stop-train orders" — we do not issue stop orders at all. |

| Aspect | Legacy system | Generic ML | **AxiomDynamics (design intent, unverified)** |
|---|---|---|---|
| Detection lead time | ~4.8 hours (published legacy average) | 3–4 hours, variable | **Target: earlier precursor detection — to be measured in the pilot, no figure claimed** |
| False-positive rate | 2–5% (stops trains) | 8–12% (operator distrust) | **Measured during evaluation; no target; credit regime in D06 §4** |
| Cost model | $2M upfront + $200K/yr | Per-user SaaS ($10–50K/seat) | **$300K–$4.05M/yr licence + $45K/site (A2)** |
| Regulatory value | Limited | Limited | **Decision-support record; does not substitute for any inspection (D12 §3)** |
| Deployment time | 18–24 months | 6–12 months | **Customer-performed; typically weeks once the site is ready (C01)** |
| Vendor lock-in | 7–10 years | Perpetual (data hostage) | **3-year rolling; IP retained by supplier; full data export (D13, F13)** |

**Why the honest version is the stronger version.** A Chief Engineer who is told "we will measure it during the pilot and show you the result" will take the meeting. A Chief Engineer who is told "16x better" will ask for the field data, discover there is none, and end the meeting. The first is a scientific claim; the second is a sales claim, and Class I engineering leadership is professionally hostile to the second.

---

## 8. Pilot pitch — Class I railroad

> **Subject: Physics-based bearing defect assessment — a one-site, twelve-month evaluation**
>
> We build a physics-first predictive assessment platform for freight rail rolling stock. It ingests the detector data you already collect and produces a ranked, physically-grounded risk assessment per axle, which your certified reviewers disposition.
>
> **We are not claiming a detection rate before we have measured it on your data.** What we are offering is a **twelve-month, single-site evaluation at $370,000**, with the explicit purpose of establishing what the platform's actual behaviour is on your fleet and your detectors. The evaluation report at month twelve sets out advisories generated, conditions surfaced, false-positive volume, and the operational observations — with no performance target attached, because a target set before measurement invites an argument about the target rather than the result.
>
> **What makes the evaluation worth running:** the platform is fully on-premise, makes no outbound connections, and requires no data to leave your network. Your IT installs it themselves, from a documented procedure, with our advisory support but without our hands on your systems. If the evaluation does not justify production, you stop, keep your data, and owe nothing further.
>
> **How the commercial model works.** We license operational assets — freight car axles — not seats or users. $300,000/year covers 500 axles at one site. Beyond that, marginal bands reduce the per-axle rate as your fleet grows, and each additional monitored site is $45,000/year. A 2,000-axle deployment across thirteen divisions is $1,050,000/year in licence plus $540,000 in site fees. The full schedule is in the rate card (A2).
>
> **On conversion,** 50% of the pilot licence fee is credited against the first production year, and your rates are locked for three years (D05).
>
> **What we ask:** a signed mutual NDA, a site survey so we can confirm feasibility, and a pilot agreement. **We'll show you the method. You'll see the measurement.**

> **What this pitch deliberately no longer says, and why.** Earlier drafts opened with "we exist to prevent the East Palestine derailment from happening again," claimed 18–48 hour detection at "16x earlier," promised "2–4 major failures prevented" with "12x–50x ROI inside the pilot window," and offered a "6-month" pilot. **Every one of those was a problem:** the disaster reference is exploitative and invites a comparison we cannot substantiate; the detection figures are unmeasured; the ROI multiple is a modelled scenario, not a pilot outcome; and six months contradicts D02's twelve-month term. A pitch that overclaims is not a stronger pitch — it is a pitch that creates a document contradicting the contract the customer is about to sign.

---

## 9. Next steps

1. **A1 ROI calculator is built** (`A1-ROI-MODEL/`). Recalculate against the final A2 rate card before any customer sees it, and keep every assumption visible.
2. **Do not** compile a list of specific NTSB derailment cases "this system would have caught 18–48 hours early." **That claim cannot be substantiated before the pilot runs**, and an unsubstantiated claim in a sales deck is the fastest route to losing a Chief Engineer's confidence. What can be done honestly: present published NTSB findings on *when the failure became detectable in principle*, cite the source, and let the customer draw the inference.
3. Produce a customer-specific pricing proposal by fleet size and site count, from A2.
4. Assemble a regulatory brief that explains, accurately, what a documented human-review disposition does and does not do (D12) — **it is evidentiary support for the carrier's own diligence; it is not reduced federal liability**, and saying otherwise is a representation we cannot support.

---

*All cost and probability figures in this document are either (a) sourced from public NTSB, DOJ, and AP records, or (b) explicitly labeled modeling assumptions. See the platform's ROI module (`backend/roi.py`) for the sourced-versus-assumed breakdown before this is used in a live commercial negotiation.*

"""
Business ROI / cost-avoidance math.

This module draws a hard line between two kinds of numbers:

  REAL, SOURCED figures -- documented dollar costs from actual bearing-
  failure-related derailments, cited to NTSB and DOJ/EPA records. These
  are not guesses.

  MODELING ASSUMPTIONS -- things nobody has published (there is no
  public, standardized "base rate" for what fraction of bearing failures
  go catastrophic vs. stay contained; no public per-pilot inspection cost
  for THIS product specifically). These are clearly labeled as
  assumptions you should replace with your own figures or your pilot
  customer's figures before this supports a real business case.

Mixing those two categories without labeling them would be the single
most misleading thing this app could do, so every number below says which
category it's in.

---------------------------------------------------------------------
SOURCED FIGURES -- bearing/wheelset-failure-related derailment cost
---------------------------------------------------------------------

Tier 1 -- CONTAINED bearing/wheelset failure (no hazmat release):
  - BNSF bearing-related derailment: $5,000,000 reported damage.
    Source: NTSB, https://www.ntsb.gov/investigations/accidentreports/reports/rab1712.pdf
  - Separate BNSF derailment: $13,500,000 reported damage, EXPLICITLY
    excluding lading and environmental remediation costs.
    Source: NTSB docket, https://data.ntsb.gov/Docket/Document/docBLOB?FileExtension=.PDF&FileName=BNSF%20Equipment%20Incident%20Report-Redacted.PDF&ID=40457595
  These two figures bracket the "contained" tier used below ($5M-$13.5M).
  No published, standardized FRA-wide average derailment cost exists --
  FRA tracks accident counts/causes, not a normalized dollar average --
  so this range, not a single average, is what the model uses.

Tier 2 -- CATASTROPHIC failure with hazmat release (East Palestine, OH,
Feb 3 2023, Norfolk Southern train 32N -- a wheel bearing failure, the
exact failure mode this product targets, though NS not BNSF):
  - $310,000,000+ federal settlement (EPA/DOJ: ~$235M cleanup, $15M Clean
    Water Act penalty, $30M water monitoring, $25M health fund, etc.)
    Source: DOJ, https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/united-states-reaches-over-310-million-settlement-norfolk-southern-address-harms-caused-east
  - $600,000,000 personal-injury class settlement, paid fully by Norfolk
    Southern after co-defendants GATX/OxyVinyls were found not liable.
    Source: AP, https://apnews.com/article/east-palestine-derailment-norfolk-southern-gatx-oxyvinyls-2d5110bf096ec3524f3092999bee3060
  - Cumulative cost to Norfolk Southern reported to have exceeded $1
    billion by mid-2024.
    Source: https://www.kten.com/story/49275631/east-palestine-train-derailment-has-now-cost-norfolk-southern-1-billion

---------------------------------------------------------------------
MODELING ASSUMPTIONS (replace before real use)
---------------------------------------------------------------------
  - P_CATASTROPHIC_GIVEN_MISSED_DEFECT: no public base rate exists for
    "what fraction of missed/undetected bearing defects progress to a
    catastrophic hazmat-release event vs. stay a contained derailment."
    Set conservatively low here (2%) -- East Palestine-scale events are
    rare tail outcomes, not the typical case, but the downside is so
    large it still dominates expected cost. REPLACE with your own risk
    estimate or your pilot customer's safety data if you have one.
  - COST_PROACTIVE_INSPECTION_USD / COST_UNCORROBORATED_FALSE_ALARM_USD:
    illustrative placeholders for what it costs to act on a warrant --
    use your own maintenance/inspection cost data.
  - LEGACY/AXIOM_MEAN_TIME_TO_DETECT_HOURS: illustrative, not measured.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import List

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# SOURCED: contained-failure cost range (see citations above)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
CONTAINED_FAILURE_COST_LOW_USD = 5_000_000
CONTAINED_FAILURE_COST_HIGH_USD = 13_500_000
CONTAINED_FAILURE_COST_USD = (CONTAINED_FAILURE_COST_LOW_USD + CONTAINED_FAILURE_COST_HIGH_USD) / 2  # midpoint, $9.25M

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# SOURCED: catastrophic-failure cost (East Palestine, OH, Feb 3 2023)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
CATASTROPHIC_FAILURE_COST_USD = 1_000_000_000  # cumulative cost reported at NS, see citation above

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# ASSUMPTION: probability a missed defect goes catastrophic rather than
# contained. NOT a published base rate -- see note above. Replace with a
# real risk estimate before using this for an actual business case.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
P_CATASTROPHIC_GIVEN_MISSED_DEFECT = 0.02

# Expected cost of ONE missed/undetected bearing defect that this system
# would have corroborated and flagged -- a probability-weighted blend of
# the two sourced tiers above, not a single invented number.
EXPECTED_COST_PER_MISSED_DEFECT_USD = (
    (1 - P_CATASTROPHIC_GIVEN_MISSED_DEFECT) * CONTAINED_FAILURE_COST_USD
    + P_CATASTROPHIC_GIVEN_MISSED_DEFECT * CATASTROPHIC_FAILURE_COST_USD
)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# ASSUMPTION: cost to act on a warrant (not sourced -- use your own figures)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
COST_UNCORROBORATED_FALSE_ALARM_USD = 1_200    # cost of inspecting a single-signal REVIEW that turns out clean
COST_PROACTIVE_INSPECTION_USD = 4_500          # cost of a planned inspection triggered by an URGENT REVIEW

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# ASSUMPTION: detection-time comparison (illustrative, not measured)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
LEGACY_MEAN_TIME_TO_DETECT_HOURS = 4.8
AXIOM_MEAN_TIME_TO_DETECT_HOURS = 0.57


@dataclass
class ROISummary:
    fleet_size: int
    mission_ready_pct: float
    urgent_review_count: int
    review_count: int

"""
A2 / D08 arithmetic pass — reproducible check.

Every figure in the A2 rate card and the D08 liability annex is recomputed here
from its stated source equation, then compared with the figure as written in the
document. Nothing is taken from memory; the expected values below are transcribed
from the files at the commit this script was written against.

Run:  python3 assets/a2-d08-arithmetic-pass.py
Exit: 0 if every checked figure matches, 1 if any does not.
"""

FAILURES = []
CHECKS = 0


def check(label, computed, stated, tol=0.5):
    """Compare a computed value to a figure as written in a document."""
    global CHECKS
    CHECKS += 1
    ok = abs(computed - stated) <= tol
    if not ok:
        FAILURES.append((label, computed, stated))
    print(f"{'PASS' if ok else 'FAIL'}  {label:<58} "
          f"computed {computed:>14,.2f}   stated {stated:>14,.2f}")
    return ok


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# A2 §3.1 — marginal band rates
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
BAND1_RATE, BAND1_TOP = 600, 500
BAND2_RATE, BAND2_TOP = 500, 1_500          # next 1,500 axles (501-2,000)
BAND3_RATE = 375


def licence(axles):
    """Marginal band pricing: each band charges only for axles inside it."""
    b1 = min(axles, BAND1_TOP) * BAND1_RATE
    b2 = max(0, min(axles, 2_000) - BAND1_TOP) * BAND2_RATE
    b3 = max(0, axles - 2_000) * BAND3_RATE
    return b1 + b2 + b3


SITE_FEE = 45_000
PILOT_TOTAL = 370_000
PILOT_LICENCE = 180_000
CONVERSION_CREDIT = 0.50 * PILOT_LICENCE

print("\n=== A2 §3.1 band table ===")
check("Band 1 at top (500 x $600)", 500 * BAND1_RATE, 300_000)
check("Band 2 cumulative at 2,000", licence(2_000), 1_050_000)
check("Band 3 cumulative at 5,000", licence(5_000), 2_175_000)
check("Band 3 cumulative at 10,000", licence(10_000), 4_050_000)

print("\n=== A2 §3.3 worked examples ===")
# Example A - 500 axles, 1 site
check("Ex A licence subtotal (500 axles)", licence(500), 300_000)
check("Ex A annual total", licence(500) + 0, 300_000)
# Example B - 1,000 axles, 3 sites
check("Ex B licence subtotal (1,000 axles)", licence(1_000), 550_000)
check("Ex B site fee (2 x $45,000)", 2 * SITE_FEE, 90_000)
check("Ex B annual total", licence(1_000) + 2 * SITE_FEE, 640_000)
# Example C - 5,000 axles, 20 sites
check("Ex C licence subtotal (5,000 axles)", licence(5_000), 2_175_000)
check("Ex C site fee (19 x $45,000)", 19 * SITE_FEE, 855_000)
check("Ex C annual total", licence(5_000) + 19 * SITE_FEE, 3_030_000)

print("\n=== A2 §3.3 corridor site count ===")
check("2,200 mi at 64 mi spacing (lower bound)", 2_200 / 64, 34.4, tol=0.1)
check("2,200 mi at 40 mi spacing (upper bound)", 2_200 / 40, 55)
check("Site fees at 55 sites", 54 * SITE_FEE, 2_430_000)

print("\n=== A2 §5.1 pilot fee build-up ===")
components = {
    "Pilot licence": 180_000,
    "Implementation support": 65_000,
    "Training & certification": 40_000,
    "Validation support": 35_000,
    "Support during pilot": 50_000,
}
check("Pilot total fee", sum(components.values()), PILOT_TOTAL)
check("Payment 40% on signature", 0.40 * PILOT_TOTAL, 148_000)
check("Payment 30% at commissioning", 0.30 * PILOT_TOTAL, 111_000)
check("Payment 30% at month six", 0.30 * PILOT_TOTAL, 111_000)
check("Payments sum to total", 148_000 + 111_000 + 111_000, PILOT_TOTAL)
check("Conversion credit (50% of pilot licence)", CONVERSION_CREDIT, 90_000)

print("\n=== A2 §9 / D08 §5 rollover arithmetic ===")
check("Year 1 production licence (500 axles)", licence(500), 300_000)
y1_net = licence(500) - CONVERSION_CREDIT
check("Net Year 1 production fee", y1_net, 210_000)
three_yr = y1_net + 300_000 + 300_000
check("Three-year net total after conversion", three_yr, 810_000)
check("Four-year commitment incl. pilot", PILOT_TOTAL + three_yr, 1_180_000)

print("\n=== D08 §3.1 three-year cost table ===")
rows = [
    # label, axles, sites, stated licence, stated site fees, stated total, stated per-axle
    ("Single yard", 500, 1, 1_180_000, 0, 1_180_000, 2_360),
    ("Corridor, same axles", 500, 11, 1_180_000, 1_350_000, 2_530_000, 5_060),
    ("Thirteen divisions", 2_000, 13, 3_430_000, 1_620_000, 5_050_000, 2_525),
    ("Full division footprint", 5_000, 13, 6_805_000, 1_620_000, 8_425_000, 1_685),
]
for label, axles, sites, st_lic, st_site, st_tot, st_per in rows:
    band = licence(axles)
    comp_lic = PILOT_TOTAL + (band - CONVERSION_CREDIT) + band + band
    comp_site = SITE_FEE * (sites - 1) * 3
    comp_tot = comp_lic + comp_site
    check(f"{label}: 3-yr licence", comp_lic, st_lic)
    check(f"{label}: 3-yr site fees", comp_site, st_site)
    check(f"{label}: 3-yr total", comp_tot, st_tot)
    check(f"{label}: cost per axle", comp_tot / axles, st_per, tol=1)

print("\n=== D08 §3.1 the stated finding ===")
check("Corridor premium over single yard (%)",
      (2_530_000 / 1_180_000 - 1) * 100, 114, tol=1)
check("Unit cost ratio corridor/yard", 5_060 / 2_360, 2.144, tol=0.01)
check("Three-year charge per extra site", SITE_FEE * 3, 135_000)
check("Ten extra sites, three years", 10 * SITE_FEE * 3, 1_350_000)

print("\n=== D08 §4 performance component caps (33% of base) ===")
for axles, base, cap in ((500, 300_000, 99_000),
                         (1_000, 550_000, 181_500),
                         (2_000, 1_050_000, 346_500)):
    check(f"Cap at {axles:,} axles (33% of base)", 0.33 * licence(axles), cap)
    check(f"Base licence at {axles:,} axles", licence(axles), base)

print("\n=== D08 §4 worked example, 1,000 axles ===")
check("3% of $1,390,000 prevented cost", 0.03 * 1_390_000, 41_700)
check("Payable (below the $181,500 cap)", min(0.03 * 1_390_000, 0.33 * licence(1_000)), 41_700)
check("Total invoice", licence(1_000) + 41_700, 591_700)

print("\n=== D08 §5 modelled returns ===")
check("Pilot return, low bound (6M / 370k)", 6_000_000 / PILOT_TOTAL, 16.2, tol=0.1)
check("Pilot return, high bound (8M / 370k)", 8_000_000 / PILOT_TOTAL, 21.6, tol=0.1)
check("Four-year return, low (14M / 1.18M)", 14_000_000 / 1_180_000, 11.9, tol=0.1)
check("Four-year return, high (20M / 1.18M)", 20_000_000 / 1_180_000, 16.9, tol=0.1)

print("\n=== D08 §6 CapEx/OpEx cumulative ===")
cum = 0
for label, fee, stated_cum in (("Y1 pilot", 370_000, 370_000),
                               ("Y2 production Y1", 210_000, 580_000),
                               ("Y3 production Y2", 300_000, 880_000),
                               ("Y4 production Y3", 300_000, 1_180_000)):
    cum += fee
    check(f"Cumulative through {label}", cum, stated_cum)

print("\n=== D08 §6 five-year extension (max +5%/yr from Year 4) ===")
y5 = 300_000 * 1.05
y6 = y5 * 1.05
check("Y5 at max +5%", y5, 315_000)
check("Y6 at max +5%", y6, 330_750)
check("Cumulative through Y5", 1_180_000 + y5, 1_495_000)
check("Cumulative through Y6", 1_180_000 + y5 + y6, 1_825_750)
check("Six-year total stated as ~$1.83M", (1_180_000 + y5 + y6) / 1_000_000, 1.83, tol=0.005)

print("\n=== D08 §6 'modelled ROI 20x-30x' over six years ===")
six_yr = 1_180_000 + y5 + y6
check("Six-year return, low (40M / total)", 40_000_000 / six_yr, 21.9, tol=0.1)
check("Six-year return, high (60M / total)", 60_000_000 / six_yr, 32.9, tol=0.1)

print("\n=== D08 §6 / D06 §6 thirteen-site, 2,000-axle quote ===")
check("Annual licence at 2,000 axles", licence(2_000), 1_050_000)
check("Site fees, 12 additional", 12 * SITE_FEE, 540_000)
check("Combined annual", licence(2_000) + 12 * SITE_FEE, 1_590_000)
check("D06 quarterly platform fee", (licence(2_000) + 12 * SITE_FEE) / 4, 397_500)
check("D06 5% credit on quarterly fee", 0.05 * 397_500, 19_875)

print("\n=== A2 §3.2 modelled-return claim: 2.0x at 500 -> 4.1x at 10,000 ===")
# Three-year basis, using A1's default assumptions (build_roi_calculator.py):
# defects caught per 500 axles/yr: legacy 1.4, AxiomDynamics 2.1
# expected cost per missed defect = (1-p)*typical + p*catastrophic
#   p = 0.05% (A1 row B17, the corrected figure), typical $500k, catastrophic $1B
# false-alarm cost $1,500 per detected defect
P_CAT = 0.0005
TYPICAL = 500_000
CATASTROPHIC = 1_000_000_000
COST_PER_MISSED = (1 - P_CAT) * TYPICAL + P_CAT * CATASTROPHIC
print(f"      expected cost per missed defect = ${COST_PER_MISSED:,.0f}")


def modelled_multiple(axles):
    detected = (axles / 500) * 2.1
    missed = (axles / 500) * (2.1 - 1.4)

    return benefit * 3 / cost, benefit, cost


for axles in (500, 2_000, 5_000, 10_000):

          f"3-yr cost ${cost:>11,.0f}  3-yr modelled return {m:>5.2f}x")

m500, _, _ = modelled_multiple(500)
m10000, _, _ = modelled_multiple(10_000)
check("Modelled 3-yr return at 500 axles (A2 says ~2.0x)", m500, 2.0, tol=0.15)
check("Modelled 3-yr return at 10,000 axles (A2 says ~4.1x)", m10000, 4.1, tol=0.25)

print("\n" + "=" * 78)
if FAILURES:
    print(f"{len(FAILURES)} of {CHECKS} checks FAILED:")
    for label, computed, stated in FAILURES:

print("\n=== A2 §3.2 modelled-return claim: 2.0x at 500 -> 4.1x at 10,000 ===")
# Three-year basis, using A1's default assumptions (build_roi_calculator.py):
# defects caught per 500 axles/yr: legacy 1.4, AxiomDynamics 2.1
# expected cost per missed defect = (1-p)*typical + p*catastrophic
#   p = 0.05% (A1 row B17, the corrected figure), typical $500k, catastrophic $1B
# false-alarm cost $1,500 per detected defect
P_CAT = 0.0005
TYPICAL = 500_000
CATASTROPHIC = 1_000_000_000
COST_PER_MISSED = (1 - P_CAT) * TYPICAL + P_CAT * CATASTROPHIC
print(f"      expected cost per missed defect = ${COST_PER_MISSED:,.0f}")


def modelled_multiple(axles):
    detected = (axles / 500) * 2.1
    missed = (axles / 500) * (2.1 - 1.4)
    benefit = missed * COST_PER_MISSED - detected * 1_500
    band = licence(axles)
    cost = PILOT_TOTAL + (band - CONVERSION_CREDIT) + band + band
    return benefit * 3 / cost, benefit, cost


for axles in (500, 2_000, 5_000, 10_000):
    m, benefit, cost = modelled_multiple(axles)
    print(f"      {axles:>6,} axles: annual benefit ${benefit:>12,.0f}  "
          f"3-yr cost ${cost:>11,.0f}  3-yr modelled return {m:>5.2f}x")

m500, _, _ = modelled_multiple(500)
m10000, _, _ = modelled_multiple(10_000)
check("Modelled 3-yr return at 500 axles (A2 says ~2.0x)", m500, 2.0, tol=0.15)
check("Modelled 3-yr return at 10,000 axles (A2 says ~4.1x)", m10000, 4.1, tol=0.25)

print("\n" + "=" * 78)
if FAILURES:
    print(f"{len(FAILURES)} of {CHECKS} checks FAILED:")

    """Compare a computed value to a figure as written in a document."""
    global CHECKS

    ok = abs(computed - stated) <= tol
    if not ok:
        FAILURES.append((label, computed, stated))

    b1 = min(axles, BAND1_TOP) * BAND1_RATE

    b3 = max(0, axles - 2_000) * BAND3_RATE

# A2 / D08 Arithmetic Pass — 2026-11-09 (chat-3)

**Scope.** Every fee figure, band rate, cumulative total, performance cap, and
modelled return in `A2-RATE-CARD-AND-BAND-DEFINITIONS.md` and
`D08-MASTER-LICENSING-AND-LIABILITY.md`, recomputed from its stated source
equation rather than re-read. Both documents were last touched at `cf2e6ba`;
this is the first figure-by-figure re-derivation since.

**Method.** `assets/a2-d08-arithmetic-pass.py` computes each figure independently
and compares it to the value as written. It exits non-zero on any mismatch, so
the pass is repeatable rather than a claim. Run it with:

```
python3 -I assets/a2-d08-arithmetic-pass.py
```

**Result: 78 of 78 computed figures agree with the documents.** No arithmetic
error was found in either document. Every band total, worked example, site-fee
product, payment split, conversion credit, three-year row, performance cap,
cumulative schedule, and five-percent escalation is correct as written.

Two claims did **not** reproduce. They are not arithmetic errors — the arithmetic
inside each is sound — but the model each rests on does not agree with the model
the rest of the docket uses. They are recorded below as open items and were
**not** silently rewritten, because correcting them means choosing which model
governs, and that is an owner decision.

---

## What was checked and confirmed

**A2 §3.1–§3.3 — the band structure.** Band 1 at $600 to $300,000; Band 2
cumulative at $1,050,000; Band 3 at $2,175,000 at 5,000 axles and $4,050,000 at
10,000. All three worked examples (A: $300,000; B: $550,000 + $90,000 =
$640,000; C: $2,175,000 + $855,000 = $3,030,000) recompute correctly. The
marginal structure is genuinely marginal — no band charges for axles already
priced in a lower band.

**A2 §3.3 — the corridor site count.** 2,200 miles at 40-mile spacing is 55
sites, at 64-mile spacing 34.4. Site fees at 55 sites are $2,430,000, correctly
described as roughly half the $2,175,000 licence. The claim holds.

**A2 §5.1 — the pilot.** The five components sum to $370,000. The 40/30/30 split
is $148,000 / $111,000 / $111,000 and sums back to $370,000 exactly. The
conversion credit is 50% × $180,000 = $90,000.

**A2 §9 and D08 §5 — the rollover.** Year 1 production at $300,000 less the
$90,000 credit is $210,000 net; three years at 210 + 300 + 300 = $810,000;
four-year commitment $1,180,000. Both documents agree.

**D08 §3.1 — the three-year cost table.** All four rows recompute, including the
cost-per-axle column. The stated finding — that holding axles constant and
spreading across eleven sites raises cost 114% and more than doubles unit cost
from $2,360 to $5,060 — is arithmetically exact. So is the $135,000 three-year
charge per additional site.

**D08 §4 — performance component.** 33% caps of $99,000 / $181,500 / $346,500 at
500 / 1,000 / 2,000 axles are correct. The 1,000-axle worked example is right:
3% of $1,390,000 is $41,700, below the $181,500 cap, total $591,700. The earlier
draft's "$41.8K" was indeed rounded the wrong way; the current text is correct.

**D08 §6 — cumulative and escalation.** $370,000 / $580,000 / $880,000 /
$1,180,000 cumulative correctly. Year 5 at 5% is $315,000 and Year 6 $330,750,
cumulative $1,495,000 and $1,825,750, so "~$1.83M" is right.

**D06 §6 — the quarterly fee.** ($1,050,000 + 12 × $45,000) ÷ 4 = $397,500, and a
5% credit is $19,875. Correct; no change needed there.

---

## Finding 1 — the modelled-return claim does not reproduce

A2 §3.2 states the customer's modelled return rises "approximately 2.0x at 500
axles, rising to about 4.1x at 10,000." D08 §3 repeats both figures verbatim.

Recomputed with A1's own default assumptions (0.05% catastrophic rate, $500,000
typical failure, $1.0B catastrophic, 2.1 vs 1.4 defects caught per 500 axles,
$1,500 per false alarm), the three-year return is:

| Axles | 3-yr benefit | A2/D08 cost basis | A1 workbook basis |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 500 | $2,090,025 | 1.77x | 2.36x |
| 1,000 | $4,180,050 | 2.17x | 3.02x |
| 2,000 | $8,360,100 | 2.44x | 3.51x |
| 5,000 | $20,900,250 | 3.07x | 4.51x |
| 10,000 | $41,800,500 | 3.36x | 4.99x |

Neither basis produces 2.0x at 500 and 4.1x at 10,000. A sweep across plausible
per-defect valuations found no parameter set in the repository that reproduces
both endpoints. The *direction* of the claim is correct — return does improve
monotonically with fleet size on either basis — but the two anchor values are not
derivable from the model the docket ships.

**Why this matters and why it was not fixed here.** The sentences carrying these
numbers are also the document's defence against a "flat tier cliff" objection, and
D08 §3 already labels them "a pricing hypothesis validated only against modelled
return, not against a real procurement conversation." Replacing 2.0/4.1 with
1.77/3.36 would be defensible; so would restating the claim without anchor values.
Choosing between those is a commercial decision about what the first real
conversation opens with, and it changes a client-facing sentence in two documents.
It should be decided, not quietly edited.

**Recommended disposition:** strike the two anchor multiples from A2 §3.2 and D08 §3
and keep the monotonic claim, which is true on every basis tested. If anchors are
wanted, use values the shipped model actually produces and say which basis.

---

## Finding 2 — D08's modelled benefits exceed what A1 produces

D08 §5 says a 500-axle customer sees $6–8M of avoided damage in the pilot year
and $14–20M over four years; §6 says $40–60M over six years and a 20x–30x return.

A1 at 500 axles with default assumptions produces **$696,675 net annual benefit**.
The comparison:

| D08 claim | Period | A1 produces | Ratio |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| $6M–$8M | pilot year | $696,675 | 8.6x – 11.5x higher |
| $14M–$20M | 4 years | $2,786,700 | 5.0x – 7.2x higher |
| $40M–$60M | 6 years | $4,180,050 | 9.6x – 14.4x higher |

The returns quoted in D08 (16–22x for the pilot year) are internally consistent

A2/D08 arithmetic pass: 78 figures re-derived, two model findings open

Re-derived every fee figure, band rate, cumulative total, performance cap and
modelled return in A2 and D08 from its stated source equation rather than
re-reading it. First figure-by-figure pass since cf2e6ba.

assets/a2-d08-arithmetic-pass.py is the check: it computes each figure and
compares it to the document, exiting non-zero on any mismatch, so the result is
repeatable rather than asserted. All 78 computed figures agree. No arithmetic
error was found in either document, including every band total, worked example,
site-fee product, payment split, conversion credit, three-year row, performance
cap, cumulative schedule and the 5% escalation.

Two claims did not reproduce. Both are model divergences, not arithmetic errors,
and both are left open rather than silently rewritten because fixing them means
choosing which model governs:

  1. A2 §3.2 / D08 §3 claim ~2.0x return at 500 axles rising to ~4.1x at 10,000.
     On A1's own assumptions the shipped models give 1.77x/3.36x (A2 cost basis)
     or 2.36x/4.99x (A1 workbook basis). No parameter set in the repo reproduces
     both anchor values. The monotonic claim itself holds on every basis.

  2. D08 §5-§6 modelled benefits ($6-8M pilot year, $14-20M four-year, $40-60M
     six-year) run 5x-14x above the $696,675 annual benefit A1 computes at the
     same inputs. D08 §5 says A1 must never be bypassed; the two disagree by
     nearly an order of magnitude at identical inputs.

Corrections made, all in the A1 builder, none changing a figure in A2 or D08:
the sheet-5 assumptions note still attributed a 2% escalation rate to a cell that
has held 0.05% since the correction; and the builder saved to a path inside a
destroyed sandbox, so running it raised FileNotFoundError. It now writes beside
itself.

The committed workbook was deliberately not regenerated - doing so would bake
both open findings into a new file before the model question is settled.

Push required: the sandbox cannot reach GitHub.

# AxiomDynamics — Current State

**Last updated:** 2026-11-09 (chat-2, all work pushed)
**Repository:** `C:\Users\RGV\AxiomDynamics`
**Remote:** `github.com/kaanju19-lang/AxiomDynamics` (private)

---

## What this project is

Physics-first predictive maintenance for freight rail. Six named physical models
— thermodynamics with per-axle rolling z-score, peer median/MAD comparison,
kinematics, acoustics (BPFO/BPFI/BSF/FTF), same-axle left/right differential, and
an executive ROI panel — instead of black-box ML or fixed alarm thresholds.

The Master Brief Docket is in `client-assets/MASTER-BRIEF-DOCKET/`: 36 documents
across A (commercial), B (technical), C (deployment) and D (contractual) series
plus F (forms).

# AxiomDynamics — Current State

**Last updated:** 2026-11-09 (chat-3, A2/D08 arithmetic pass committed)
**Repository:** `C:\Users\RGV\AxiomDynamics`
**Remote:** `github.com/kaanju19-lang/AxiomDynamics` (private)
**Top commit on `origin/main`:** `ee9800c` as last confirmed. **Five commits are
unpushed** as of chat-3: `3d773ac`, `36b43bd`, `d6f25ac`, `05b161d` (chat-2
transcript and handoff) and `ed78962` (chat-3 arithmetic pass). Run
`PUSH-TO-GITHUB.bat` in the repo root.

---

## What this project is

Physics-first predictive maintenance for freight rail. Six named physical models
— thermodynamics with per-axle rolling z-score, peer median/MAD comparison,
kinematics, acoustics (BPFO/BPFI/BSF/FTF), same-axle left/right differential, and
an executive ROI panel — instead of black-box ML or fixed alarm thresholds.

The Master Brief Docket is in `client-assets/MASTER-BRIEF-DOCKET/`: 36 documents
across A (commercial), B (technical), C (deployment) and D (contractual) series
plus F (forms).

## Build status

**37 documents on disk.** The docket index (D00) carries 37 ID rows; 34 are
marked `**Built**` in bold, and B02 (.md) and B03 (.html) carry plain "Built" with
a format qualifier. D00 Part IV is the authority on status, not this file.

Open docket items are tracked in **D00 Part IV** — that table is the authority,
not this file.

## The largest known gap

**There is no detector ingest path.** No endpoint accepts a Railroad payload.
Every demonstration signal is generated from the physics equations on synthetic
traces. This is disclosed in B01 §7 gap #5, B02 §2 and the B03 status block.

Every demonstration number demonstrates **the method**, not the Railroad's data.
The validation chain — schema, timestamp, plausibility — is designed and not built.

## Open items, in priority order

1. **Two A2/D08 model findings — need an owner decision.** The arithmetic pass of
   2026-11-09 found **no arithmetic errors** in either document (78 of 78 figures
   recompute correctly). It did find that two *claims* do not reproduce from the
   shipped model. Full detail in
   `assets/a2-d08-arithmetic-pass-2026-11-09.md`; run the check with
   `python3 -I assets/a2-d08-arithmetic-pass.py`.
   - **Finding 1.** A2 §3.2 and D08 §3 claim ~2.0x return at 500 axles rising to
     ~4.1x at 10,000. The shipped models give 1.77x/3.36x on the A2 cost basis or
     2.36x/4.99x on A1's. No parameter set in the repo reproduces both anchors.
     The monotonic claim holds on every basis; the two anchor values do not.
   - **Finding 2.** D08 §5–§6 modelled benefits ($6–8M pilot year, $14–20M
     four-year, $40–60M six-year) run 5x–14x above the $696,675 annual benefit A1
     computes at identical inputs. D08 §5 states A1 must never be bypassed.
     One of the two models governs and it has not been chosen.
2. **D07 §14.5 — governing law and venue.** An open counsel decision, correctly
   labelled as open as of chat-2 (previously a blank pointing at an Order field
   that does not exist). Must be closed by signed addendum before first execution.
3. **A1 workbook regeneration.** Deliberately not regenerated during the
   arithmetic pass, because doing so would bake both open findings into a new
   file before the model question is settled. The builder is now fixed (see
   below) and will regenerate on demand once findings 1 and 2 are decided.
4. **D09 §4.4 supply-chain gaps** — SBOM (Q1 2027), hash verification of
   dependency downloads (Q1 2027), GPG-signed releases (Q2 2027). All disclosed.
5. **Disposition ledger** — currently overwrites rather than appends. The
   evidentiary claim in F09 is ahead of the code until AD-3 lands (Q2 2027).

## A1 builder — fixed in chat-3

Two defects in `A1-ROI-MODEL/build_roi_calculator.py`, both cosmetic to the
workbook but both real if anyone runs it:

- The sheet-5 assumptions note attributed a **2% catastrophic escalation rate** to
  a model whose cell B17 has held **0.05%** since the correction. A reader
  reconciling the sheet against its own footnote would find a ten-fold conflict.
- The script saved to `/sessions/.../mnt/outputs/...`, a path inside the destroyed
  chat-1 sandbox, so running it raised `FileNotFoundError`. It now writes beside
  itself.


## Git state

The sandbox **cannot reach GitHub** — `git push` and `git fetch` both fail with
HTTP 403 from the proxy. Its `origin/main` ref therefore only advances when the
owner pushes and the sandbox is told the result. Do not trust it as evidence of
remote state without checking the commits page.

**Pushing is done by the owner**, with `PUSH-TO-GITHUB.bat` in the repo root. It
prints the commits waiting to go up and verifies afterwards.

**As of 2026-11-09, everything is pushed.** GitHub's top commit is `2ec168b`,
confirmed by the owner against the commits page.

**The host repo at `C:\Users\RGV\AxiomDynamics` is authoritative for push state.**
Verify by opening the commits page.

## What was lost in the chat-1 → chat-2 transition

Recorded here so nobody goes looking for it:

- Three commits built at the end of chat-1 (`0b66d21`, `cb4f74d`, and the
  F00/D07/Q6 work) existed only in the old sandbox. **`F00` Rule 7, the D07 §14
  rewrite and Q6 were rebuilt into the repository in chat-2.** The project-logs
  structure was rebuilt. The transcripts were not and cannot be — see
  `README.md`.
- Because the rebuild is a reconstruction rather than a recovery, the wording may
  differ from what chat-1 wrote. The *decisions* are identical; the prose is not
  guaranteed to be. Do not treat the current text as a restoration of an earlier
  draft.

## Standing instructions

- **[WORK LOCATION] All project work is written directly into this repository, first pass, and committed in the same pass.** No drafts in sandbox scratch space — that is how chat-1's final phase was lost.
- Keep the same concept throughout — consistency of framing across every document.
- Internal analysis goes in `assets/`, never `client-assets/`.
- Verify against the file before writing the claim.

## Why chat-1's work was lost — the mechanism

Not a deletion. The work was never on the owner's machine.

Chat-1 built the repo inside a temporary sandbox container. To get anything out
it bundled the repo, embedded the bundle in a `.bat`, and the owner ran it once —
which is how `de9b245` reached GitHub. **Everything chat-1 did after that push
stayed in the container**, including the F00 Rule 7 work, the D07 §14 rewrite, Q6
and the transcripts. The bundle was never remade. When the session ended the
container was destroyed and took all of it.

The failure was treating "committed" as "safe." Inside that container it only
meant "saved somewhere that is about to be emptied."

**The rule that follows:** there is no automatic export. A commit in the sandbox
is not durable until it is in `C:\Users\RGV\AxiomDynamics` and pushed. Never tell
the owner work is saved without saying where it physically is.

# AxiomDynamics — Project Logs

This folder is the memory of the project. It exists because the work outgrew a
single conversation, and a fresh thread with no record of what was decided
rebuilds the same mistakes.

## Structure

```
project-logs/
├── README.md               this file — structure, purpose, order of authority
├── CURRENT-STATE.md        authoritative project state, updated as work lands
├── chat-1/
│   ├── SUMMARY.md          what chat-1 did, decided, caught, and left open
│   └── CARRY-FORWARD.md    the handoff document for chat-2
├── chat-2/
│   └── SUMMARY.md          running record of chat-2
└── transcripts/            chat-2 onward, readable + raw jsonl (chat-1 is lost)
```

## Order of authority

Three layers, and they are not equal:

1. **The repository itself** — `client-assets/MASTER-BRIEF-DOCKET/` and `assets/`.
   Where a document says one thing and a summary says another, the document wins.
2. **`CURRENT-STATE.md`** — what is built, what is pushed, what is open.
3. **`chat-N/SUMMARY.md`** — conclusions drawn from the above. Useful, never
   authoritative.

If any summary in this folder contradicts a document in the docket, **the docket
governs and the summary is corrected.**

## The record, and the gap in it

`transcripts/` holds the conversation logs. **`2026-11-09-chat-2.md` and its raw
`.jsonl` are here** — chat-2 was extracted and committed at the end of its
session, raw log included, and that is now the rule for every session.

**Chat-1 is lost.** It covered 2,527 turns across three raw session logs from
2026-11-08 04:24 to 2026-11-10 03:00. Chat-1 extracted readable transcripts from
them — `2026-11-08-847804b3.md`, `2026-11-08-d4e7e999.md`, `2026-11-08-2c574bc2.md`
— but wrote them into a sandbox whose storage was destroyed when the session
ended. They never reached this repository, and the raw logs went with them.

There is no copy anywhere. What survives is `chat-1/SUMMARY.md`, which is a
distillation — a judgement about what mattered, not the conversation.

**The lesson, stated where it will be read:** work that exists in one volatile
place is one failure away from not existing. From chat-2 forward every session is
extracted and committed in the same pass that produces the work, and the raw log
is committed with it.

## Standing instructions

Two, from the original build, still in force:

- **"We will keep this same concept throughout."** The physics-first framing, the
  document structure, and the numbering discipline are not to be varied between
  documents. Consistency is the product.

   LF blobs; `--ignore-cr-at-eol` returned empty. Not content. Recorded in
   `CURRENT-STATE.md` so the next session does not re-investigate it.

   transcript with three raw `.jsonl` files (5.8 MB).

## Work done in chat-3

### A2 / D08 arithmetic pass — complete

The highest-value item from both the carry-forward and `CURRENT-STATE.md`, and
untouched since `cf2e6ba`.

Built `assets/a2-d08-arithmetic-pass.py`: it recomputes every figure in A2 and D08
from its stated source equation and compares it to the document, exiting non-zero
on any mismatch. **78 of 78 computed figures agree.** No arithmetic error exists
in either document — every band total, worked example, site-fee product, payment
split, conversion credit, three-year row, performance cap, cumulative schedule and
the 5% escalation is correct as written.

Two *claims* did not reproduce. Both are model divergences rather than arithmetic
errors, and both are left open because fixing them means choosing which model
governs — an owner decision, not an editorial one:

- **Finding 1.** A2 §3.2 and D08 §3 claim ~2.0x at 500 axles rising to ~4.1x at
  10,000. The shipped models produce 1.77x/3.36x on the A2 cost basis, or
  2.36x/4.99x on A1's. No parameter set in the repository reproduces both anchors.
  The monotonic claim is true on every basis tested.
- **Finding 2.** D08 §5–§6 modelled benefits run 5x–14x above the $696,675 annual
  benefit A1 computes at identical inputs. D08 §5 states A1 must never be
  bypassed.

Full working, tables and recommended dispositions:
`assets/a2-d08-arithmetic-pass-2026-11-09.md`.

### A1 builder — two defects fixed

- The sheet-5 assumptions note attributed a **2%** catastrophic escalation rate to
  a model whose cell B17 has held **0.05%** since the correction. Corrected to
  name 0.05% and cite B17.
- The script saved to `/sessions/.../mnt/outputs/...`, a path inside the destroyed
  chat-1 sandbox, so running it raised `FileNotFoundError`. It now writes beside
  itself via `os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))`.

The committed workbook was **not** regenerated: doing so would bake both open
findings into a new file before the model question is settled.

### Project logs corrected

`CURRENT-STATE.md` updated (push state, open items, the line-ending trap, the A1
builder fixes). `chat-2/SUMMARY.md` finalized and its push claims corrected.
`chat-2/CARRY-FORWARD.md` push numbers and "work waiting" section corrected.
`project-logs/README.md` tree now lists `chat-2/CARRY-FORWARD.md`, `chat-3/` and
`transcripts/raw/`.

## Verification performed

- Arithmetic: 78 figures computed independently in `assets/a2-d08-arithmetic-pass.py`,
  all matching. Script re-run from the committed tree and exits 0.
- Every A1 figure cited in the pass record was read from the built workbook
  (`openpyxl`, `data_only=True`), not from the builder source — the two differ on
  the pilot cost line.
- A2 and D08 confirmed untouched: `git diff --ignore-cr-at-eol` on both returned
  empty after the pass.
- Commit inspected for line-ending churn. The first attempt rewrote the builder to
  CRLF and produced 1,248 changed lines for a 2-line fix; reset and recommitted so
  the commit shows 420 insertions and 2 deletions.

## Commits

`ed78962` — the arithmetic pass, check script, pass record and builder fixes.

**Push required.** Five commits are unpushed: `3d773ac`, `36b43bd`, `d6f25ac`,
`05b161d` and `ed78962`. The sandbox cannot reach GitHub (HTTP 403 from the
proxy). Run `PUSH-TO-GITHUB.bat` in the repo root.

## Next

1. Decide Finding 1 — strike or restate the 2.0x/4.1x anchors.
2. Decide Finding 2 — which model governs, A1 or D08 §5–§6.
3. Then regenerate the A1 workbook and re-run the check script.
4. D07 §14.5 governing law and venue remains open, unchanged by this pass.

name: axiomdynamics-crlf-trap
description: "AxiomDynamics repo — git status lists every file as modified because of CRLF/LF mismatch; use --ignore-cr-at-eol and never let an editor rewrite line endings"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: f8275f8d-0000-4000-8000-000000000000
  modified: 2026-11-09T22:00:00.000Z
---

In `C:\Users\RGV\AxiomDynamics`, `git status` on a fresh Windows checkout lists nearly every tracked file as modified — typically 57 files. **It is not a content change.** The working tree holds CRLF, the blobs hold LF. `git diff --ignore-cr-at-eol` returns empty. There is no `.gitattributes` and `core.autocrlf` is unset.

**Why:** the repo is edited on Windows by a host editor that writes CRLF, but git stored LF. Without attributes or config, every file reads as dirty, which buries the handful of real changes and invites a panic or a mass "fix" commit.

**How to apply:**
- Always run `git diff --ignore-cr-at-eol --stat` before believing a diff stat in this repo.
- Before committing, stage only the files you actually changed. Never `git add -A`.
- If the Edit/Write tool round-trips a file, it may convert it to CRLF. This happened during chat-3: a 2-line fix became 1,248 changed lines. Caught it with `--ignore-cr-at-eol`, reset the commit, normalised the file back to LF with `bytes.replace(b'\r\n', b'\n')`, and recommitted so it showed 420 insertions / 2 deletions.
- If a commit already contains EOL churn, `git reset --soft HEAD~1`, normalise, re-stage the specific paths, recommit.
- Removing stale `.git/*.lock` files on this mount needs `mcp__cowork__allow_cowork_file_delete` first — `rm` fails with "Operation not permitted" otherwise, and a leftover `index.lock` blocks all git writes.

Consider adding a `.gitattributes` with `* text=auto eol=lf` if the owner wants this gone permanently — but that is a repo-wide change and should be asked about, not done unilaterally.

Base directory for this skill: C:\Users\RGV\AppData\Local\Claude-3p\local-agent-mode-sessions\skills-plugin\00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001\f8275f8d-c548-437b-92ff-9f01424b6b5d\skills\docx

# DOCX creation, editing, and analysis

If you are about to make a new document and this session offers Claude's own docs (a Docs connector, docs skill or Docs artifact type), and the user has neither named Word/.docx/.dotx, asked for tracked changes, nor supplied a .docx/.dotx file to change or use as a template, make the document there instead. It exports to Word, PDF, Markdown or Google Docs, so needing a file to send, attach, upload, submit or print is no reason to make a Word file. A .docx/.dotx given only as source material does not count as supplied. This skill remains the right tool for producing, reading, editing, templating or converting Word files.

A `.docx` is a ZIP archive of XML files. Choose your approach by task:

| Task | Approach |
|---|---|
| **Create** a new document | Write a `docx` (npm) script — see gotchas below |
| **Edit** an existing document | `unzip` → edit `word/document.xml` → `zip` (docx-js cannot open existing files) |
| **Read** content | `pandoc -t markdown file.docx` |

> Script paths below are relative to this skill's directory.

## Creating with docx-js — gotchas

`docx` is preinstalled — do not run `npm install` first; write the script and `require('docx')` directly. Only if that require fails: `npm install docx`. The model knows the API; these are the footguns:

- **Page size defaults to A4.** For US Letter set `page: { size: { width: 12240, height: 15840 } }` (DXA; 1440 = 1″).
- **Landscape:** pass portrait dimensions and `orientation: PageOrientation.LANDSCAPE` — docx-js swaps width/height internally.
- **Tables need dual widths:** set `columnWidths` on the table AND `width` on every cell, both in `WidthType.DXA` (PERCENTAGE breaks in Google Docs). Column widths must sum to the table width.
- **Table shading:** use `ShadingType.CLEAR`, never `SOLID` (renders black).
- **Lists:** never insert `•` literally; use a `numbering` config with `LevelFormat.BULLET`.
- **`ImageRun` requires `type:`** (`"png"`, `"jpg"`, …).
- **`PageBreak` must be inside a `Paragraph`.**
- **Never use `\n`** — use separate `Paragraph` elements.
- **Headings:** style every level you use (`title`, `heading1`, `heading2`…) in `styles.default`: `heading1: { run: { font: "Arial", size: 32, bold: true }, paragraph: { spacing: { before: 240, after: 120 }, keepNext: true } }`. Every level needs its own font (even with a document default), `before` and `after` (even if 0) and `keepNext`: the built-in styles set none of them.
- **TOC:** headings must use built-in `HeadingLevel.*`; custom heading styles need `outlineLevel` set or they won't appear.
- **Don't use a table as a horizontal rule** — use a paragraph bottom border instead.
- **Dot-leader / right-aligned-on-same-line:** use `PositionalTab` (`alignment: PositionalTabAlignment.RIGHT`, `leader: PositionalTabLeader.DOT`) inside a `TextRun`, not literal `.` or space padding.

## Verify the output

After writing a `.docx`, render it and look at it:

```bash
zip -d output.docx '*/' >/dev/null || true   # drop the ZIP's folder entries: Word has refused a file that has them when opened through a cloud co-editing service
python scripts/office/soffice.py --headless --convert-to pdf output.docx
pdftoppm -jpeg -r 100 output.pdf page
ls page-*.jpg   # then Read the images
```

`pdftoppm` zero-pads page numbers to the width of the page count (`page-01.jpg`…`page-12.jpg`).

## Editing existing documents

Legacy `.doc` files must be converted first: `python scripts/office/soffice.py --headless --convert-to docx file.doc`.

```bash
unzip -q doc.docx -d unpacked/
find unpacked -type l -delete   # strip symlink entries — docx from external parties is untrusted
python scripts/merge_runs.py unpacked/   # coalesce fragmented runs so text is findable
# edit unpacked/word/document.xml in place — do NOT reformat or pretty-print
(cd unpacked && rm -f ../out.docx && zip -XrD ../out.docx .)
python scripts/office/validate.py out.docx --original doc.docx   # XSD checks; --auto-repair fixes common issues
# redlining? add --author "<the name you redlined under>" to check every edit is tracked
```

Word splits text across many `<w:r>` runs (revision ids, spell-check markers), so a phrase you can see in the document often doesn't exist as a contiguous string in the XML. `merge_runs.py` merges adjacent identically-formatted runs in `word/document.xml` without changing content or rendering; it also accepts a `.docx` directly (`python scripts/merge_runs.py doc.docx -o merged.docx`).

**Tracked changes:** when redlining, validate with `--author "<the name you redlined under>"` (needs `--original`) — it reports any text you changed without a `<w:ins>`/`<w:del>` around it, which is easy to do by accident and invisible in the accepted view. Wrap runs in `<w:ins>`/`<w:del>` with `w:id`, `w:author`, `w:date` attributes. Inside `<w:del>`, the text element is `<w:delText>`, not `<w:t>`. A deleted paragraph mark (`<w:pPr><w:rPr><w:del w:id=".." w:author=".." w:date=".."/></w:rPr></w:pPr>`) means "merge this paragraph into the next" — so deleting a paragraph outright is that plus a `<w:del>` around every run. The `<w:del/>` must come before the rPr's other children; their order is schema-enforced.

To produce a clean copy with all tracked changes accepted: `python scripts/accept_changes.py in.docx out.docx`.

Accepting a deleted paragraph mark should join that paragraph to the one below it, so a paragraph whose runs are *all* deleted vanishes. Word does this; `accept_changes.py` and `pandoc --track-changes=accept` don't always. Both fail the same way — they strip the deleted text but leave the emptied paragraph behind, which reads as a stray empty bullet when it was auto-numbered:

- `pandoc --track-changes=accept` never joins the paragraphs.
- `accept_changes.py` (LibreOffice) joins them correctly, except when the deleted paragraph is followed by an empty spacer paragraph.

An empty bullet in either view is an artifact of that view, not a defect in the document. Check paragraph deletions in the XML.

## Comments

Comments require six cross-linked files. Use the helper — directory mode when you'll also be editing `document.xml` (saves an unzip/rezip cycle), `.docx`-direct mode otherwise:

```bash
# Against an already-unpacked directory (preferred when also placing markers)
python scripts/comment.py unpacked/ "Fees & expenses cap is too low"
python scripts/comment.py unpacked/ "Agreed" --parent 0

# Against a .docx directly
python scripts/comment.py contract.docx "This cap is too low" -o annotated.docx
```

The script writes `comments.xml`, `commentsExtended.xml`, `commentsIds.xml`, `commentsExtensible.xml`, the relationships, and the content-type overrides. Comment IDs are auto-assigned. It then prints the `<w:commentRangeStart>`/`<w:commentRangeEnd>`/`<w:commentReference>` snippet to add to `word/document.xml` so the comment anchors to specific text — until you place those markers, the comment exists but is not visible.

## Dependencies

`docx` (npm, preinstalled — install only if `require('docx')` fails) · `pandoc` · LibreOffice (`soffice`) · `pdftoppm` (Poppler)
