---

## What this project is

Physics-first predictive maintenance for freight rail. Six named physical models
— thermodynamics with per-axle rolling z-score, peer median/MAD comparison,
kinematics, acoustics (BPFO/BPFI/BSF/FTF), same-axle left/right differential, and
an executive ROI panel — instead of black-box ML or fixed alarm thresholds.

The Master Brief Docket is in `client-assets/MASTER-BRIEF-DOCKET/`: 38 artifacts
— 36 Markdown documents, the A1 Excel model (with its build script beside it) and
the B03 HTML infographic — across A (commercial), B (technical), C (deployment)
and D (contractual) series plus F (forms).

## Build status

**38 artifacts on disk; 37 docket IDs on disk (A1 is a folder holding the `.xlsx`
and the builder, so it counts as one ID and two files).** The docket index (D00)
carries 37 ID rows; 34 are marked `**Built**` in bold, and B02 (.md) and B03
(.html) carry plain "Built" with a format qualifier. D00 Part IV is the authority
on status, not this file.

A long-form account of the whole build — every stage, every document, every
correction, and the loss and rebuild — is at
`project-logs/AxiomDynamics-Build-History-and-Working-Summary.docx` (29 pages).
It is generated by `project-logs/build-history-summary.js`; re-run
`node project-logs/build-history-summary.js` after a material change.

Open docket items are tracked in **D00 Part IV** — that table is the authority,
not this file.

## The largest known gap

**There is no detector ingest path.** No endpoint accepts a Railroad payload.
Every demonstration signal is generated from the physics equations on synthetic
traces. This is disclosed in B01 §7 gap #5, B02 §2 and the B03 status block.

Every demonstration number demonstrates **the method**, not the Railroad's data.
The validation chain — schema, timestamp, plausibility — is designed and not built.

## Open items, in priority order

1. **Two A2/D08 model findings — need an owner decision.** The arithmetic pass of
   2026-11-09 found **no arithmetic errors** in either document (78 of 78 figures
   recompute correctly). It did find that two *claims* do not reproduce from the
   shipped model. Full detail in
   `assets/a2-d08-arithmetic-pass-2026-11-09.md`; run the check with
   `python3 -I assets/a2-d08-arithmetic-pass.py`.
   - **Finding 1.** A2 §3.2 and D08 §3 claim ~2.0x return at 500 axles rising to
     ~4.1x at 10,000. The shipped models give 1.77x/3.36x on the A2 cost basis or
     2.36x/4.99x on A1's. No parameter set in the repo reproduces both anchors.
     The monotonic claim holds on every basis; the two anchor values do not.
   - **Finding 2.** D08 §5–§6 modelled benefits ($6–8M pilot year, $14–20M
     four-year, $40–60M six-year) run 5x–14x above the $696,675 annual benefit A1
     computes at identical inputs. D08 §5 states A1 must never be bypassed.
     One of the two models governs and it has not been chosen.
2. **D07 §14.5 — governing law and venue.** An open counsel decision, correctly
   labelled as open as of chat-2 (previously a blank pointing at an Order field
   that does not exist). Must be closed by signed addendum before first execution.
3. **A1 workbook regeneration.** Deliberately not regenerated during the
   arithmetic pass, because doing so would bake both open findings into a new
   file before the model question is settled. The builder is now fixed (see
   below) and will regenerate on demand once findings 1 and 2 are decided.
4. **D09 §4.4 supply-chain gaps** — SBOM (Q1 2027), hash verification of
   dependency downloads (Q1 2027), GPG-signed releases (Q2 2027). All disclosed.
5. **Disposition ledger** — currently overwrites rather than appends. The
   evidentiary claim in F09 is ahead of the code until AD-3 lands (Q2 2027).

## A1 builder — fixed in chat-3

Two defects in `A1-ROI-MODEL/build_roi_calculator.py`, both cosmetic to the
workbook but both real if anyone runs it:

- The sheet-5 assumptions note attributed a **2% catastrophic escalation rate** to
  a model whose cell B17 has held **0.05%** since the correction. A reader
  reconciling the sheet against its own footnote would find a ten-fold conflict.
- The script saved to `/sessions/.../mnt/outputs/...`, a path inside the destroyed
  chat-1 sandbox, so running it raised `FileNotFoundError`. It now writes beside
  itself.


## Git state

The sandbox **cannot reach GitHub** — `git push` and `git fetch` both fail with
HTTP 403 from the proxy. Its `origin/main` ref therefore only advances when the
owner pushes and the sandbox is told the result. Do not trust it as evidence of
remote state without checking the commits page.

**Pushing is done by the owner**, with `PUSH-TO-GITHUB.bat` in the repo root. It
prints the commits waiting to go up and verifies afterwards.

**As of 2026-11-09, everything is pushed.** GitHub's top commit is `2ec168b`,
confirmed by the owner against the commits page.

**The host repo at `C:\Users\RGV\AxiomDynamics` is authoritative for push state.**
Verify by opening the commits page.

**The line-ending trap.** `git status` in this repo lists nearly every tracked file
as modified on a fresh Windows checkout. It is CRLF working-tree content against
LF blobs, not a content change — `git diff --ignore-cr-at-eol` returns empty.
There is no `.gitattributes` and `core.autocrlf` is unset. **Always check with
`--ignore-cr-at-eol` before believing a diff stat**, and never let an editor
rewrite a whole file's endings into a commit: doing so once during chat-3 turned a
two-line fix into 1,248 changed lines, which had to be reset and recommitted.


## What was lost in the chat-1 → chat-2 transition

Recorded here so nobody goes looking for it:

- Three commits built at the end of chat-1 (`0b66d21`, `cb4f74d`, and the
  F00/D07/Q6 work) existed only in the old sandbox. **`F00` Rule 7, the D07 §14
  rewrite and Q6 were rebuilt into the repository in chat-2.** The project-logs
  structure was rebuilt. The transcripts were not and cannot be — see
  `README.md`.
- Because the rebuild is a reconstruction rather than a recovery, the wording may
  differ from what chat-1 wrote. The *decisions* are identical; the prose is not
  guaranteed to be. Do not treat the current text as a restoration of an earlier
  draft.

## Standing instructions

- **[WORK LOCATION] All project work is written directly into this repository, first pass, and committed in the same pass.** No drafts in sandbox scratch space — that is how chat-1's final phase was lost.
- Keep the same concept throughout — consistency of framing across every document.
- Internal analysis goes in `assets/`, never `client-assets/`.
- Verify against the file before writing the claim.

## Why chat-1's work was lost — the mechanism

Not a deletion. The work was never on the owner's machine.

Chat-1 built the repo inside a temporary sandbox container. To get anything out
it bundled the repo, embedded the bundle in a `.bat`, and the owner ran it once —
which is how `de9b245` reached GitHub. **Everything chat-1 did after that push
stayed in the container**, including the F00 Rule 7 work, the D07 §14 rewrite, Q6
and the transcripts. The bundle was never remade. When the session ended the
container was destroyed and took all of it.

The failure was treating "committed" as "safe." Inside that container it only
meant "saved somewhere that is about to be emptied."

**The rule that follows:** there is no automatic export. A commit in the sandbox
is not durable until it is in `C:\Users\RGV\AxiomDynamics` and pushed. Never tell
the owner work is saved without saying where it physically is.

# AxiomDynamics — Project Logs

This folder is the memory of the project. It exists because the work outgrew a
single conversation, and a fresh thread with no record of what was decided
rebuilds the same mistakes.

## Structure

```
project-logs/
├── README.md               this file — structure, purpose, order of authority
├── CURRENT-STATE.md        authoritative project state, updated as work lands
├── chat-1/
│   ├── SUMMARY.md          what chat-1 did, decided, caught, and left open
│   └── CARRY-FORWARD.md    the handoff document for chat-2
├── chat-2/
│   ├── SUMMARY.md          what chat-2 did; closed 2026-11-09
│   └── CARRY-FORWARD.md    the handoff document for chat-3
├── chat-3/
│   └── SUMMARY.md          running record of chat-3
└── transcripts/            chat-2 onward, readable + raw jsonl (chat-1 is lost)
    └── raw/                the source logs, committed with each transcript
```

## Order of authority

Three layers, and they are not equal:

1. **The repository itself** — `client-assets/MASTER-BRIEF-DOCKET/` and `assets/`.
   Where a document says one thing and a summary says another, the document wins.
2. **`CURRENT-STATE.md`** — what is built, what is pushed, what is open.
3. **`chat-N/SUMMARY.md`** — conclusions drawn from the above. Useful, never
   authoritative.

If any summary in this folder contradicts a document in the docket, **the docket
governs and the summary is corrected.**

## The record, and the gap in it

`transcripts/` holds the conversation logs. **`2026-11-09-chat-2.md` and its raw
`.jsonl` are here** — chat-2 was extracted and committed at the end of its
session, raw log included, and that is now the rule for every session.

**Chat-1 is lost.** It covered 2,527 turns across three raw session logs from
2026-11-08 04:24 to 2026-11-10 03:00. Chat-1 extracted readable transcripts from
them — `2026-11-08-847804b3.md`, `2026-11-08-d4e7e999.md`, `2026-11-08-2c574bc2.md`
— but wrote them into a sandbox whose storage was destroyed when the session
ended. They never reached this repository, and the raw logs went with them.

There is no copy anywhere. What survives is `chat-1/SUMMARY.md`, which is a
distillation — a judgement about what mattered, not the conversation.

**The lesson, stated where it will be read:** work that exists in one volatile
place is one failure away from not existing. From chat-2 forward every session is
extracted and committed in the same pass that produces the work, and the raw log
is committed with it.

## Standing instructions

Two, from the original build, still in force:

- **"We will keep this same concept throughout."** The physics-first framing, the
  document structure, and the numbering discipline are not to be varied between
  documents. Consistency is the product.
- **"Strictly goes in our assets folder."** Internal analysis belongs in
  `assets/`, never in `client-assets/`. Client-facing material is
  `client-assets/MASTER-BRIEF-DOCKET/` only.

A third, added 2026-11-09 after the loss described above:

- **"Drop all the entire project work directly in AxiomDynamics folder so we don't
  lose any data from sandbox."** Work is written into this repository on the first
  pass and committed in the same pass that produces it. No drafts parked anywhere
  else. The sandbox is scratch space and its storage does not survive a session;
  this repository does.

## The discipline that matters most

Chat-1's own summary records it, and the record confirms it: nearly every bad
citation in the project came from writing a claim from memory and checking
afterwards. The worst defect — the detector ingest path drawn as built when no
inbound route exists — came from the same habit applied to a diagram.

**So: verify against the file, then write. Not the reverse.**

"""
SQLite-backed persistence for reviewer dispositions.

Deliberately the stdlib `sqlite3` module -- no new dependency, no server
process, one file (`axiom.db`) that lives next to the app and survives a
restart. This replaces an earlier in-memory dict: a disposition is an
audit-relevant record (who reviewed what, and what they decided), and
losing it on every restart undercuts the whole "human-in-the-loop" story.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
import sqlite3
from contextlib import contextmanager
from typing import Dict, Optional

DB_PATH = os.environ.get("AXIOM_DB_PATH", os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))), "axiom.db"))


@contextmanager
def _connect():
    conn = sqlite3.connect(DB_PATH)
    try:
        yield conn
        conn.commit()
    finally:
        conn.close()


def init_db():
    with _connect() as conn:
        conn.execute("""
            CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS dispositions (
                advisory_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
                reviewer_name TEXT NOT NULL,
                cert_id TEXT NOT NULL,
                disposition TEXT NOT NULL,
                recorded_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now'))
            )
        """)


def save_disposition(advisory_id: str, reviewer_name: str, cert_id: str, disposition: str):
    with _connect() as conn:
        conn.execute(
            """
            INSERT INTO dispositions (advisory_id, reviewer_name, cert_id, disposition, recorded_at)
            VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, datetime('now'))
            ON CONFLICT(advisory_id) DO UPDATE SET
                reviewer_name=excluded.reviewer_name,
                cert_id=excluded.cert_id,
                disposition=excluded.disposition,
                recorded_at=excluded.recorded_at
            """,
            (advisory_id, reviewer_name, cert_id, disposition),
        )


def get_disposition(advisory_id: str) -> Optional[Dict[str, str]]:
    with _connect() as conn:
        row = conn.execute(
            "SELECT reviewer_name, cert_id, disposition, recorded_at FROM dispositions WHERE advisory_id = ?",
            (advisory_id,),
        ).fetchone()
    if row is None:
        return None
    return {"reviewer_name": row[0], "cert_id": row[1], "disposition": row[2], "recorded_at": row[3]}


def all_dispositions() -> Dict[str, Dict[str, str]]:
    with _connect() as conn:
        rows = conn.execute(
            "SELECT advisory_id, reviewer_name, cert_id, disposition, recorded_at FROM dispositions"
        ).fetchall()
    return {
        r[0]: {"reviewer_name": r[1], "cert_id": r[2], "disposition": r[3], "recorded_at": r[4]}
        for r in rows
    }

VALID_DISPOSITIONS = {
    "concur_dispatch": "Concurred — dispatch order issued",

    "override_downgrade": "Reviewer override — downgraded on field experience",
    "reject_sensor": "Rejected — suspected sensor/hardware fault, S&C dispatched",

def _apply_disposition(warrant):
    rec = store.get_disposition(warrant.advisory_id)
    if rec:
        warrant.reviewer_disposition = (
            f"{VALID_DISPOSITIONS.get(rec['disposition'], rec['disposition'])} "
            f"— {rec['reviewer_name']} ({rec['cert_id']})"
        )
    return warrant


def route_alerts(_query):
    """

    warrant fuses every independent model's reading for one axle and is
    only escalated to URGENT REVIEW when at least two independent signal

    out = []

    warrants_list = route_alerts(_query)
    summary = roi_mod.compute_roi_summary(warrants_list)
    flagged_assets = {w.asset_id for w in warrants_list}

input.content:
"""
SQLite-backed, append-only persistence for reviewer dispositions.

Implements AD-3 (B01 §2): a disposition may be superseded but never overwritten
and never deleted. Three layers enforce that, and each one is load-bearing:

1. **No UPDATE or DELETE path in Python.** There is no function here that
   mutates a row. A correction is a new row carrying `supersedes_id`, which
   points at the row it corrects. Both rows survive.

2. **Database-level triggers.** Even someone holding the sqlite3 CLI, or a
   future contributor who adds an innocent-looking UPDATE, is stopped:
   `BEFORE UPDATE` and `BEFORE DELETE` on the ledger raise ABORT. The Python
   layer is not the guarantee; the schema is.

3. **A hash chain.** Each row carries `prev_hash` (the previous row's
   `record_hash`, or 64 zeros for the first) and `record_hash`, a SHA-256 over
   the row's own content plus `prev_hash`. Editing a row in place therefore
   breaks its own hash, and deleting one breaks the next row's `prev_hash`.
   `verify_chain()` recomputes the whole chain and reports the first row that
   fails.

What this does and does not prove — state it plainly rather than implying more:

- It **does** prove the ledger has not been altered *by anything that went
  through this database*. An attacker with write access to the file can drop the
  triggers, rewrite rows and recompute every hash; the chain is a tamper-*evident*
  control, not tamper-*proof*.
- It **does** make an accidental overwrite impossible rather than merely
  discouraged, which is what the old upsert allowed.
- It does **not** replicate off-box. A destroyed disk still destroys the
  ledger. Off-box replication and signed audit export remain separate gaps
  (D09 §4.4).

Deliberately the stdlib `sqlite3` module — no new dependency, no server
process, one file that survives a restart.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
import os
import sqlite3
from contextlib import contextmanager
from typing import Dict, List, Optional

DB_PATH = os.environ.get("AXIOM_DB_PATH", os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))), "axiom.db"))

GENESIS_HASH = "0" * 64

SCHEMA_VERSION = 2


@contextmanager
def _connect():
    conn = sqlite3.connect(DB_PATH)
    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
    try:
        yield conn
        conn.commit()
    finally:
        conn.close()


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Chain arithmetic
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def _row_payload(row: Dict[str, object]) -> str:
    """
    Canonical serialisation of the fields the hash covers.

    `sort_keys=True`, no whitespace, fixed separators — so the same row always
    hashes the same way and a verifier in another language can reproduce it
    from the documented field list. `record_hash` is excluded, obviously.
    """
    covered = {
        "advisory_id": row["advisory_id"],
        "reviewer_name": row["reviewer_name"],
        "cert_id": row["cert_id"],
        "disposition": row["disposition"],
        "note": row["note"],
        "recorded_at": row["recorded_at"],
        "supersedes_id": row["supersedes_id"],
        "prev_hash": row["prev_hash"],
    }
    return json.dumps(covered, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"))


def _compute_hash(row: Dict[str, object]) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(_row_payload(row).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Schema
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def init_db():
    """
    Create the ledger and its guard triggers, and migrate a v1 table in place.

    The v1 schema was `dispositions(advisory_id PRIMARY KEY, ...)` — one row per
    advisory, overwritten on re-decision. A v1 row held the *latest* decision
    and nothing else. Migration keeps that decision, marks it as the first link
    in the chain, and cannot invent history it never had; the timestamps of any
    prior overwrites are already gone and are not fabricated.
    """
    with _connect() as conn:
        existing = conn.execute(
            "SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table' AND name='dispositions'"
        ).fetchone()

        if existing is not None:
            cols = {r["name"] for r in conn.execute("PRAGMA table_info(dispositions)").fetchall()}
            if "record_hash" not in cols:
                _migrate_v1(conn)

        conn.execute("""
            CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS dispositions (
                id            INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
                advisory_id   TEXT NOT NULL,
                reviewer_name TEXT NOT NULL,
                cert_id       TEXT NOT NULL,
                disposition   TEXT NOT NULL,
                note          TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
                recorded_at   TEXT NOT NULL,
                supersedes_id INTEGER REFERENCES dispositions(id),
                prev_hash     TEXT NOT NULL,
                record_hash   TEXT NOT NULL
            )
        """)
        conn.execute("""
            CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_dispositions_advisory
            ON dispositions (advisory_id, id)
        """)

        # Guard triggers. `IF NOT EXISTS` so re-running init_db is harmless.
        # DROP TRIGGER is itself possible for someone with file access — see the
        # module docstring on what the chain does and does not prove.
        conn.execute("""
            CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS dispositions_no_update
            BEFORE UPDATE ON dispositions
            BEGIN
                SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'disposition ledger is append-only: UPDATE is not permitted (AD-3)');
            END
        """)
        conn.execute("""
            CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS dispositions_no_delete
            BEFORE DELETE ON dispositions
            BEGIN
                SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'disposition ledger is append-only: DELETE is not permitted (AD-3)');
            END
        """)

        conn.execute("PRAGMA user_version = %d" % SCHEMA_VERSION)


def _migrate_v1(conn):
    """Convert the v1 one-row-per-advisory table into an append-only ledger."""
    rows = conn.execute(
        "SELECT advisory_id, reviewer_name, cert_id, disposition, recorded_at "
        "FROM dispositions ORDER BY recorded_at, advisory_id"
    ).fetchall()

    conn.execute("ALTER TABLE dispositions RENAME TO dispositions_v1")

    prev = GENESIS_HASH
    for r in rows:
        rec = {
            "advisory_id": r["advisory_id"],
            "reviewer_name": r["reviewer_name"],
            "cert_id": r["cert_id"],
            "disposition": r["disposition"],
            "note": "",
            "recorded_at": r["recorded_at"],
            "supersedes_id": None,
            "prev_hash": prev,
        }
        rec["record_hash"] = _compute_hash(rec)
        conn.execute(
            """
            INSERT INTO dispositions
                (advisory_id, reviewer_name, cert_id, disposition, note,
                 recorded_at, supersedes_id, prev_hash, record_hash)
            VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
            """,
            (rec["advisory_id"], rec["reviewer_name"], rec["cert_id"],
             rec["disposition"], rec["note"], rec["recorded_at"],
             None, rec["prev_hash"], rec["record_hash"]),
        )
        prev = rec["record_hash"]

    conn.execute("DROP TABLE dispositions_v1")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Writes — insert only
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def save_disposition(advisory_id: str, reviewer_name: str, cert_id: str,
                     disposition: str, note: str = "") -> Dict[str, object]:
    """
    Append a disposition. Never updates.

    A second decision on the same advisory becomes a new row whose
    `supersedes_id` names the row it replaces. The earlier row keeps its own
    timestamp and content and remains readable.

    Runs under BEGIN IMMEDIATE so two concurrent appends cannot both read the
    same `prev_hash` and fork the chain.
    """
    with _connect_atomic() as conn:
        prev = conn.execute(
            "SELECT record_hash FROM dispositions ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 1"
        ).fetchone()
        prev_hash = prev["record_hash"] if prev else GENESIS_HASH

        prior = conn.execute(
            "SELECT id FROM dispositions WHERE advisory_id = ? ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 1",
            (advisory_id,),
        ).fetchone()

        recorded_at = conn.execute("SELECT datetime('now') AS t").fetchone()["t"]

        rec = {
            "advisory_id": advisory_id,
            "reviewer_name": reviewer_name,
            "cert_id": cert_id,
            "disposition": disposition,
            "note": note,
            "recorded_at": recorded_at,
            "supersedes_id": prior["id"] if prior else None,
            "prev_hash": prev_hash,
        }
        rec["record_hash"] = _compute_hash(rec)

        cur = conn.execute(
            """
            INSERT INTO dispositions
                (advisory_id, reviewer_name, cert_id, disposition, note,
                 recorded_at, supersedes_id, prev_hash, record_hash)
            VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
            """,
            (rec["advisory_id"], rec["reviewer_name"], rec["cert_id"],
             rec["disposition"], rec["note"], rec["recorded_at"],
             rec["supersedes_id"], rec["prev_hash"], rec["record_hash"]),
        )
        rec["id"] = cur.lastrowid
        return dict(rec)


@contextmanager
def _connect_atomic():
    conn = sqlite3.connect(DB_PATH, isolation_level=None)
    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
    try:
        conn.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
        yield conn
        conn.execute("COMMIT")
    except Exception:
        conn.execute("ROLLBACK")
        raise
    finally:
        conn.close()


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Reads
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def get_disposition(advisory_id: str) -> Optional[Dict[str, object]]:
    """The current (latest) disposition for one advisory, or None."""
    with _connect() as conn:
        row = conn.execute(
            """
            SELECT id, advisory_id, reviewer_name, cert_id, disposition, note,
                   recorded_at, supersedes_id, prev_hash, record_hash
            FROM dispositions WHERE advisory_id = ? ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 1
            """,
            (advisory_id,),
        ).fetchone()
    return dict(row) if row else None


def disposition_history(advisory_id: str) -> List[Dict[str, object]]:
    """Every disposition ever recorded for one advisory, oldest first."""
    with _connect() as conn:
        rows = conn.execute(
            """
            SELECT id, advisory_id, reviewer_name, cert_id, disposition, note,
                   recorded_at, supersedes_id, prev_hash, record_hash
            FROM dispositions WHERE advisory_id = ? ORDER BY id ASC
            """,
            (advisory_id,),
        ).fetchall()
    return [dict(r) for r in rows]


def all_dispositions() -> Dict[str, Dict[str, object]]:
    """Current disposition per advisory — the shape callers already expect."""
    out: Dict[str, Dict[str, object]] = {}
    with _connect() as conn:
        rows = conn.execute(
            """
            SELECT id, advisory_id, reviewer_name, cert_id, disposition, note,
                   recorded_at, supersedes_id, prev_hash, record_hash
            FROM dispositions ORDER BY id ASC
            """
        ).fetchall()
    for r in rows:
        out[r["advisory_id"]] = dict(r)
    return out


def ledger_size() -> int:
    with _connect() as conn:
        return conn.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM dispositions").fetchone()["n"]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Verification
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def verify_chain() -> Dict[str, object]:
    """
    Recompute the whole chain. Returns
        {"ok": bool, "rows": n, "broken_at_id": int|None, "reason": str|None}

    Detects: a row whose content was changed (its own hash stops matching), a
    row removed from the middle (the next row's prev_hash no longer matches),
    and a chain whose links point at nothing.
    """
    with _connect() as conn:
        rows = conn.execute(
            """
            SELECT id, advisory_id, reviewer_name, cert_id, disposition, note,
                   recorded_at, supersedes_id, prev_hash, record_hash
            FROM dispositions ORDER BY id ASC
            """
        ).fetchall()

    expected_prev = GENESIS_HASH
    for r in rows:
        rec = dict(r)
        if rec["prev_hash"] != expected_prev:
            return {"ok": False, "rows": len(rows), "broken_at_id": rec["id"],
                    "reason": "prev_hash does not match the preceding row "
                              "(a row was inserted, removed or reordered)"}
        if _compute_hash(rec) != rec["record_hash"]:
            return {"ok": False, "rows": len(rows), "broken_at_id": rec["id"],
                    "reason": "record_hash does not match the row content "
                              "(the row was altered)"}
        expected_prev = rec["record_hash"]

    return {"ok": True, "rows": len(rows), "broken_at_id": None, "reason": None}

   mutates a row. A correction is a new row carrying `supersedes_id`, which
   points at the row it corrects. Both rows survive.

2. **Database-level triggers.** Even someone holding the sqlite3 CLI, or a
   future contributor who adds an innocent-looking UPDATE, is stopped:
   `BEFORE UPDATE` and `BEFORE DELETE` on the ledger raise ABORT. The Python
   layer is not the guarantee; the schema is.

3. **A hash chain.** Each row carries `prev_hash` (the previous row's
   `record_hash`, or 64 zeros for the first) and `record_hash`, a SHA-256 over
   the row's own content plus `prev_hash`. Editing a row in place therefore
   breaks its own hash, and deleting one breaks the next row's `prev_hash`.
   `verify_chain()` recomputes the whole chain and reports the first row that
   fails.

What this does and does not prove — state it plainly rather than implying more:

- It **does** prove the ledger has not been altered *by anything that went
  through this database*. An attacker with write access to the file can drop the
  triggers, rewrite rows and recompute every hash; the chain is a tamper-*evident*
  control, not tamper-*proof*.
- It **does** make an accidental overwrite impossible rather than merely
  discouraged, which is what the old upsert allowed.
- It does **not** replicate off-box. A destroyed disk still destroys the
  ledger. Off-box replication and signed audit export remain separate gaps
  (D09 §4.4).

Deliberately the stdlib `sqlite3` module — no new dependency, no server
process, one file that survives a restart.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
import os
import sqlite3
from contextlib import contextmanager
from typing import Dict, List, Optional

DB_PATH = os.environ.get("AXIOM_DB_PATH", os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))), "axiom.db"))

GENESIS_HASH = "0" * 64

SCHEMA_VERSION = 2


@contextmanager
def _connect():
    conn = sqlite3.connect(DB_PATH)
    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
    try:
        yield conn
        conn.commit()
    finally:
        conn.close()


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Chain arithmetic
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def _row_payload(row: Dict[str, object]) -> str:
    """
    Canonical serialisation of the fields the hash covers.

    `sort_keys=True`, no whitespace, fixed separators — so the same row always
    hashes the same way and a verifier in another language can reproduce it
    from the documented field list. `record_hash` is excluded, obviously.
    """
    covered = {
        "advisory_id": row["advisory_id"],
        "reviewer_name": row["reviewer_name"],
        "cert_id": row["cert_id"],
        "disposition": row["disposition"],
        "note": row["note"],
        "recorded_at": row["recorded_at"],
        "supersedes_id": row["supersedes_id"],
        "prev_hash": row["prev_hash"],
    }
    return json.dumps(covered, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"))


def _compute_hash(row: Dict[str, object]) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(_row_payload(row).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Schema
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def init_db():
    """
    Create the ledger and its guard triggers, and migrate a v1 table in place.

    The v1 schema was `dispositions(advisory_id PRIMARY KEY, ...)` — one row per
    advisory, overwritten on re-decision. A v1 row held the *latest* decision
    and nothing else. Migration keeps that decision, marks it as the first link
    in the chain, and cannot invent history it never had; the timestamps of any
    prior overwrites are already gone and are not fabricated.
    """
    with _connect() as conn:
        existing = conn.execute(
            "SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table' AND name='dispositions'"
        ).fetchone()

        if existing is not None:
            cols = {r["name"] for r in conn.execute("PRAGMA table_info(dispositions)").fetchall()}
            if "record_hash" not in cols:
                _migrate_v1(conn)

        conn.execute("""
            CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS dispositions (
                id            INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
                advisory_id   TEXT NOT NULL,
                reviewer_name TEXT NOT NULL,
                cert_id       TEXT NOT NULL,
                disposition   TEXT NOT NULL,
                note          TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
                recorded_at   TEXT NOT NULL,
                supersedes_id INTEGER REFERENCES dispositions(id),
                prev_hash     TEXT NOT NULL,
                record_hash   TEXT NOT NULL
            )
        """)
        conn.execute("""
            CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_dispositions_advisory
            ON dispositions (advisory_id, id)
        """)

        # Guard triggers. `IF NOT EXISTS` so re-running init_db is harmless.
        # DROP TRIGGER is itself possible for someone with file access — see the
        # module docstring on what the chain does and does not prove.
        conn.execute("""
            CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS dispositions_no_update
            BEFORE UPDATE ON dispositions
            BEGIN
                SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'disposition ledger is append-only: UPDATE is not permitted (AD-3)');
            END
        """)
        conn.execute("""
            CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS dispositions_no_delete
            BEFORE DELETE ON dispositions
            BEGIN
                SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'disposition ledger is append-only: DELETE is not permitted (AD-3)');
            END
        """)

        conn.execute("PRAGMA user_version = %d" % SCHEMA_VERSION)


def _migrate_v1(conn):
    """Convert the v1 one-row-per-advisory table into an append-only ledger."""
    rows = conn.execute(
        "SELECT advisory_id, reviewer_name, cert_id, disposition, recorded_at "
        "FROM dispositions ORDER BY recorded_at, advisory_id"
    ).fetchall()

    conn.execute("ALTER TABLE dispositions RENAME TO dispositions_v1")

    prev = GENESIS_HASH
    for r in rows:
        rec = {
            "advisory_id": r["advisory_id"],
            "reviewer_name": r["reviewer_name"],
            "cert_id": r["cert_id"],
            "disposition": r["disposition"],
            "note": "",
            "recorded_at": r["recorded_at"],
            "supersedes_id": None,
            "prev_hash": prev,
        }
        rec["record_hash"] = _compute_hash(rec)
        conn.execute(
            """
            INSERT INTO dispositions
                (advisory_id, reviewer_name, cert_id, disposition, note,
                 recorded_at, supersedes_id, prev_hash, record_hash)
            VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
            """,
            (rec["advisory_id"], rec["reviewer_name"], rec["cert_id"],
             rec["disposition"], rec["note"], rec["recorded_at"],
             None, rec["prev_hash"], rec["record_hash"]),
        )
        prev = rec["record_hash"]

    conn.execute("DROP TABLE dispositions_v1")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Writes — insert only
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def save_disposition(advisory_id: str, reviewer_name: str, cert_id: str,
                     disposition: str, note: str = "") -> Dict[str, object]:
    """
    Append a disposition. Never updates.

    A second decision on the same advisory becomes a new row whose
    `supersedes_id` names the row it replaces. The earlier row keeps its own
    timestamp and content and remains readable.

    Runs under BEGIN IMMEDIATE so two concurrent appends cannot both read the
    same `prev_hash` and fork the chain.
    """
    with _connect_atomic() as conn:
        prev = conn.execute(
            "SELECT record_hash FROM dispositions ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 1"
        ).fetchone()
        prev_hash = prev["record_hash"] if prev else GENESIS_HASH

        prior = conn.execute(
            "SELECT id FROM dispositions WHERE advisory_id = ? ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 1",
            (advisory_id,),
        ).fetchone()

        recorded_at = conn.execute("SELECT datetime('now') AS t").fetchone()["t"]

        rec = {
            "advisory_id": advisory_id,
            "reviewer_name": reviewer_name,
            "cert_id": cert_id,
            "disposition": disposition,
            "note": note,
            "recorded_at": recorded_at,
            "supersedes_id": prior["id"] if prior else None,
            "prev_hash": prev_hash,
        }
        rec["record_hash"] = _compute_hash(rec)

        cur = conn.execute(
            """
            INSERT INTO dispositions
                (advisory_id, reviewer_name, cert_id, disposition, note,
                 recorded_at, supersedes_id, prev_hash, record_hash)
            VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
            """,
            (rec["advisory_id"], rec["reviewer_name"], rec["cert_id"],
             rec["disposition"], rec["note"], rec["recorded_at"],
             rec["supersedes_id"], rec["prev_hash"], rec["record_hash"]),
        )
        rec["id"] = cur.lastrowid
        return dict(rec)


@contextmanager
def _connect_atomic():
    conn = sqlite3.connect(DB_PATH, isolation_level=None)
    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
    try:
        conn.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
        yield conn
        conn.execute("COMMIT")
    except Exception:
        conn.execute("ROLLBACK")
        raise
    finally:
        conn.close()


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Reads
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def get_disposition(advisory_id: str) -> Optional[Dict[str, object]]:
    """The current (latest) disposition for one advisory, or None."""
    with _connect() as conn:
        row = conn.execute(
            """
            SELECT id, advisory_id, reviewer_name, cert_id, disposition, note,
                   recorded_at, supersedes_id, prev_hash, record_hash
            FROM dispositions WHERE advisory_id = ? ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 1
            """,
            (advisory_id,),
        ).fetchone()
    return dict(row) if row else None


def disposition_history(advisory_id: str) -> List[Dict[str, object]]:
    """Every disposition ever recorded for one advisory, oldest first."""
    with _connect() as conn:
        rows = conn.execute(
            """
            SELECT id, advisory_id, reviewer_name, cert_id, disposition, note,
                   recorded_at, supersedes_id, prev_hash, record_hash
            FROM dispositions WHERE advisory_id = ? ORDER BY id ASC
            """,
            (advisory_id,),
        ).fetchall()
    return [dict(r) for r in rows]


def all_dispositions() -> Dict[str, Dict[str, object]]:
    """Current disposition per advisory — the shape callers already expect."""
    out: Dict[str, Dict[str, object]] = {}
    with _connect() as conn:
        rows = conn.execute(
            """
            SELECT id, advisory_id, reviewer_name, cert_id, disposition, note,
                   recorded_at, supersedes_id, prev_hash, record_hash
            FROM dispositions ORDER BY id ASC
            """
        ).fetchall()
    for r in rows:
        out[r["advisory_id"]] = dict(r)
    return out


def ledger_size() -> int:
    with _connect() as conn:
        return conn.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM dispositions").fetchone()["n"]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Verification
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def verify_chain() -> Dict[str, object]:
    """
    Recompute the whole chain. Returns
        {"ok": bool, "rows": n, "broken_at_id": int|None, "reason": str|None}

    Detects: a row whose content was changed (its own hash stops matching), a
    row removed from the middle (the next row's prev_hash no longer matches),
    and a chain whose links point at nothing.
    """
    with _connect() as conn:
        rows = conn.execute(
            """
            SELECT id, advisory_id, reviewer_name, cert_id, disposition, note,
                   recorded_at, supersedes_id, prev_hash, record_hash
            FROM dispositions ORDER BY id ASC
            """
        ).fetchall()

    expected_prev = GENESIS_HASH
    for r in rows:
        rec = dict(r)
        if rec["prev_hash"] != expected_prev:
            return {"ok": False, "rows": len(rows), "broken_at_id": rec["id"],
                    "reason": "prev_hash does not match the preceding row "
                              "(a row was inserted, removed or reordered)"}
        if _compute_hash(rec) != rec["record_hash"]:
            return {"ok": False, "rows": len(rows), "broken_at_id": rec["id"],
                    "reason": "record_hash does not match the row content "
                              "(the row was altered)"}
        expected_prev = rec["record_hash"]

    return {"ok": True, "rows": len(rows), "broken_at_id": None, "reason": None}

"""
SQLite-backed persistence for reviewer dispositions.

Deliberately the stdlib `sqlite3` module -- no new dependency, no server
process, one file (`axiom.db`) that lives next to the app and survives a
restart. This replaces an earlier in-memory dict: a disposition is an
audit-relevant record (who reviewed what, and what they decided), and
losing it on every restart undercuts the whole "human-in-the-loop" story.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
import sqlite3
from contextlib import contextmanager
from typing import Dict, Optional

DB_PATH = os.environ.get("AXIOM_DB_PATH", os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))), "axiom.db"))


@contextmanager
def _connect():
    conn = sqlite3.connect(DB_PATH)
    try:
        yield conn
        conn.commit()
    finally:
        conn.close()


def init_db():
    with _connect() as conn:
        conn.execute("""
            CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS dispositions (
                advisory_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
                reviewer_name TEXT NOT NULL,
                cert_id TEXT NOT NULL,
                disposition TEXT NOT NULL,
                recorded_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now'))
            )
        """)


def save_disposition(advisory_id: str, reviewer_name: str, cert_id: str, disposition: str):
    with _connect() as conn:
        conn.execute(
            """
            INSERT INTO dispositions (advisory_id, reviewer_name, cert_id, disposition, recorded_at)
            VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, datetime('now'))
            ON CONFLICT(advisory_id) DO UPDATE SET
                reviewer_name=excluded.reviewer_name,
                cert_id=excluded.cert_id,
                disposition=excluded.disposition,
                recorded_at=excluded.recorded_at
            """,
            (advisory_id, reviewer_name, cert_id, disposition),
        )


def get_disposition(advisory_id: str) -> Optional[Dict[str, str]]:
    with _connect() as conn:
        row = conn.execute(
            "SELECT reviewer_name, cert_id, disposition, recorded_at FROM dispositions WHERE advisory_id = ?",
            (advisory_id,),
        ).fetchone()
    if row is None:
        return None
    return {"reviewer_name": row[0], "cert_id": row[1], "disposition": row[2], "recorded_at": row[3]}


def all_dispositions() -> Dict[str, Dict[str, str]]:
    with _connect() as conn:
        rows = conn.execute(
            "SELECT advisory_id, reviewer_name, cert_id, disposition, recorded_at FROM dispositions"
        ).fetchall()
    return {
        r[0]: {"reviewer_name": r[1], "cert_id": r[2], "disposition": r[3], "recorded_at": r[4]}
        for r in rows
    }

"""
SQLite-backed, append-only persistence for reviewer dispositions.

Implements AD-3 (B01 §2): a disposition may be superseded but never overwritten
and never deleted. Three layers enforce that, and each one is load-bearing:

1. **No UPDATE or DELETE path in Python.** There is no function here that
   mutates a row. A correction is a new row carrying `supersedes_id`, which
   points at the row it corrects. Both rows survive.

2. **Database-level triggers.** Even someone holding the sqlite3 CLI, or a
   future contributor who adds an innocent-looking UPDATE, is stopped:
   `BEFORE UPDATE` and `BEFORE DELETE` on the ledger raise ABORT. The Python
   layer is not the guarantee; the schema is.

3. **A hash chain.** Each row carries `prev_hash` (the previous row's
   `record_hash`, or 64 zeros for the first) and `record_hash`, a SHA-256 over
   the row's own content plus `prev_hash`. Editing a row in place therefore
   breaks its own hash, and deleting one breaks the next row's `prev_hash`.
   `verify_chain()` recomputes the whole chain and reports the first row that
   fails.

What this does and does not prove — state it plainly rather than implying more:

- It **does** prove the ledger has not been altered *by anything that went
  through this database*. An attacker with write access to the file can drop the
  triggers, rewrite rows and recompute every hash; the chain is a tamper-*evident*
  control, not tamper-*proof*.
- It **does** make an accidental overwrite impossible rather than merely
  discouraged, which is what the old upsert allowed.
- It does **not** replicate off-box. A destroyed disk still destroys the
  ledger. Off-box replication and signed audit export remain separate gaps
  (D09 §4.4).

Deliberately the stdlib `sqlite3` module — no new dependency, no server
process, one file that survives a restart.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
import os
import sqlite3
from contextlib import contextmanager
from typing import Dict, List, Optional

DB_PATH = os.environ.get("AXIOM_DB_PATH", os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))), "axiom.db"))

GENESIS_HASH = "0" * 64

SCHEMA_VERSION = 2


@contextmanager
def _connect():
    conn = sqlite3.connect(DB_PATH)
    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
    try:
        yield conn
        conn.commit()
    finally:
        conn.close()


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Chain arithmetic
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def _row_payload(row: Dict[str, object]) -> str:
    """
    Canonical serialisation of the fields the hash covers.

    `sort_keys=True`, no whitespace, fixed separators — so the same row always
    hashes the same way and a verifier in another language can reproduce it
    from the documented field list. `record_hash` is excluded, obviously.
    """
    covered = {
        "advisory_id": row["advisory_id"],
        "reviewer_name": row["reviewer_name"],
        "cert_id": row["cert_id"],
        "disposition": row["disposition"],
        "note": row["note"],
        "recorded_at": row["recorded_at"],
        "supersedes_id": row["supersedes_id"],
        "prev_hash": row["prev_hash"],
    }
    return json.dumps(covered, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"))


def _compute_hash(row: Dict[str, object]) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(_row_payload(row).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Schema
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def init_db():
    """
    Create the ledger and its guard triggers, and migrate a v1 table in place.

    The v1 schema was `dispositions(advisory_id PRIMARY KEY, ...)` — one row per
    advisory, overwritten on re-decision. A v1 row held the *latest* decision
    and nothing else. Migration keeps that decision, marks it as the first link
    in the chain, and cannot invent history it never had; the timestamps of any
    prior overwrites are already gone and are not fabricated.
    """
    with _connect() as conn:
        existing = conn.execute(
            "SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table' AND name='dispositions'"
        ).fetchone()

        if existing is not None:
            cols = {r["name"] for r in conn.execute("PRAGMA table_info(dispositions)").fetchall()}
            if "record_hash" not in cols:
                _migrate_v1(conn)

        conn.execute("""
            CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS dispositions (
                id            INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
                advisory_id   TEXT NOT NULL,
                reviewer_name TEXT NOT NULL,
                cert_id       TEXT NOT NULL,
                disposition   TEXT NOT NULL,
                note          TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
                recorded_at   TEXT NOT NULL,
                supersedes_id INTEGER REFERENCES dispositions(id),
                prev_hash     TEXT NOT NULL,
                record_hash   TEXT NOT NULL
            )
        """)
        conn.execute("""
            CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_dispositions_advisory
            ON dispositions (advisory_id, id)
        """)

        # Guard triggers. `IF NOT EXISTS` so re-running init_db is harmless.
        # DROP TRIGGER is itself possible for someone with file access — see the
        # module docstring on what the chain does and does not prove.
        conn.execute("""
            CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS dispositions_no_update
            BEFORE UPDATE ON dispositions
            BEGIN
                SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'disposition ledger is append-only: UPDATE is not permitted (AD-3)');
            END
        """)
        conn.execute("""
            CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS dispositions_no_delete
            BEFORE DELETE ON dispositions
            BEGIN
                SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'disposition ledger is append-only: DELETE is not permitted (AD-3)');
            END
        """)

        conn.execute("PRAGMA user_version = %d" % SCHEMA_VERSION)


def _migrate_v1(conn):
    """Convert the v1 one-row-per-advisory table into an append-only ledger."""
    rows = conn.execute(
        "SELECT advisory_id, reviewer_name, cert_id, disposition, recorded_at "
        "FROM dispositions ORDER BY recorded_at, advisory_id"
    ).fetchall()

    conn.execute("ALTER TABLE dispositions RENAME TO dispositions_v1")

    prev = GENESIS_HASH
    for r in rows:
        rec = {
            "advisory_id": r["advisory_id"],
            "reviewer_name": r["reviewer_name"],
            "cert_id": r["cert_id"],
            "disposition": r["disposition"],
            "note": "",
            "recorded_at": r["recorded_at"],
            "supersedes_id": None,
            "prev_hash": prev,
        }
        rec["record_hash"] = _compute_hash(rec)
        conn.execute(
            """
            INSERT INTO dispositions
                (advisory_id, reviewer_name, cert_id, disposition, note,
                 recorded_at, supersedes_id, prev_hash, record_hash)
            VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
            """,
            (rec["advisory_id"], rec["reviewer_name"], rec["cert_id"],
             rec["disposition"], rec["note"], rec["recorded_at"],
             None, rec["prev_hash"], rec["record_hash"]),
        )
        prev = rec["record_hash"]

    conn.execute("DROP TABLE dispositions_v1")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Writes — insert only
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def save_disposition(advisory_id: str, reviewer_name: str, cert_id: str,
                     disposition: str, note: str = "") -> Dict[str, object]:
    """
    Append a disposition. Never updates.

    A second decision on the same advisory becomes a new row whose
    `supersedes_id` names the row it replaces. The earlier row keeps its own
    timestamp and content and remains readable.

    Runs under BEGIN IMMEDIATE so two concurrent appends cannot both read the
    same `prev_hash` and fork the chain.
    """
    with _connect_atomic() as conn:
        prev = conn.execute(
            "SELECT record_hash FROM dispositions ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 1"
        ).fetchone()
        prev_hash = prev["record_hash"] if prev else GENESIS_HASH

        prior = conn.execute(
            "SELECT id FROM dispositions WHERE advisory_id = ? ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 1",
            (advisory_id,),
        ).fetchone()

        recorded_at = conn.execute("SELECT datetime('now') AS t").fetchone()["t"]

        rec = {
            "advisory_id": advisory_id,
            "reviewer_name": reviewer_name,
            "cert_id": cert_id,
            "disposition": disposition,
            "note": note,
            "recorded_at": recorded_at,
            "supersedes_id": prior["id"] if prior else None,
            "prev_hash": prev_hash,
        }
        rec["record_hash"] = _compute_hash(rec)

        cur = conn.execute(
            """
            INSERT INTO dispositions
                (advisory_id, reviewer_name, cert_id, disposition, note,
                 recorded_at, supersedes_id, prev_hash, record_hash)
            VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
            """,
            (rec["advisory_id"], rec["reviewer_name"], rec["cert_id"],
             rec["disposition"], rec["note"], rec["recorded_at"],
             rec["supersedes_id"], rec["prev_hash"], rec["record_hash"]),
        )
        rec["id"] = cur.lastrowid
        return dict(rec)


@contextmanager
def _connect_atomic():
    conn = sqlite3.connect(DB_PATH, isolation_level=None)
    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
    try:
        conn.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
        yield conn
        conn.execute("COMMIT")
    except Exception:
        conn.execute("ROLLBACK")
        raise
    finally:
        conn.close()


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Reads
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def get_disposition(advisory_id: str) -> Optional[Dict[str, object]]:
    """The current (latest) disposition for one advisory, or None."""
    with _connect() as conn:
        row = conn.execute(
            """
            SELECT id, advisory_id, reviewer_name, cert_id, disposition, note,
                   recorded_at, supersedes_id, prev_hash, record_hash
            FROM dispositions WHERE advisory_id = ? ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 1
            """,
            (advisory_id,),
        ).fetchone()
    return dict(row) if row else None


def disposition_history(advisory_id: str) -> List[Dict[str, object]]:
    """Every disposition ever recorded for one advisory, oldest first."""
    with _connect() as conn:
        rows = conn.execute(
            """
            SELECT id, advisory_id, reviewer_name, cert_id, disposition, note,
                   recorded_at, supersedes_id, prev_hash, record_hash
            FROM dispositions WHERE advisory_id = ? ORDER BY id ASC
            """,
            (advisory_id,),
        ).fetchall()
    return [dict(r) for r in rows]


def all_dispositions() -> Dict[str, Dict[str, object]]:
    """Current disposition per advisory — the shape callers already expect."""
    out: Dict[str, Dict[str, object]] = {}
    with _connect() as conn:
        rows = conn.execute(
            """
            SELECT id, advisory_id, reviewer_name, cert_id, disposition, note,
                   recorded_at, supersedes_id, prev_hash, record_hash
            FROM dispositions ORDER BY id ASC
            """
        ).fetchall()
    for r in rows:
        out[r["advisory_id"]] = dict(r)
    return out


def ledger_size() -> int:
    with _connect() as conn:
        return conn.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM dispositions").fetchone()["n"]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Verification
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def verify_chain() -> Dict[str, object]:
    """
    Recompute the whole chain. Returns
        {"ok": bool, "rows": n, "broken_at_id": int|None, "reason": str|None}

    Detects: a row whose content was changed (its own hash stops matching), a
    row removed from the middle (the next row's prev_hash no longer matches),
    and a chain whose links point at nothing.
    """
    with _connect() as conn:
        rows = conn.execute(
            """
            SELECT id, advisory_id, reviewer_name, cert_id, disposition, note,
                   recorded_at, supersedes_id, prev_hash, record_hash
            FROM dispositions ORDER BY id ASC
            """
        ).fetchall()

    expected_prev = GENESIS_HASH
    for r in rows:
        rec = dict(r)
        if rec["prev_hash"] != expected_prev:
            return {"ok": False, "rows": len(rows), "broken_at_id": rec["id"],
                    "reason": "prev_hash does not match the preceding row "
                              "(a row was inserted, removed or reordered)"}
        if _compute_hash(rec) != rec["record_hash"]:
            return {"ok": False, "rows": len(rows), "broken_at_id": rec["id"],
                    "reason": "record_hash does not match the row content "
                              "(the row was altered)"}
        expected_prev = rec["record_hash"]

    return {"ok": True, "rows": len(rows), "broken_at_id": None, "reason": None}

"""
Tests for the append-only disposition ledger (AD-3).

These are adversarial on purpose. The claim being tested is not "save_disposition
works" but "this ledger cannot silently lose an earlier decision", so most of
these tests try to lose one and assert that the attempt fails.

Run: python3 -I tests/test_store.py
"""

import os
import sqlite3
import sys
import tempfile

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))

# Point the store at a throwaway file before importing it.
_TMPDIR = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="axiom-store-test-")
os.environ["AXIOM_DB_PATH"] = os.path.join(_TMPDIR, "test.db")

from backend import store  # noqa: E402

RESULTS = []


def test(fn):
    try:
        fn()
        RESULTS.append((fn.__name__, True, None))
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - reporting, not swallowing
        RESULTS.append((fn.__name__, False, exc))
    return fn


def fresh():
    """Empty ledger for one test."""
    if os.path.exists(store.DB_PATH):
        os.remove(store.DB_PATH)
    store.init_db()


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Baseline behaviour
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
@test
def test_first_disposition_is_recorded():
    fresh()
    rec = store.save_disposition("AD-2025-0001", "A. Reviewer", "CERT-001", "concur_dispatch")
    assert rec["id"] == 1, rec
    assert rec["supersedes_id"] is None, rec
    assert rec["prev_hash"] == store.GENESIS_HASH, rec
    assert store.ledger_size() == 1


@test
def test_current_disposition_round_trips():
    fresh()
    store.save_disposition("AD-2025-0001", "A. Reviewer", "CERT-001", "concur_dispatch")
    got = store.get_disposition("AD-2025-0001")
    assert got is not None
    assert got["disposition"] == "concur_dispatch"
    assert got["reviewer_name"] == "A. Reviewer"
    assert got["cert_id"] == "CERT-001"
    assert got["supersedes_id"] is None


@test
def test_unknown_advisory_returns_none():
    fresh()
    assert store.get_disposition("AD-9999-9999") is None


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The core property: a second decision supersedes, it does not replace
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
@test
def test_second_disposition_supersedes_rather_than_overwrites():
    fresh()
    first = store.save_disposition("AD-2025-0001", "A. Reviewer", "CERT-001",
                                   "concur_dispatch", note="Initial call")
    second = store.save_disposition("AD-2025-0001", "B. Reviewer", "CERT-002",
                                    "reject_sensor", note="Sensor flagged on inspection")

    assert store.ledger_size() == 2, "the earlier row must survive"
    assert second["id"] != first["id"], "a second decision must be a new row"
    assert second["supersedes_id"] == first["id"], second

    chain = store.disposition_history("AD-2025-0001")
    assert [r["disposition"] for r in chain] == ["concur_dispatch", "reject_sensor"]
    assert chain[0]["note"] == "Initial call"
    assert chain[1]["note"] == "Sensor flagged on inspection"


@test
def test_first_recorded_at_survives_a_later_decision():
    """The specific thing the old upsert destroyed."""
    fresh()
    first = store.save_disposition("AD-2025-0001", "A. Reviewer", "CERT-001", "concur_dispatch")
    store.save_disposition("AD-2025-0001", "B. Reviewer", "CERT-002", "escalate")

    chain = store.disposition_history("AD-2025-0001")
    assert chain[0]["recorded_at"] == first["recorded_at"]
    assert chain[0]["reviewer_name"] == "A. Reviewer"


@test
def test_current_read_returns_latest_not_first():
    fresh()
    store.save_disposition("AD-2025-0001", "A. Reviewer", "CERT-001", "concur_dispatch")
    store.save_disposition("AD-2025-0001", "B. Reviewer", "CERT-002", "escalate")
    cur = store.get_disposition("AD-2025-0001")
    assert cur["disposition"] == "escalate"
    assert cur["reviewer_name"] == "B. Reviewer"


@test
def test_third_decision_chains_to_the_second():
    fresh()
    a = store.save_disposition("AD-2025-0001", "A", "C1", "concur_dispatch")
    b = store.save_disposition("AD-2025-0001", "B", "C2", "escalate")
    c = store.save_disposition("AD-2025-0001", "C", "C3", "override_downgrade")
    assert c["supersedes_id"] == b["id"]
    assert b["supersedes_id"] == a["id"]
    assert store.ledger_size() == 3


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The schema refuses mutation, whoever is asking
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
@test
def test_update_is_refused_by_the_database():
    fresh()
    store.save_disposition("AD-2025-0001", "A. Reviewer", "CERT-001", "concur_dispatch")

    conn = sqlite3.connect(store.DB_PATH)
    try:
        try:
            conn.execute("UPDATE dispositions SET disposition='escalate' WHERE id=1")
            raise AssertionError("UPDATE was allowed — the append-only guard is missing")
        except sqlite3.DatabaseError as exc:
            assert "append-only" in str(exc).lower(), exc
    finally:
        conn.close()

    assert store.get_disposition("AD-2025-0001")["disposition"] == "concur_dispatch"


@test
def test_delete_is_refused_by_the_database():
    fresh()
    store.save_disposition("AD-2025-0001", "A. Reviewer", "CERT-001", "concur_dispatch")

    conn = sqlite3.connect(store.DB_PATH)
    try:
        try:
            conn.execute("DELETE FROM dispositions WHERE id=1")
            raise AssertionError("DELETE was allowed — the append-only guard is missing")
        except sqlite3.DatabaseError as exc:
            assert "append-only" in str(exc).lower(), exc
    finally:
        conn.close()

    assert store.ledger_size() == 1


@test
def test_triggers_survive_reopening_the_database():
    """init_db on an existing ledger must not drop the guards."""
    fresh()
    store.save_disposition("AD-2025-0001", "A", "C1", "concur_dispatch")
    store.init_db()  # second call, as happens on every process start

    conn = sqlite3.connect(store.DB_PATH)
    try:
        try:
            conn.execute("DELETE FROM dispositions")
            raise AssertionError("guards were lost on re-init")
        except sqlite3.DatabaseError:
            pass
    finally:
        conn.close()


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The hash chain
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
@test
def test_chain_verifies_when_untouched():
    fresh()
    store.save_disposition("AD-2025-0001", "A", "C1", "concur_dispatch")
    store.save_disposition("AD-2025-0002", "B", "C2", "escalate")
    store.save_disposition("AD-2025-0001", "C", "C3", "reject_sensor")

    result = store.verify_chain()
    assert result["ok"] is True, result
    assert result["rows"] == 3


@test
def test_chain_links_each_row_to_the_previous():
    fresh()
    a = store.save_disposition("AD-1", "A", "C1", "concur_dispatch")
    b = store.save_disposition("AD-2", "B", "C2", "escalate")
    assert a["prev_hash"] == store.GENESIS_HASH
    assert b["prev_hash"] == a["record_hash"]


@test
def test_tampered_row_is_detected():
    """The triggers stop UPDATE through the engine; this tests detection of a
    row changed by something that bypassed them, which is the real threat."""
    fresh()
    store.save_disposition("AD-1", "A", "C1", "concur_dispatch")
    store.save_disposition("AD-2", "B", "C2", "escalate")

    conn = sqlite3.connect(store.DB_PATH)
    try:
        conn.execute("DROP TRIGGER dispositions_no_update")
        conn.execute("UPDATE dispositions SET reviewer_name='Mallory' WHERE id=2")
        conn.commit()
    finally:
        conn.close()

    result = store.verify_chain()
    assert result["ok"] is False, result
    assert result["broken_at_id"] == 2
    assert "altered" in result["reason"]


@test
def test_removed_row_is_detected():
    fresh()
    store.save_disposition("AD-1", "A", "C1", "concur_dispatch")
    store.save_disposition("AD-2", "B", "C2", "escalate")
    store.save_disposition("AD-3", "C", "C3", "reject_sensor")

    conn = sqlite3.connect(store.DB_PATH)
    try:
        conn.execute("DROP TRIGGER dispositions_no_delete")
        conn.execute("DELETE FROM dispositions WHERE id=2")
        conn.commit()
    finally:
        conn.close()

    result = store.verify_chain()
    assert result["ok"] is False, result
    assert result["broken_at_id"] == 3
    assert "prev_hash" in result["reason"]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Migration from the v1 one-row-per-advisory schema
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
@test
def test_v1_table_migrates_without_losing_the_existing_decision():
    if os.path.exists(store.DB_PATH):
        os.remove(store.DB_PATH)

    # Recreate the v1 schema exactly as it shipped.
    conn = sqlite3.connect(store.DB_PATH)
    conn.execute("""
        CREATE TABLE dispositions (
            advisory_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
            reviewer_name TEXT NOT NULL,
            cert_id TEXT NOT NULL,
            disposition TEXT NOT NULL,
            recorded_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now'))
        )
    """)
    conn.execute(
        "INSERT INTO dispositions VALUES ('AD-2025-0007','Legacy Reviewer','CERT-9','escalate','2026-11-01 10:00:00')"
    )
    conn.commit()
    conn.close()

    store.init_db()

    got = store.get_disposition("AD-2025-0007")
    assert got is not None, "migration lost the row"
    assert got["disposition"] == "escalate"
    assert got["reviewer_name"] == "Legacy Reviewer"
    assert got["recorded_at"] == "2026-11-01 10:00:00", "timestamp must not be rewritten"
    assert got["supersedes_id"] is None
    assert got["prev_hash"] == store.GENESIS_HASH
    assert store.verify_chain()["ok"] is True

# a demo, not a system of record). Keyed by advisory_id. This is what
# makes "REVIEW" / "URGENT REVIEW" an actual workflow step a named,

# story this product depends on.

VALID_DISPOSITIONS = {
    "concur_dispatch": "Concurred — dispatch order issued",
    "escalate": "Escalated to engineering/leadership",
    "override_downgrade": "Reviewer override — downgraded on field experience",
    "reject_sensor": "Rejected — suspected sensor/hardware fault, S&C dispatched",
}


def _apply_disposition(warrant):
    rec = store.get_disposition(warrant.advisory_id)
    if rec:
        warrant.reviewer_disposition = (
            f"{VALID_DISPOSITIONS.get(rec['disposition'], rec['disposition'])} "
            f"— {rec['reviewer_name']} ({rec['cert_id']})"

# A disposition is never overwritten: a second decision on the same advisory is
# appended as a new row carrying `supersedes_id`, and the earlier row keeps its
# own content and timestamp. SQLite triggers refuse UPDATE and DELETE outright,
# and every row is chained by SHA-256 to the one before it, so a row edited or
# removed outside the app is detectable via store.verify_chain().
#
# This is what makes "REVIEW" / "URGENT REVIEW" an actual workflow step a named,
# credentialed person acts on, rather than a status string nothing ever writes
# back to -- the core of the "human-in-the-loop, AI never dispatches" story, and
# the record F09 produces.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
VALID_DISPOSITIONS = {
    "concur_dispatch": "Concurred — dispatch order issued",
    "escalate": "Escalated to engineering/leadership",
    "override_downgrade": "Reviewer override — downgraded on field experience",
    "reject_sensor": "Rejected — suspected sensor/hardware fault, S&C dispatched",
}


def _disposition_label(rec):
    """'Label — Name (CERT)' plus a superseded-count marker when there is one."""
    label = (
        f"{VALID_DISPOSITIONS.get(rec['disposition'], rec['disposition'])} "
        f"— {rec['reviewer_name']} ({rec['cert_id']})"
    )
    history = store.disposition_history(rec["advisory_id"])
    if len(history) > 1:
        label += f" · supersedes {len(history) - 1} earlier record{'s' if len(history) > 2 else ''}"
    return label, len(history)


def _apply_disposition(warrant):
    rec = store.get_disposition(warrant.advisory_id)
    if rec:
        warrant.reviewer_disposition, warrant.disposition_history_count = _disposition_label(rec)
    return warrant

"""
Predictive Ghost Warrant construction.

A "Ghost Warrant" is this product's name for a single traceable evidence
packet: one axle, one point in time, every signal that fired on it, a
severity tier, and a cryptographic hash binding the record so it can't be
quietly edited after the fact. This is the audit/evidence-trail layer that
turns "the dashboard said critical" into something a railroad's safety and
legal team can actually stand behind.

Two design choices worth calling out explicitly:

1. Severity tiers are named INFORMATIONAL / REVIEW / URGENT REVIEW, not
   "watch/warning/critical" -- the point of the rename is to make it
   impossible to mistake these for operational alarm levels. See the
   CRITICAL SAFETY GUARDRAIL note below and in the README: this system
   never issues a stop-train or braking instruction. It produces evidence
   for a human to review. Existing railroad operating rules, detector
   logic, and authorized personnel remain the sole authority over any
   train-movement decision.

2. Escalation to URGENT REVIEW requires CORROBORATION: at least two
   independent signal types (e.g. thermal rate-of-change AND a peer-group
   outlier, or thermal AND acoustic) must agree. A single signal, even one
   that is itself severe, is capped at REVIEW. This directly implements
   the infographic's "acoustic detection requires corroboration before
   fracture classification" rule, generalized across all signal types, so
   one noisy sensor can't single-handedly manufacture a false urgent case.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
from dataclasses import dataclass, asdict
from typing import Dict, List, Optional

# Internal physics-module severities ("watch"/"warning"/"critical") map
# onto a 0..3 ordinal so independent signals can be compared and combined.
_SEVERITY_ORDINAL = {None: 0, "normal": 0, "watch": 1, "warning": 2, "critical": 3}

TIER_INFORMATIONAL = "INFORMATIONAL"
TIER_REVIEW = "REVIEW"
TIER_URGENT_REVIEW = "URGENT REVIEW"

RECOMMENDED_RESPONSE = {
    TIER_INFORMATIONAL: "Record in audit ledger. No operational action required.",
    TIER_REVIEW: "Authorized analyst examination and prioritization.",
    TIER_URGENT_REVIEW: "Escalate to authorized railroad personnel per carrier-approved procedures.",
}


@dataclass
class SignalEvidence:
    """One independent signal's reading on this axle at this pass."""
    signal_type: str          # "thermal_rate_of_change" | "ambient_relative_legacy" | "peer_historical" | "peer_cross_fleet" | "acoustic_bearing_defect"
    severity: str             # "normal" | "watch" | "warning" | "critical"
    detail: str
    confidence_note: str = ""


@dataclass
class GhostWarrant:
    advisory_id: str
    asset_id: str
    train_consist: str
    detector_location: str
    component_position: str
    timestamp_s: float
    severity_tier: str
    corroborated: bool
    evidence: List[SignalEvidence]
    reference_population_version: str
    model_version: str
    confidence: str
    recommended_response: str
    reviewer_disposition: str
    ground_truth_status: str
    cryptographic_hash: str


REFERENCE_POPULATION_VERSION = "v1.4.2"   # stands in for a real versioned baseline dataset
MODEL_VERSION = "0.97"                     # stands in for a real model/ruleset version


def _severity_to_tier(worst_ordinal: int, corroborated: bool) -> str:
    if worst_ordinal <= 0:
        return TIER_INFORMATIONAL
    if worst_ordinal >= 3 and corroborated:
        return TIER_URGENT_REVIEW
    if worst_ordinal >= 2 and corroborated:
        return TIER_URGENT_REVIEW
    # Severe-but-uncorroborated, or merely moderate: held at REVIEW, not
    # escalated further, until a second independent signal agrees.
    return TIER_REVIEW


def build_warrant(
    advisory_seq: int,
    asset_id: str,
    train_consist: str,
    detector_location: str,
    component_position: str,
    timestamp_s: float,
    evidence: List[SignalEvidence],
    confidence: Optional[str] = None,
    reviewer_disposition: str = "Pending",
    ground_truth_status: str = "Not available",
) -> Optional[GhostWarrant]:
    """
    Fuses a set of independent signal readings for one axle/pass into a
    single Ghost Warrant. Returns None if every signal is normal (no
    warrant is generated for a clean reading -- nothing to review).
    """
    flagged = [e for e in evidence if _SEVERITY_ORDINAL.get(e.severity, 0) > 0]
    if not flagged:
        return None

    worst_ordinal = max(_SEVERITY_ORDINAL.get(e.severity, 0) for e in evidence)
    distinct_signal_types_flagged = {e.signal_type for e in flagged}
    corroborated = len(distinct_signal_types_flagged) >= 2

    tier = _severity_to_tier(worst_ordinal, corroborated)

    if confidence is None:
        confidence = "High" if corroborated else "Moderate (single signal, uncorroborated)"

    advisory_id = f"AD-{2025}-{advisory_seq:04d}"

    canonical = json.dumps({
        "advisory_id": advisory_id,
        "asset_id": asset_id,
        "timestamp_s": timestamp_s,
        "evidence": [asdict(e) for e in evidence],
        "model_version": MODEL_VERSION,
        "reference_population_version": REFERENCE_POPULATION_VERSION,
    }, sort_keys=True)
    crypto_hash = hashlib.sha256(canonical.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()

    return GhostWarrant(
        advisory_id=advisory_id,
        asset_id=asset_id,
        train_consist=train_consist,
        detector_location=detector_location,
        component_position=component_position,
        timestamp_s=timestamp_s,
        severity_tier=tier,
        corroborated=corroborated,
        evidence=evidence,
        reference_population_version=REFERENCE_POPULATION_VERSION,
        model_version=MODEL_VERSION,
        confidence=confidence,
        recommended_response=RECOMMENDED_RESPONSE[tier],
        reviewer_disposition=reviewer_disposition,
        ground_truth_status=ground_truth_status,
        cryptographic_hash=crypto_hash,
    )

        if rel_path in ("", "/"):
            rel_path = "index.html"

        if not full_path.startswith(FRONTEND_DIR) or not os.path.isfile(full_path):

        ext = os.path.splitext(full_path)[1]

        with open(full_path, "rb") as f:
            body = f.read()
        self.send_response(200)
        self.send_header("Content-Type", mime)
        self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body)))
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(body)

        parsed = urlparse(self.path)
        path = parsed.path
        query = {k: v[0] for k, v in parse_qs(parsed.query).items()}

content.description: Compare the independently computed value to the figure as written in A2/D08. Correct every mismatch in the repo, citing the source equation in the pass record.

content.description: Write the arithmetic pass record to assets/, re-check cross-document figure consistency (A1 ROI model, D02, D05, F05 reference the same rates), then commit in the same pass. Note push requirement.

content.subject: Read the entire AxiomDynamics folder
content.description: Read all 37 docket documents, 9 internal assets, backend/frontend/tests, and the full project-logs and chat-2 transcript so the summary is built from what the files say rather than from memory.

content.subject: Reconstruct the stage-by-stage build chronology
content.description: Reconstruct each stage of the build in order from git history, the docket's own status records, and the transcripts. Identify what was built when, what was decided, what was lost, and what was rebuilt.

content.subject: Write the comprehensive build summary as a .docx
content.description: Author a comprehensive, granular, stage-by-stage working summary as a .docx saved into the AxiomDynamics repo. Cover every document, every model, every decision, every open item, and the loss/reconstruction history.

content.subject: Render, verify and commit the document
content.description: Render the .docx to PDF, view the pages, check for layout problems, and verify every factual claim in it traces to a file. Confirm it lands in the repo and commit it.

content.subject: Rebuild disposition ledger as append-only (AD-3)
content.description: Replace the upsert write path with an insert-only ledger: new schema (id, advisory_id, reviewer, cert, disposition, recorded_at, supersedes_id, note, prev_hash, record_hash), SQLite triggers that ABORT on UPDATE/DELETE, a per-row SHA-256 chain, supersede-not-overwrite corrections, and a migration that carries existing rows forward without loss. Rework main.py to read current vs history.

content.subject: Test append-only semantics and hash chain
content.description: Prove the properties rather than assert them: an UPDATE raises, a DELETE raises, a second disposition supersedes rather than replaces, the first row survives with its timestamp intact, the hash chain verifies, a tampered row fails verification, and migration from the old single-column schema loses nothing.

content.subject: Close the append-only gap across the docket
content.description: Close gap #2 in every document that discloses it — B01 §7, D09 §4.4 and the audit-logging row, D00 Part VI, F09 Part 7 — and state precisely what is now true and what still is not (no off-box replication, no signed export yet). Verify each claim against the running code before writing it.
