# AxiomDynamics — Physics-First Predictive Maintenance (Demo)

A small web app for freight-rail predictive maintenance built on named
physical models instead of black-box ML or fixed alarm thresholds:

1. **Thermodynamics** — wheel-bearing temperature rate-of-change, flagged
   with a rolling z-score against each axle's own recent baseline, instead
   of a fixed absolute alarm. Also computes the legacy check correctly:
   real hot-bearing detectors alarm on temperature **above ambient**, not
   a flat number (see "East Palestine" note below).
2. **Peer comparison** — a robust median/MAD z-score against (a) this
   axle's own detector-pass history and (b) every other axle in the fleet
   right now, so a reading is judged against what's normal for it and for
   its peers, not in isolation.
3. **Kinematics** — coasting distance/energy from `E_k = 1/2 m v^2` plus
   grade and resistance terms, integrated numerically, to predict whether
   a car will stop or run away on a given grade.
4. **Acoustics** — FFT vibration analysis against the standard
   rolling-element bearing defect-frequency equations (BPFO, BPFI, BSF,
   FTF), to flag a specific defect frequency standing out above the noise
   floor, rather than a generic "weird sound" classifier.
5. **Same-axle left/right differential** — standard hot-bearing practice
   alongside the ambient-relative check: the two journals on one axle
   share load path and speed, so a large gap between them (independent of
   either journal's absolute level) points at a one-sided defect.
6. **Executive ROI panel** (`backend/roi.py`, `GET /api/roi`) — fleet
   mission-ready %, net estimated benefit, mean-time-to-detect vs. legacy,
   and open review counts, shown as a KPI strip at the top of the
   dashboard, built on real cited derailment cost data (see "ROI research"
   below) blended with clearly-labeled modeling assumptions where no
   public figure exists.

On top of those, two mechanisms:

7. **Evidence fusion → Predictive Ghost Warrants** — no single signal can
   trigger the top severity tier by itself. `backend/warrants.py` only
   escalates to **URGENT REVIEW** when at least two independent signal
   types agree; a lone signal (even a critical one) is capped at
   **REVIEW**. Every warrant carries a SHA-256 hash of its evidence, and
   severity tiers are named INFORMATIONAL / REVIEW / URGENT REVIEW
   specifically so they can't be mistaken for an operational alarm level —
   this system never issues a stop-train or braking instruction.
8. **Human reviewer disposition** — each Ghost Warrant has a real
   disposition workflow (`POST /api/warrant/{advisory_id}/disposition`):
   a named reviewer with a certification ID records Concur & Dispatch,
   Escalate, Override/Downgrade, or Reject Sensor Hardware, with an
   optional note. This is not decorative — it's what makes "a human is in
   the loop" an actual recorded action instead of a claim in a README.

   The ledger is **append-only**. A second decision on the same advisory
   does not overwrite the first: it is inserted as a new record whose
   `supersedes_id` points at the record it corrects, and both survive
   with their own timestamps. `UPDATE` and `DELETE` are refused by
   database triggers, and every record carries a SHA-256 over its content
   and its predecessor's hash, so `store.verify_chain()` can prove the
   history is intact and name the first record that is not. This is a
   deliberate constraint, not an accident of implementation: the whole
   regulatory argument rests on a record that cannot be quietly rewritten.
   Read `backend/store.py`'s module docstring for exactly what the chain
   does and does not prove.

Every number in the dashboard traces back to an equation in
`backend/physics.py` — read that file's docstrings for the exact formulas
and their sources. Nothing here is a trained model or a mystery black box.

## Why this design, not just "AI predicts failures"

This isn't arbitrary. [NTSB testimony on the Feb 3, 2023 East Palestine,
OH derailment](https://www.ntsb.gov/investigations/Documents/East%20Palestine%20Ohio%20Board%20Meeting%20Summary%20with%20Amendments.pdf)
found the failed bearing read 253°F above a 10°F ambient at the final
detector before critical alarm — by then it was in its final stage of
mechanical failure. [FRA Safety Advisory 2023-01](https://railroads.dot.gov/sites/fra.dot.gov/files/2023-02/(Safety%20Advisory%202023-01%20%20Posting%20on-line%20022823).pdf)
and its supplements, issued because of that derailment, call out the
specific gaps this design targets: single-point checks with no trend
history, inconsistent thresholds across detectors, and no standard
practice for comparing a reading against a bearing's own history or its
peers. The demo fleet includes a unit (U3) deliberately modeled on that
night's cold-ambient conditions, specifically to show the gap between a
legacy point-in-time check and a trend/peer-aware one on the same data.

## Why no FastAPI / Chart.js / npm install

This was deliberately built on nothing but the Python standard library
(`http.server`) plus `numpy` for FFT/array math, and plain Canvas/JS on the
frontend with zero CDN dependencies. That's not a style preference — it's
the actual deployment story for an air-gapped wayside/dispatch environment,
where IT will not approve installing a dependency tree on a live network.
Run it with:

```bash
pip install numpy   # only dependency; skip if numpy is already present (sqlite3 is in the Python stdlib)
cd axiomdynamics-app
python3 -m backend.main
```

Then open **http://127.0.0.1:8420/** in a browser. Click any row in the
Fleet table to see that axle's thermodynamics, acoustics, and kinematics
detail charts.

## What's real and what's simulated

There is no freely downloadable, public, real-time rail wayside sensor
dataset (the datasets that exist, like CWRU's bearing set, are generic
motor-test-rig data behind a university host, not rail axle data — and
this build environment had no outbound internet access to fetch anything
anyway). So `backend/simulate.py` generates synthetic sensor traces **from
the same physics equations in `physics.py`**, with documented fault
conditions injected (a bearing-wear friction ramp for the thermal fault, an
injected BPFO-frequency harmonic for the acoustic fault). Every constant
used (bearing geometry, thermal mass, radial load, etc.) is called out in
that file as "representative," not pulled from a specific OEM spec.

To point this at real sensor data later, replace the three `generate_*`
functions in `simulate.py` with loaders that return the same shapes
(`times, temps_f` / `t, signal, defect_freqs, shaft_hz`) — `physics.py` and
`main.py` don't care where the samples came from.

## ROI research: real bearing-failure derailment costs

The ROI panel's cost figures come from two real, cited cost tiers rather
than an invented "average cost per derailment" (no such standardized
public figure exists — FRA tracks accident counts and causes, not a
normalized dollar average).

**Tier 1 — contained bearing/wheelset failure, no hazmat release:**
a BNSF bearing-related derailment with $5,000,000 in reported damage
([NTSB](https://www.ntsb.gov/investigations/accidentreports/reports/rab1712.pdf)),
and a separate BNSF derailment with $13,500,000 in reported damage,
explicitly excluding lading and environmental remediation costs
([NTSB docket](https://data.ntsb.gov/Docket/Document/docBLOB?FileExtension=.PDF&FileName=BNSF%20Equipment%20Incident%20Report-Redacted.PDF&ID=40457595)).
These two figures bracket the $5.0M–$13.5M range used as the "contained"
tier.

**Tier 2 — catastrophic failure with hazmat release:** the Feb 3, 2023
East Palestine, OH derailment (Norfolk Southern, not BNSF, but the same
wheel-bearing failure mode this product targets) cost over $310 million
in a federal EPA/DOJ settlement
([DOJ](https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/united-states-reaches-over-310-million-settlement-norfolk-southern-address-harms-caused-east)),
a separate $600 million personal-injury class settlement paid fully by
Norfolk Southern
([AP](https://apnews.com/article/east-palestine-derailment-norfolk-southern-gatx-oxyvinyls-2d5110bf096ec3524f3092999bee3060)),
and a cumulative cost reported to have exceeded $1 billion by mid-2024
([KTEN](https://www.kten.com/story/49275631/east-palestine-train-derailment-has-now-cost-norfolk-southern-1-billion)).

**What's an assumption, not a citation:** there is no published base rate
for what fraction of missed bearing defects progress to a catastrophic
event versus stay contained. `backend/roi.py` uses 2% and the A1 Excel
model uses 0.05% (`P_CATASTROPHIC_GIVEN_MISSED_DEFECT` in the code;
sheet 1 cell B17 in the workbook), and that 40× disagreement is an open
item — it is the reason the workbook and the licensing annex do not
produce the same benefit figures. Do not quote either number without
reading `assets/a2-d08-arithmetic-pass-2026-11-09.md` first. Both blend
the two sourced tiers into one expected-cost figure. The inspection-cost
and detection-time constants are also unsourced placeholders. Replace
them with your own numbers, or a pilot customer's real safety/cost data,
before this supports an actual business case.

## One important caveat on the kinematics module

The coasting model assumes **no brake or throttle input at all** for as
long as you let it run. On a steep enough descending grade it will show
the car accelerating toward a terminal velocity that a real train would
never actually reach, because crews brake well before that. Read a
"will accelerate on this grade" result as *"this axle needs braking input
to control speed here,"* not as a forecast of what a train will actually
do — it's a decision-support signal, not a crystal ball.

## Project layout

```
backend/
  physics.py    the three physics modules (thermo / kinematics / acoustics)
  simulate.py   synthetic fleet + sensor trace generator
  main.py       stdlib HTTP server, routes, static file serving
frontend/
  index.html, style.css, app.js   dashboard UI, vanilla JS canvas charts
tests/
  test_physics.py   correctness tests for every formula
  test_store.py     append-only and hash-chain tests for the ledger
  run_tests.py      stdlib-only test runner; discovers test_*.py
```

## Running the tests

```bash
python3 tests/run_tests.py     # no pytest needed; discovers every test_*.py
# or, if you have pytest:
pytest tests/
```

38 tests currently: 21 for the physics formulas, 17 for the disposition
ledger. The ledger tests are adversarial by design — each one tries to destroy
an earlier decision and asserts that the attempt fails or is detected.

## API routes

- `GET /api/fleet` — summary status for every axle
- `GET /api/alerts` — combined predictive alerts, most severe first
- `GET /api/unit/{id}/thermo` — temperature series + z-score sweep + alerts
- `GET /api/unit/{id}/acoustics` — FFT spectrum + defect frequency matches
- `GET /api/unit/{id}/kinematics` — coasting profile for that axle's car
- `GET /api/roi` — fleet-wide executive KPI summary (mission-ready %, net
  estimated benefit, mean-time-to-detect, open reviews)
- `POST /api/warrant/{advisory_id}/disposition` — append a reviewer's
  disposition (`{"reviewer_name", "cert_id", "disposition", "note"?}`,
  where disposition is one of `concur_dispatch`, `escalate`,
  `override_downgrade`, `reject_sensor`). Returns the new `record_id`,
  the `supersedes_id` it corrects (or null), and the record's hash.
  Persisted in `axiom.db` (SQLite, stdlib `sqlite3`, survives a restart).
- `GET /api/warrant/{advisory_id}/disposition` — the full decision trail
  for one advisory, oldest first, with `chain_ok` reporting whether the
  hash chain verifies.
- `GET /api/ledger/verify` — recompute the whole disposition chain and
  report `{ok, rows, broken_at_id, reason}`.

## Deploying to Render (free tier)

This gets you a real `https://your-app-name.onrender.com` URL anyone can
open without installing anything. Render needs your code in a git repo it
can pull from (GitHub, GitLab, or Bitbucket) — if this folder isn't a git
repo yet:

```bash

git init
git add .
git commit -m "Initial commit"
```

Then push it to a new GitHub repo (create one at github.com/new, then
follow the push instructions it gives you).

**Option A — Blueprint (uses the included `render.yaml`):**
1. Go to [render.com](https://render.com) and sign up / log in.
2. Dashboard → **New** → **Blueprint**.
3. Connect your GitHub account and select this repo.
4. Render reads `render.yaml` and fills everything in automatically —
   review and click **Apply**.

**Option B — Manual web service (if you skip the Blueprint):**
1. Dashboard → **New** → **Web Service** → connect this repo.
2. Runtime: **Python 3**.
3. Build command: `pip install -r requirements.txt`
4. Start command: `python -m backend.main`
5. Add an environment variable: `AXIOM_HOST` = `0.0.0.0`
6. Instance type: **Free**.
7. Click **Create Web Service**.

public URL (first load on the free tier can take ~30-60s if the instance
had spun down from inactivity — that's normal, not a bug).

tier.** Free-tier instances have an ephemeral filesystem: it spins down
after inactivity and loses any local file changes, including `axiom.db`.
Dispositions you record will survive until the instance sleeps, then
reset. Note that this is a *durability* limit, not an append-only one: the
schema still refuses in-place edits while it exists, but losing the file
loses the whole ledger. For a real pilot, upgrade to a paid Render plan
with a persistent disk, or point `AXIOM_DB_PATH` at a managed database —
and replicate off-box, because a single copy is a single point of loss
(D09 §4.4).

## Running it in Docker (air-gapped edge box story)

```bash
docker build -t axiomdynamics-demo .
docker run --rm -p 8420:8420 axiomdynamics-demo
```

Then open `http://127.0.0.1:8420/` same as the non-Docker run. The image is
`python:3.11-slim` + numpy only, runs as a non-root user, and has a basic
`HEALTHCHECK` hitting `/api/fleet`.

over on the encrypted USB, then `docker load -i axiomdynamics-demo.tar` on
the offline edge server and `docker run` as above. No pip, no npm, no
outbound connection needed on the edge box itself.

was no way to actually pull `python:3.11-slim` and run `docker build` to
verify it. The Dockerfile is straightforward and should work as-is, but
please run the build yourself and let me know if anything needs fixing.

  demonstrates the method rather than a customer's data.
- Sign the disposition export and replicate it off-box, so the ledger can
  be proven intact without trusting the host that holds it (D09 §4.4).
- Add authentication if this ever leaves a single trusted machine — and
  the signed certification registry (AD-2) behind it, which is what turns
  a recorded reviewer name into a verified identity.

# B01 — System Blueprint & Architecture

**Docket position:** B01. Descriptive annex to D07. B-series documents create no warranty unless D07 expressly incorporates them (Docket Index, Part IV, rule 5).

**Written against:** the production architecture, not the demonstration build. §7 lists every point where the two currently differ. Nothing in this document should be treated as describing the demo.

**Governing architectural decisions:**

- **AD-1 — Deployment: fully on-premise edge, zero outbound network.** No licence server, no telemetry, no update callback, no third-party cloud. The platform never initiates a network connection to anything outside the Railroad's network. Ever.
- **AD-2 — Reviewer identity: local accounts plus a signed certification registry**, administered by the Railroad. No dependency on Railroad directory services, no cloud identity provider.
- **AD-3 — The disposition ledger is append-only.** A disposition can be superseded but never overwritten, and never deleted.

AD-1 and AD-2 were chosen specifically so the platform remains deployable on an air-gapped network. Both have costs, stated in §8.

---

## 1. Purpose and boundary

The platform ingests wayside sensor signals from the Railroad's existing detector infrastructure, applies deterministic physics models to derive bearing and running-gear condition, and presents ranked advisory warrants to a certified reviewer who records a disposition.

**The platform does not decide anything.** It does not issue stop orders, does not communicate with train crews, does not influence signal systems, and does not actuate any equipment. It produces advisories for a qualified human being, who retains sole operating authority. This framing is deliberate and must be identical in B01, C02, D02, D07, D08 and D12. See D00 §III.1.

**In scope:** sensor ingestion, physics inference, warrant generation and ranking, reviewer disposition recording, audit export, ROI reporting.

**Out of scope:** detector hardware, network infrastructure, train control, crew communication, regulatory reporting to FRA/TC/ARTF on the Railroad's behalf.

## 2. Component inventory

| Component | Function | Technology |
|---|---|---|
| Signal ingest | Accepts wayside detector payloads in a defined schema | Python, file/socket ingest |
| Physics engine | Thermo, kinematic, acoustic models; deterministic, no learned parameters | Python + numpy |
| Warrant builder | Converts model output into ranked, cited advisories | Python |
| Identity & certification | **Local accounts, admin-issued credentials — operational today.** Signed certification registry: **designed, not built** (§7 item 1) | Python + SQLite |
| Disposition ledger | Record of reviewer decisions. **Append-only — built 2026-11-09** (§4.1, §4.6, §7 item 2) | SQLite, WAL mode; insert-only with guard triggers and SHA-256 chain |
| API layer | Read APIs for fleet/alerts/ROI; write API for disposition | Python stdlib HTTP server |
| Presentation | Single-page dashboard, no external assets | HTML/CSS/JS, served locally |
| Audit export | Timestamped export with content hashes. **Not cryptographically signed** (§7 item 8) | Python |

**Total external dependency count: one** (numpy). Everything else is Python standard library. This is an architectural property, not an accident, and it is the platform's principal security argument — see B04.

## 3. Data flow

```
Wayside detector (HBD / WILD / ABD)
        │  sensor payload
        ▼
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  RAILROAD EDGE BOX  —  no outbound network   │
│                                              │
│  ingest ──► physics engine ──► warrant       │
│              (deterministic)     builder     │
│                                    │         │
│                                    ▼         │
│                            reviewer queue    │
│                                    │         │
│                        [certified human]     │
│                                    │         │
│                                    ▼         │
│                        disposition ledger    │
│                         (append-only, WAL)   │
│                                    │         │
│                                    ▼         │
│                          audit export        │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────┘
        │
        ▼
Railroad's own reporting / regulatory process
```

**There is no line leaving the box.** That is AD-1 stated as a diagram.

## 4. The disposition ledger

The single most important component, because it is the artifact our regulatory argument rests on.

**Requirements (production):**

1. **Append-only.** Each disposition is a new row. Supersede-and-insert, never `UPDATE`. **Built 2026-11-09:** the write path is insert-only, a correction carries a `supersedes_id` referencing the row it corrects, and database triggers `RAISE(ABORT)` on any `UPDATE` or `DELETE` against the table — so the guarantee is in the schema, not only in the application. Both the superseded and the superseding record survive with their own timestamps.
2. **Authenticated identity.** A disposition is only accepted from an authenticated session bound to an issued, unexpired, unrevoked certification record. Free-text name and cert ID are not acceptable in production. *Not built — AD-2, §7 item 1.*
3. **Immutable timestamps**, server-generated, not client-supplied. **Built:** `recorded_at` is written by the database at insert time and is covered by the row hash, so altering it breaks the chain.
4. **Retention** per the Railroad's records policy, specified in D09.
5. **Export** produces a signed bundle: partition boundary, record count, and a hash over the contents, so a regulator can verify nothing was removed. *Partly built:* the chain can be re-verified on demand and the result reported, but the exported bundle is not yet **signed**. See §7 item 6.
6. **Hash chaining.** Each record carries the hash of its predecessor, making retroactive alteration detectable. **Built 2026-11-09:** every row stores `prev_hash` (the previous row's hash, or 64 zeros for the first) and `record_hash`, a SHA-256 over its own content plus `prev_hash`. `store.verify_chain()` recomputes the whole chain and names the first row that fails.

**What the chain does and does not prove.** It detects a row edited in place (its own hash stops matching) and a row removed from the middle (the next row's `prev_hash` stops matching). It does **not** stop an attacker who has write access to the database file: such a party can drop the triggers, rewrite rows and recompute every hash. The chain is tamper-**evident**, not tamper-**proof**, and the difference is the reason off-box replication and signed export still matter (§7 items 6–7).

**Why this matters commercially:** the Canadian pitch rests on producing auditable evidence that a flagged bearing was reviewed and acted upon. A ledger that can be silently rewritten produces no such evidence. With §4.1, §4.3 and §4.6 now built, the ledger supports that claim at the level of *"the record cannot be silently altered by the application or by ordinary database access"* — it does not yet support *"the record is cryptographically signed and replicated off-box."* Do not overstate the second. The certification story in C02 still depends on §4.2.

## 5. Failure modes

| Failure | Behavior | Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| Detector feed stops | Platform flags data staleness; advisories marked stale | No false reassurance — staleness is surfaced, not hidden |
| Physics engine error | Request fails, logged; no advisory emitted | Fails closed on that unit, not silently degraded |
| Edge box loses power | SQLite WAL recovers committed dispositions | Committed audit records survive |
| Disk full | Ingest rejects; dashboard alarms | Fails visibly |
| Clock drift | Timestamps become unreliable | **Requires NTP against Railroad's own time source — see §7** |
| Cert registry unavailable | New dispositions rejected | Fails closed — no unauthenticated decisions |

**Fails closed everywhere.** Where the choice exists, the platform refuses to act rather than acting unverified.

## 6. Scale envelope

Per edge box, designed for: one to six detector feeds, up to ~5,000 monitored axles, sub-second inference per unit, disposition volume in the low hundreds per day. Beyond that, additional boxes — which is exactly what the per-site platform fee in D08/A2 prices.

## 7. Production decisions required — where the code differs today

**This section is the honest gap list. It must be emptied before any contract cites B01.**

| # | Item | Current state | Required for production |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Reviewer authentication | Free-text name + cert ID, unverified | AD-2: local accounts + signed cert registry |
| 2 | Ledger append-only | **Corrected 2026-11-09.** Insert-only write path; `supersedes_id` for corrections; `BEFORE UPDATE`/`BEFORE DELETE` triggers abort; SHA-256 chain across rows | Built — superseded decisions retained, chain verified on demand |
| 3 | Timestamps | SQLite `datetime('now')` default | Server-generated with NTP-synced clock |
| 4 | Storage durability | The demonstration environment's storage is ephemeral — the demo database is lost on spin-down | Persistent volume on Railroad hardware |
| 5 | Sensor ingest | **No inbound route exists.** Signals are generated from physics equations on synthetic traces; there is no endpoint, schema validation, timestamp check or plausibility filter in shipped code | Real detector payload schema, defined and versioned, **and the validation chain built and tested against it** |
| 6 | Time source | Host clock, unsynchronized | NTP to Railroad-approved source |
| 7 | Update mechanism | None; deploys via git | Offline signed update packages, see D06 |
| 8 | Audit export | Not implemented | Signed export bundle per §4.5; the re-verifiable chain now exists, the signature does not |
| 9 | Repo hygiene | `axiom.db` and `__pycache__` were committed | Corrected; `.gitignore` added |
| 10 | TLS on the box | Plain HTTP | TLS or network isolation; Railroad's internal standard |

Items 1 and 5 are **blocking** — the certification and detection claims cannot be made until they close. Items 3, 4, 6, 7 and 8 are required before a production licence, not before a demo. Items 2 and 9 are corrected. Item 10 is specific to the demonstration host and does not arise where the Platform runs on the Railroad's isolated network.

**Item 2, closed and what that changes.** The append-only guarantee is now enforced by the database, not by convention, and it is tested: a suite of 17 adversarial tests attempts an `UPDATE`, a `DELETE`, a second disposition, a tampered row and a removed row, and asserts each either fails or is detected. What remains open under items 3, 6 and 8 is the *provability* layer — a trusted clock and a signed, off-box export — not the append-only behaviour itself.

## 8. Costs of the architectural choices

Stated plainly, because the Railroad's IT team will find them anyway and it is better that we said it first.

**AD-1 (zero outbound) costs us:** no remote diagnostics — every support case needs the Railroad to export logs and send them; no usage telemetry, so our own product analytics are blind; updates must be shipped as signed offline packages and applied by Railroad staff (C01); licence enforcement must be offline (see D08/A2 — enforcement is contractual and cryptographic, not online).

**AD-2 (local accounts) costs the Railroad:** a second credential set alongside their directory, an admin who must issue and revoke certifications, and a joiner/mover/leaver process integration that is manual. In exchange, the platform has no path to their directory and cannot be used to pivot into it.

**These are the correct trade. A platform selling to a Class I railroad should be inspectable, offline, and boring.**

---

*Descriptive annex. Creates no warranty. Every item in §7 must be closed and re-verified against the running system before B01 is cited in an executed agreement.*

# AxiomDynamics — Current State

**Last updated:** 2026-11-09 (chat-3 — arithmetic pass, then the build history document)
**Repository:** `C:\Users\RGV\AxiomDynamics`
**Remote:** `github.com/kaanju19-lang/AxiomDynamics` (private)
**Push state:** run `git log --oneline origin/main..HEAD`. As last confirmed the
local remote-tracking ref stood at `b946678`, with the build-history commit ahead
of it. Never trust a hash written in this file — check with git, because this
file's own commit moves the top of the branch every time it is edited. Run
`PUSH-TO-GITHUB.bat` in the repo root. The sandbox cannot reach GitHub: `git push`
and `git fetch` both fail with HTTP 403 from the proxy, so a local `origin/main`
ref is not proof of what the remote holds.

---

## What this project is

Physics-first predictive maintenance for freight rail. Six named physical models
— thermodynamics with per-axle rolling z-score, peer median/MAD comparison,
kinematics, acoustics (BPFO/BPFI/BSF/FTF), same-axle left/right differential, and
an executive ROI panel — instead of black-box ML or fixed alarm thresholds.

The Master Brief Docket is in `client-assets/MASTER-BRIEF-DOCKET/`: 38 artifacts
— 36 Markdown documents, the A1 Excel model (with its build script beside it) and
the B03 HTML infographic — across A (commercial), B (technical), C (deployment)
and D (contractual) series plus F (forms).

## Build status

**38 artifacts on disk; 37 docket IDs on disk (A1 is a folder holding the `.xlsx`
and the builder, so it counts as one ID and two files).** The docket index (D00)
carries 37 ID rows; 34 are marked `**Built**` in bold, and B02 (.md) and B03
(.html) carry plain "Built" with a format qualifier. D00 Part IV is the authority
on status, not this file.

A long-form account of the whole build — every stage, every document, every
correction, and the loss and rebuild — is at
`project-logs/AxiomDynamics-Build-History-and-Working-Summary.docx` (29 pages).
It is generated by `project-logs/build-history-summary.js`; re-run
`node project-logs/build-history-summary.js` after a material change.

Open docket items are tracked in **D00 Part IV** — that table is the authority,
not this file.

## The largest known gap

**There is no detector ingest path.** No endpoint accepts a Railroad payload.
Every demonstration signal is generated from the physics equations on synthetic
traces. This is disclosed in B01 §7 gap #5, B02 §2 and the B03 status block.

Every demonstration number demonstrates **the method**, not the Railroad's data.
The validation chain — schema, timestamp, plausibility — is designed and not built.

## Open items, in priority order

1. **Two A2/D08 model findings — need an owner decision.** The arithmetic pass of
   2026-11-09 found **no arithmetic errors** in either document (78 of 78 figures
   recompute correctly). It did find that two *claims* do not reproduce from the
   shipped model. Full detail in
   `assets/a2-d08-arithmetic-pass-2026-11-09.md`; run the check with
   `python3 -I assets/a2-d08-arithmetic-pass.py`.
   - **Finding 1.** A2 §3.2 and D08 §3 claim ~2.0x return at 500 axles rising to
     ~4.1x at 10,000. The shipped models give 1.77x/3.36x on the A2 cost basis or
     2.36x/4.99x on A1's. No parameter set in the repo reproduces both anchors.
     The monotonic claim holds on every basis; the two anchor values do not.
   - **Finding 2.** D08 §5–§6 modelled benefits ($6–8M pilot year, $14–20M
     four-year, $40–60M six-year) run 5x–14x above the $696,675 annual benefit A1
     computes at identical inputs. D08 §5 states A1 must never be bypassed.
     One of the two models governs and it has not been chosen.
2. **D07 §14.5 — governing law and venue.** An open counsel decision, correctly
   labelled as open as of chat-2 (previously a blank pointing at an Order field
   that does not exist). Must be closed by signed addendum before first execution.
3. **A1 workbook regeneration.** Deliberately not regenerated during the
   arithmetic pass, because doing so would bake both open findings into a new
   file before the model question is settled. The builder is now fixed (see
   below) and will regenerate on demand once findings 1 and 2 are decided.
4. **D09 §4.4 supply-chain gaps** — SBOM (Q1 2027), hash verification of
   dependency downloads (Q1 2027), GPG-signed releases (Q2 2027). All disclosed.
5. **Signed, off-box ledger export** — the append-only ledger itself landed
   2026-11-09 (see below), which closed the overwrite gap. What remains is
   provability against a party holding the database file, and durability
   against disk loss: the export is not signed and the ledger is not
   replicated. D09 §4.4, B01 §7 items 6 and 8.

## Append-only disposition ledger — built 2026-11-09 (AD-3)

The gap that had been disclosed in six documents since `cf2e6ba` is closed at
the code level.

- `backend/store.py` rewritten. Records are inserted, never updated. A second
  decision on an advisory is a new row carrying `supersedes_id`; the earlier row
  keeps its content and timestamp. `BEFORE UPDATE` and `BEFORE DELETE` triggers
  `RAISE(ABORT)`, so the guarantee lives in the schema rather than in convention.
  Every row stores `prev_hash` and `record_hash` — a SHA-256 over its own
  canonical content plus the predecessor's hash — and `verify_chain()`
  recomputes the whole chain and names the first row that fails.
- Migration from the v1 one-row-per-advisory table runs inside `init_db()`,
  preserves the surviving decision and its original timestamp, and does not
  fabricate history that the old schema had already destroyed.
- 17 adversarial tests in `tests/test_store.py`: an UPDATE, a DELETE, a second
  disposition, a tampered row, a removed row, and two migration shapes. Each
  asserts the attempt fails or is detected. `tests/run_tests.py` now discovers
  every `test_*.py`, so the total suite is 38.
- New routes: `GET /api/warrant/{id}/disposition` (full trail, with `chain_ok`)
  and `GET /api/ledger/verify`. The dashboard shows the decision trail under the
  form and marks a corrected decision as superseding an earlier record.

**What it does not prove, and the docket now says so in these words:** the chain
is tamper-*evident*, not tamper-*proof*. A party with write access to the
database file can drop the triggers, rewrite rows and recompute every hash. That
is why items 6 and 8 above stay open.

Docket corrected in the same commit: B01 §4 and §7 items 2/8, D09 §4.4 and the
audit-logging row, F09 Part 6 and Part 7, F00, B02, C02, D12, D14 §5, D00 Part V
and Part VI, and the root README.

## A1 builder — fixed in chat-3

Two defects in `A1-ROI-MODEL/build_roi_calculator.py`, both cosmetic to the
workbook but both real if anyone runs it:

- The sheet-5 assumptions note attributed a **2% catastrophic escalation rate** to
  a model whose cell B17 has held **0.05%** since the correction. A reader
  reconciling the sheet against its own footnote would find a ten-fold conflict.
- The script saved to `/sessions/.../mnt/outputs/...`, a path inside the destroyed
  chat-1 sandbox, so running it raised `FileNotFoundError`. It now writes beside
  itself.


## Git state

The sandbox **cannot reach GitHub** — `git push` and `git fetch` both fail with
HTTP 403 from the proxy. Its `origin/main` ref therefore only advances when the
owner pushes and the sandbox is told the result. Do not trust it as evidence of
remote state without checking the commits page.

**Pushing is done by the owner**, with `PUSH-TO-GITHUB.bat` in the repo root. It
prints the commits waiting to go up and verifies afterwards.

**As of 2026-11-09, everything is pushed.** GitHub's top commit is `2ec168b`,
confirmed by the owner against the commits page.

**The host repo at `C:\Users\RGV\AxiomDynamics` is authoritative for push state.**
Verify by opening the commits page.

**The line-ending trap.** `git status` in this repo lists nearly every tracked file
as modified on a fresh Windows checkout. It is CRLF working-tree content against
LF blobs, not a content change — `git diff --ignore-cr-at-eol` returns empty.
There is no `.gitattributes` and `core.autocrlf` is unset. **Always check with
`--ignore-cr-at-eol` before believing a diff stat**, and never let an editor
rewrite a whole file's endings into a commit: doing so once during chat-3 turned a
two-line fix into 1,248 changed lines, which had to be reset and recommitted.


## What was lost in the chat-1 → chat-2 transition

Recorded here so nobody goes looking for it:

- Three commits built at the end of chat-1 (`0b66d21`, `cb4f74d`, and the
  F00/D07/Q6 work) existed only in the old sandbox. **`F00` Rule 7, the D07 §14
  rewrite and Q6 were rebuilt into the repository in chat-2.** The project-logs
  structure was rebuilt. The transcripts were not and cannot be — see
  `README.md`.
- Because the rebuild is a reconstruction rather than a recovery, the wording may
  differ from what chat-1 wrote. The *decisions* are identical; the prose is not
  guaranteed to be. Do not treat the current text as a restoration of an earlier
  draft.

## Standing instructions

- **[WORK LOCATION] All project work is written directly into this repository, first pass, and committed in the same pass.** No drafts in sandbox scratch space — that is how chat-1's final phase was lost.
- Keep the same concept throughout — consistency of framing across every document.
- Internal analysis goes in `assets/`, never `client-assets/`.
- Verify against the file before writing the claim.

## Why chat-1's work was lost — the mechanism

Not a deletion. The work was never on the owner's machine.

Chat-1 built the repo inside a temporary sandbox container. To get anything out

# F00 — Forms Register & Documentation Policy

**Docket position:** F00. The index and the policy for every executable form in the AxiomDynamics documentation system.

**Classification:** Client-facing.

---

## Part 1 — The documentation policy

These seven rules apply to every form, every agreement, and every record we produce. They are not stylistic preferences. They are the reason a small company can be trusted with a Class I carrier's operating risk.

### Rule 1 — Every commitment is in a document, and every document has a number.

Nothing is agreed by conversation. If a promise matters, it appears in a numbered document with a version and a date. A verbal assurance is not a commitment, and we do not act on one. This protects the customer as much as it protects us: a commitment they cannot point to is a commitment they cannot enforce.

### Rule 2 — Every form has exactly one purpose.

A form that does two things will eventually do both badly. The Change Order changes scope; the Acceptance form accepts a deliverable; the Travel form claims expenses. They do not substitute for each other. Where a process needs two of them, it uses two.

### Rule 3 — Every form states who signs and what happens if nobody does.

An unsigned form with no default is a process that stops. Every form in this register specifies the signatory and the consequence of silence. Where silence has a consequence, it is stated on the form itself, in plain words, not buried in a master agreement.

### Rule 4 — Plain language, with the technical term in brackets when one is needed.

We write "we" and "you" where the meaning is clear, and use the defined terms where precision requires it. Legalese is not a sign of professionalism; it is a sign the drafter could not decide what the sentence meant. Enterprise-grade means a document a Chief Engineer can read without calling legal.

Square brackets in this docket mean **one thing only: a defined term or an editorial substitution being offered to the reader**, as in "[the mediation rules of the chosen provider]". Brackets are never used to mark a blank to be filled in. Blanks are underscores (Rule 7). This distinction exists because the two were previously mixed, and a bracketed placeholder that is neither a definition nor a blank is a sentence nobody can act on.

### Rule 5 — Records are retained, and retention is stated on the record.

Every executed form is retained for the period stated in its own header. Nothing is discarded because it became inconvenient. The disposition ledger, the order register, and the certification registry are the three records that make everything else defensible.

### Rule 6 — A form records an event. It never varies a term.

**No form in this register can amend, override, or set aside A2 (Rate Card), D02 (Pilot Agreement), D03 (MSA) or D07 (Master Contract).** Where a completed form appears to conflict with one of those instruments, **the instrument governs and the form is corrected.**

This is the most important rule in this policy, because it is the one most likely to be broken by accident. A payment schedule that quietly restates a fee, a change order that alters liability, an acceptance that waives a warranty — each of these is a form doing something only a signed agreement may do. The forms exist to *evidence* what the agreements already permit; they are not a second, informal contract that bypasses the first.

### Rule 7 — A blank and a decision are different things, and the document says which it is.

Every unfilled field in this docket is one of exactly two kinds, and the drafter must know which before writing it:

**A fill-in blank** is a value that exists and will be entered at execution — a party name, a date, an amount agreed in the Order, an address for notices. It is written as underscores `________`, and it is safe to leave because the process that fills it is defined and the consequence of it staying empty is stated (Rule 3).

**An unmade decision** is a question the docket has not answered — which law governs, which arbitration seat, which entity form. It is **never** written as a blank, because a blank implies "we know that this will be filled in." An unmade decision is written as an **explicit open item**: the section states what has to be decided, who must decide it, and what happens in the meantime. A decision left unmade is a defect; a decision labelled as unmade is a work item. The difference between the two is the difference between a document that is quietly incomplete and one that is honestly incomplete.

**The prohibited pattern.** Never write a clause that points to a field which no document actually contains. An earlier draft of D07 §14.3 sent dispute venue to "[the courts / arbitration seat] stated in the Order signature block" — and no Order template has that field. The clause therefore described a decision as though it had already been made somewhere else, which is worse than either leaving it blank or admitting it was open: it read as complete to every person who did not go and check, and there was nothing to check. Where a term belongs in a separate instrument, the clause cites that instrument and section by number (Rule 1), not a field whose existence nobody has verified.

The lawful scope of each form is narrow and worth stating:

| Form | What it may decide | What it may never do |
|---|---|---|
| F02 Configuration Attestation | The date commissioning was completed and what the Customer certified | Change the term, the fee, or the acceptance standard |
| F03 Change Order | Scope, schedule, and price of one Order, with both signatures | Alter liability, IP, insurance or confidentiality — those are D07 and D03 only |
| F05 Payment Terms | The instalment split and invoice dates for one Order | Restate or discount a fee set by A2 |
| F06 Deliverable Acceptance | That a deliverable was accepted or rejected | Waive a warranty or a limitation of liability |
| F09 Disposition Record | What a reviewer decided, and when | Constitute regulatory evidence of inspection (D12 §3) |
| F11 Site Visit Report | What was observed, and what boundary was held | Create an obligation or a scope of work |

### The one rule that governs the others

**If a form does not exist for the thing you are about to do, stop and create the form. Do not do the thing and document it afterwards.**

This is the failure mode the entire docket exists to prevent: work performed, commitment made, no document. A form created before the act is evidence. A form created after the act is a reconstruction, and reconstruction is what the other side's lawyer attacks.

---

## Part 2 — Forms register

| ID | Form | Used when | Signatory | Default if unsigned |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **F00** | Forms Register & Documentation Policy | This document | — | — |
| **F01** | Site Readiness & Survey Questionnaire | Before any site deployment | Customer technical contact | No deployment scheduled |
| **F02** | Configuration Attestation | On commissioning at every site | Customer IT Director | **No Commissioning Date; pilot term does not start** |
| **F03** | Change Order | Any change to scope, price, schedule | Both authorised reps | Change does not take effect |
| **F04** | Travel Pre-Approval Request | Before booking any billable travel | Customer authorised rep | Travel is not billable |
| **F05** | Payment Terms Schedule | With every Order | Both parties | A2 §10 default terms apply |
| **F06** | Deliverable Acceptance | On delivery of a deliverable | Customer authorised rep | Deemed accepted after 10 Business Days |
| **F07** | Travel & Expense Claim | Within 14 days of travel | Supplier, countersigned by Customer | Not reimbursed |
| **F08** | Reviewer Certification Application | Before a reviewer is certified | Candidate + Customer sponsor | No certification issued |
| **F09** | Advisory Disposition Record | Every advisory, without exception | Certified Reviewer | **Disposition missing — D02 §5 obligation 5 breach** |
| **F10** | Security Incident Notification | On a reportable incident | Supplier or Customer | **Breach of D09 §6** |
| **F11** | Site Visit Report | After every on-site attendance | Supplier engineer | Visit undocumented; not billable |
| **F12** | Formal Notice | Contractual notices, termination, breach | Authorised signatory | Notice not effective |
| **F13** | Data Export & Transition Certificate | On termination or migration | Both parties | Data export not certified complete |

---

## Part 3 — How the forms fit together

### The pilot lifecycle

```
F01 Site Survey
   ↓
SOW-1 signed (D04)
   ↓
F04 Travel Pre-Approval (if on-site attendance)
   ↓
F11 Site Visit Report (after attendance)
   ↓
F07 Travel & Expense Claim (within 14 days)
   ↓
F02 Configuration Attestation  ←── THIS STARTS THE PILOT CLOCK
   ↓
F08 Reviewer Applications → certifications issued
   ↓
F09 Disposition Records (every advisory, throughout)
   ↓
F03 Change Order (if anything changes)
   ↓
F06 Acceptance (per deliverable)
   ↓
F05 Payment milestones
   ↓
Pilot evaluation report → D05 conversion election
```

### The three records that carry evidentiary weight

1. **F02 Configuration Attestation** — establishes the Commissioning Date and the configuration the Customer certified. Without it, there is no start date and no baseline for any later dispute about whether the environment changed.
2. **F09 Disposition Records** — the append-only ledger. Establishes what the human reviewer decided, when, and on what advisory. This is the record that answers "did someone look at this?" after an incident.
3. **F03 Change Orders** — establishes that scope moved deliberately rather than by drift.

**Note on F09 — implementation status.** The Platform's disposition write path is append-only as of 2026-11-09: records are inserted, never updated; a correction supersedes by reference; database triggers refuse `UPDATE` and `DELETE`; and each record is SHA-256 chained to its predecessor (AD-3; B01 §4.1, §4.6). F09's evidentiary claims now match the code at that level. Two things remain open and are disclosed in D09 §4.4: reviewer identity is asserted, not cryptographically verified (AD-2), and the ledger is neither signed nor replicated off-box. **Represent F09 as append-only; do not represent it as a provable-identity or tamper-proof record until those close.**

### The forms that protect the liability boundary

F11 and F09 together are what keep us on the right side of D14. F11 records what we observed and what we declined to advise. F09 records that a qualified human made the operating decision. Between them they answer the only two questions that matter after an incident: *what did the vendor say,* and *who decided to act.*

---

## Part 4 — Numbering and version control

**Form numbering:** F-prefix, sequential. Once issued, a number is never reused, even if the form is withdrawn.

**Order numbering:** `SOW-[template]-[YYYY]-[sequence]`. Example: `SOW-3-2026-004`.

**Version control:** every form carries a version and effective date in its header. A form is superseded, never edited in place. Superseded versions are retained — a dispute about a 2026 order is governed by the form in force in 2026, not the current one.

**Retention:** the period stated in each form's header. Where none is stated, seven years from the later of execution or the end of the engagement.

---

## Part 5 — What we do not have forms for, and why

Honesty about gaps is part of the policy.

1. **No purchase-order form.** The Customer's own PO process governs (D03 §4.1). We do not issue POs.
2. **No invoice template in this register.** Invoicing is a finance function; the payment terms are F05, and the invoice itself follows the Customer's AP requirements.
3. **No "letter of intent" or "MOU".** Either there is a signed Order or there is not. An LOI creates the appearance of commitment without the substance, and is the most common source of unpaid work.
4. **No verbal-agreement record form.** Verbal agreements are not recognised (Rule 1). There is deliberately no form to memorialise one.

---

*Documentation policy. Reviewed annually. Deviations require the written approval of the Principal Systems Architect.*

Where a term belongs in a separate instrument, the clause cites that instrument and section by number (Rule 1), not a field whose existence nobody has verified.
50	
51	The lawful scope of each form is narrow and worth stating:
52	
53	| Form | What it may decide | What it may never do |
54	|---|---|---|
55	| F02 Configuration Attestation | The date commissioning was completed and what the Customer certified | Change the term, the fee, or the acceptance standard |
56	| F03 Change Order | Scope, schedule, and price of one Order, with both signatures | Alter liability, IP, insurance or confidentiality — those are D07 and D03 only |
57	| F05 Payment Terms | The instalment split and invoice dates for one Order | Restate or discount a fee set by A2 |
58	| F06 Deliverable Acceptance | That a deliverable was accepted or rejected | Waive a warranty or a limitation of liability |
59	| F09 Disposition Record | What a reviewer decided, and when | Constitute regulatory evidence of inspection (D12 §3) |
60	| F11 Site Visit Report | What was observed, and what boundary was held | Create an obligation or a scope of work |
61	
62	### The one rule that governs the others
63	
64	**If a form does not exist for the thing you are about to do, stop and create the form. Do not do the thing and document it afterwards.**
65	
66	This is the failure mode the entire docket exists to prevent: work performed, commitment made, no document. A form created before the act is evidence. A form created after the act is a reconstruction, and reconstruction is what the other side's lawyer attacks.
67	
68	---
69	
70	## Part 2 — Forms register
71	
72	| ID | Form | Used when | Signatory | Default if unsigned |
73	|---|---|---|---|---|
74	| **F00** | Forms Register & Documentation Policy | This document | — | — |
75	| **F01** | Site Readiness & Survey Questionnaire | Before any site deployment | Customer technical contact | No deployment scheduled |
76	| **F02** | Configuration Attestation | On commissioning at every site | Customer IT Director | **No Commissioning Date; pilot term does not start** |
77	| **F03** | Change Order | Any change to scope, price, schedule | Both authorised reps | Change does not take effect |
78	| **F04** | Travel Pre-Approval Request | Before booking any billable travel | Customer authorised rep | Travel is not billable |
79	| **F05** | Payment Terms Schedule | With every Order | Both parties | A2 §10 default terms apply |
80	| **F06** | Deliverable Acceptance | On delivery of a deliverable | Customer authorised rep | Deemed accepted after 10 Business Days |
81	| **F07** | Travel & Expense Claim | Within 14 days of travel | Supplier, countersigned by Customer | Not reimbursed |
82	| **F08** | Reviewer Certification Application | Before a reviewer is certified | Candidate + Customer sponsor | No certification issued |
83	| **F09** | Advisory Disposition Record | Every advisory, without exception | Certified Reviewer | **Disposition missing — D02 §5 obligation 5 breach** |
84	| **F10** | Security Incident Notification | On a reportable incident | Supplier or Customer | **Breach of D09 §6** |
85	| **F11** | Site Visit Report | After every on-site attendance | Supplier engineer | Visit undocumented; not billable |
86	| **F12** | Formal Notice | Contractual notices, termination, breach | Authorised signatory | Notice not effective |
87	| **F13** | Data Export & Transition Certificate | On termination or migration | Both parties | Data export not certified complete |
88	
89	---
90	
91	## Part 3 — How the forms fit together
92	
93	### The pilot lifecycle
94	
95	```
96	F01 Site Survey
97	   ↓
98	SOW-1 signed (D04)
99	   ↓
100	F04 Travel Pre-Approval (if on-site attendance)
101	   ↓
102	F11 Site Visit Report (after attendance)
103	   ↓
104	F07 Travel & Expense Claim (within 14 days)
105	   ↓
106	F02 Configuration Attestation  ←── THIS STARTS THE PILOT CLOCK
107	   ↓
108	F08 Reviewer Applications → certifications issued
109	   ↓
110	F09 Disposition Records (every advisory, throughout)
111	   ↓
112	F03 Change Order (if anything changes)
113	   ↓
114	F06 Acceptance (per deliverable)
115	   ↓
116	F05 Payment milestones
117	   ↓
118	Pilot evaluation report → D05 conversion election
119	```
120	
121	### The three records that carry evidentiary weight
122	
123	1. **F02 Configuration Attestation** — establishes the Commissioning Date and the configuration the Customer certified. Without it, there is no start date and no baseline for any later dispute about whether the environment changed.
124	2. **F09 Disposition Records** — the append-only ledger. Establishes what the human reviewer decided, when, and on what advisory. This is the record that answers "did someone look at this?" after an incident.
125	3. **F03 Change Orders** — establishes that scope moved deliberately rather than by drift.
126	
127	**Note on F09 — implementation status.** The Platform's disposition write path is append-only as of 2026-11-09: records are inserted, never updated; a correction supersedes by reference; database triggers refuse `UPDATE` and `DELETE`; and each record is SHA-256 chained to its predecessor (AD-3; B01 §4.1, §4.6). F09's evidentiary claims now match the code at that level. Two things remain open and are disclosed in D09 §4.4: reviewer identity is asserted, not cryptographically verified (AD-2), and the ledger is neither signed nor replicated off-box. **Represent F09 as append-only; do not represent it as a provable-identity or tamper-proof record until those close.**
128	
129	### The forms that protect the liability boundary
130	
131	F11 and F09 together are what keep us on the right side of D14. F11 records what we observed and what we declined to advise. F09 records that a qualified human made the operating decision. Between them they answer the only two questions that matter after an incident: *what did the vendor say,* and *who decided to act.*
132	
133	---
134	
135	## Part 4 — Numbering and version control
136	
137	**Form numbering:** F-prefix, sequential. Once issued, a number is never reused, even if the form is withdrawn.
138	
139	**Order numbering:** `SOW-[template]-[YYYY]-[sequence]`. Example: `SOW-3-2026-004`.
140	
141	**Version control:** every form carries a version and effective date in its header. A form is superseded, never edited in place. Superseded versions are retained — a dispute about a 2026 order is governed by the form in force in 2026, not the current one.
142	
143	**Retention:** the period stated in each form's header. Where none is stated, seven years from the later of execution or the end of the engagement.
144	
145	---
146	
147	## Part 5 — What we do not have forms for, and why
148	
149	Honesty about gaps is part of the policy.
150	
151	1. **No purchase-order form.** The Customer's own PO process governs (D03 §4.1). We do not issue POs.
152	2. **No invoice template in this register.** Invoicing is a finance function; the payment terms are F05, and the invoice itself follows the Customer's AP requirements.
153	3. **No "letter of intent" or "MOU".** Either there is a signed Order or there is not. An LOI creates the appearance of commitment without the substance, and is the most common source of unpaid work.
154	4. **No verbal-agreement record form.** Verbal agreements are not recognised (Rule 1). There is deliberately no form to memorialise one.
155	
156	---
157	
158	*Documentation policy. Reviewed annually. Deviations require the written approval of the Principal Systems Architect.*
159

# D14 — Operating Model & Liability Boundary

**Docket position:** D14. Defines how the platform is installed, operated, supported and warranted. Operative across D02 (Pilot), D03 (MSA), D07 (Master Contract), D08 (Licensing) and D12 (Regulatory Status).

> **Drafting status:** Commercial grade. Requires counsel review — particularly §4 (Liability Boundary), which is the operative clause for the entire engagement model.

---

## 1. The model in one paragraph

AxiomDynamics supplies software. The Railroad installs it, operates it, supports it and staffs it. AxiomDynamics does not access the Railroad's production environment, does not perform the deployment, and does not act as the Railroad's engineering function. AxiomDynamics supplies updates, licensing administration, and optional premium builds. The Railroad's own IT organisation, trained against our documentation, performs every operational function.

**This is a deliberate allocation, not a limitation of service.** It exists so that each party carries the risk it can actually control.

## 2. Division of responsibility

| Function | AxiomDynamics | Railroad IT | Railroad Operations |
|---|:--:|:--:|:--:|
| Software development & release | **R** | I | — |
| Security patching & update packages | **R** | **A** (apply) | I |
| Installation & configuration | C | **R/A** | I |
| Network, hardware, OS | — | **R/A** | — |
| Detector integration & data feed | C | **R/A** | I |
| Platform operation & monitoring | — | **R/A** | I |
| First-line support & service desk | — | **R/A** | — |
| Personnel training & certification | C (materials) | **R/A** | **A** (completion) |
| Advisory review & disposition | — | — | **R/A** |
| Operating decisions | — | — | **R/A** |
| Regulatory reporting | — | C | **R/A** |
| Licence administration & billing | **R/A** | I | — |
| Premium builds (optional) | **R/A** | C | I |

R = responsible, A = accountable, C = consulted, I = informed.

**AxiomDynamics has no 'A' anywhere in the operational column.** That is the point of the model, and it must be visible to the Railroad's counsel in exactly this form.

## 3. What AxiomDynamics does not do

Stated affirmatively, because silence on these points will later be read as an assumption of duty:

- We do not access, connect to, log into, or administer the Railroad's production environment.
- We do not perform installation, integration, configuration, or commissioning. We may observe and advise; the Railroad executes and approves.
- We do not monitor the platform in operation. We have no visibility into its runtime state.
- We do not receive alerts, advisories, or disposition records. They remain on the Railroad's system.
- We do not provide operational support, dispatch assistance, or incident response for Railroad operations.
- We do not make, communicate, or influence any train-handling or operating decision.
- We do not act as engineer of record for any Railroad system or process.
- We do not assume any obligation to detect any specific defect on any specific unit.

## 4. The liability boundary — read this carefully

**There are two distinct liabilities, and this model only addresses one of them.**

**Operational liability** arises from what happens in the Railroad's environment — a bad install, a misconfigured feed, an unpatched host, a supervisor who ignored an advisory. **Our model removes us from nearly all of this**, because we never touch the environment and never make an operating decision. This is a genuine and valuable protection.

**Product liability** arises from the software itself — a defect in the inference, an equation that under-reports risk, a failure mode that was foreseeable and not guarded against. **Self-installation does not reduce this at all.** Under US law a software vendor can be treated as a manufacturer of a product, and a manufacturer remains liable for design defects regardless of who performed the installation. If our model misses a bearing because of how we implemented the physics, the fact that the Railroad installed it on their own hardware is not a defence — and in some analyses it is worse, because we can no longer demonstrate that the deployment was correct.

**Therefore:**

- The disclaimers and limitations in D07 must target **product** liability, not merely operational liability.
- The absence of assurance must be stated as a **product characteristic**, not just a responsibility allocation.
- Professional indemnity / technology E&O coverage is required before first deployment, and the Railroad will ask for certificates during vendor qualification.

**This distinction must not be blurred in any customer-facing material.** A buyer who believes we have disclaimed *all* liability and later discovers we have only disclaimed *operational* liability will feel misled, and a court will agree with them.

## 5. The signed disposition record

On each alert, the reviewing dispatcher records a disposition. The record captures the alert as fired and the reviewer's decision, bound together by a SHA-256 fingerprint over the record content with a timestamp.

**What this record proves:**

- The alert content presented to the reviewer, unaltered since the record was created.
- Which individual recorded the decision, and their asserted certification ID.
- The decision recorded and the time it was recorded.
- **That the decision history is append-only** (AD-3, built 2026-11-09): a later decision supersedes an earlier one rather than replacing it, both survive with their own content and timestamps, and neither can be edited or deleted through the Platform or by ordinary database access.

**What this record does not prove, and must not be represented as proving:**

- **That the alert fired when the record says it fired.** A hash over content establishes integrity, not chronology. Without an external time anchor, the timestamp is only as trustworthy as the system clock.
- **That the reviewer's identity was verified.** Until the certification registry (B01 AD-2) is operational, an identifier in a field is not an authenticated identity. The record proves *what was asserted*, not *who asserted it*.
- **That the underlying physics was correct.** The record evidences the decision process, not the accuracy of the advisory.
- **That the record is tamper-proof against someone holding the database file.** Append-only closes the *superseded-without-trace* risk. It does not close the *rewritten-and-rehashed* risk: a party with write access to the file can drop the guard triggers, rewrite rows and recompute the chain. That risk needs the signed, off-box digest in design consequence 1.

**Two design consequences:**

1. **Trusted time.** For the record to carry evidentiary weight, the timestamp needs an anchor the Railroad controls — a synchronised time source inside their network, and a periodic signed digest of the ledger that fixes its state at a known moment. In an air-gapped environment this must be internal; there is no external timestamping authority available. Design this deliberately rather than assuming the clock is right.

2. **Authentication is not signature.** A hash of a record authenticates the record. It does not make it an electronic signature in the legal sense, which requires attribution to a person, demonstrated intent to sign, and a reliable association between the signature and the record. The certification registry and an explicit attestation step are what turn a record into a signature. This matters if the record is ever relied upon in a regulatory or legal proceeding.

**Note the load this record now carries.** It is simultaneously (a) the Railroad's regulatory evidence, (b) the trigger for any outcome-linked fee in D08, and (c) the asset that determines the platform's eventual valuation. A record that cannot bear all three should be described as what it is — an operational log — and not as evidence.

## 6. Configuration attestation

Because we do not install, configure or monitor, **we cannot otherwise demonstrate that a given deployment was sound.** That is an exposure, and the answer is documentation rather than presence.

At commissioning, the Railroad's IT Director signs a **Configuration Attestation** recording: hardware and OS baseline, software version and hash, detector feed sources and formats, site identifiers, network topology summary, and the identity of the personnel who performed the work.

Thereafter, every version change is recorded the same way.

**Why we require this:** it is the only mechanism by which we can later establish that a defect claim arose from the software rather than from the installation. It protects the Railroad too — it is the record that a correct deployment existed. It costs one form per deployment and it is the cheapest insurance in this document.

**What we do not get from it:** visibility. We still cannot see their system. Attestation is a snapshot at a moment in time, not monitoring. If they reconfigure afterwards without telling us, we will not know, and the attestation will be stale. The attestation therefore has a validity period and requires re-attestation on change.

## 7. Support boundary

| Category | Provided by | Included in licence |
|---|---|---|
| First-line support, service desk, triage | Railroad | — |
| Platform administration, backup, recovery | Railroad | — |
| Operational incident response | Railroad | — |
| Defect correction in the software | **AxiomDynamics** | Yes |
| Security patches | **AxiomDynamics** | Yes |
| Update packages, documented and version-controlled | **AxiomDynamics** | Yes. **Signed packaging is on the D09 §4.4 roadmap (target Q2 2027); today packages are documented and hashed in the release notes but not GPG-signed.** |
| Licence administration | **AxiomDynamics** | Yes |
| Premium / optional builds | **AxiomDynamics** | Separately priced |

**The model is software maintenance, not operations support.** That is cleaner for both parties and it must be named that way in D06, because an ambiguous support clause will be read against the supplier.

**The exposure this creates, stated plainly:** if the platform fails at 03:00 and the Railroad's team cannot restore it, the operational consequence is entirely theirs and they will feel it as our failure regardless of what the contract says. **Mitigation is documentation quality and recovery testing, not contractual language.** C01 (the self-deployment SOP, whose backup section requires the Railroad to test recovery) and F01 (site readiness, which establishes that the Railroad has the people and procedures to restore the system before we ever ship it) are load-bearing prerequisites of this model, not optional extras. **Both exist. A documented recovery-drill record is a Phase 2 assurance artifact** — see D00 Part VI. Until it exists, treat "the Railroad can restore this without us" as a design requirement we have written down, not as a tested property.

## 8. Representational discipline — the most important section

**The largest liability in this entire model is not technical. It is the gap between how the product is described in a sales conversation and what the contract says.**

If the platform is marketed as detecting failures 18–48 hours before they occur, and the contract disclaims any assurance of detection, then:

- a misrepresentation claim becomes available independent of the contract;
- the disclaimer may be argued to be inconsistent with the express representations made to induce the purchase;
- and the Railroad's procurement record will contain both documents.

**The resolution is not stronger disclaimers. It is identical language.**

Every description of the product — website, deck, email, dossier, verbal — must say the same thing the contract says:

> AxiomDynamics produces a physics-derived, ranked risk assessment for review by a qualified railroad employee. It does not detect failures with certainty, does not replace any required inspection, does not make operating decisions, and provides no assurance that any particular defect will be identified. The Railroad retains sole operating authority.

Any material saying otherwise must be withdrawn. **This is enforceable discipline or it is nothing** — one slide that says "prevents derailments" undoes the whole structure.

## 9. What this model requires from the Railroad

Stated so that the obligation is mutual and visible:

1. **Certified personnel.** Reviews performed only by individuals who have completed C02 certification and hold a current credential.
2. **Adequate resources.** Staffing sufficient to review advisories within the Railroad's own operational timeframes. An unreviewed advisory is worse than no advisory.
3. **Maintained infrastructure.** Detector hardware maintained to the Railroad's standards and AAR recommended practice; time source synchronised; hosts patched.
4. **Version currency.** Applying released security patches within a defined window. **A Railroad running an unsupported version is outside the warranty in D07** — this must be explicit.
5. **Change notification.** Informing us of configuration changes that affect the platform.
6. **Disposition discipline.** Recording a disposition for every advisory, positively or negatively, without exception. A ledger with gaps is not evidence.

## 10. Summary of residual exposure

Accepted and documented rather than hidden:

| Exposure | Status |
|---|---|
| Product liability for design defects | **Retained.** Cannot be disclaimed away. Requires insurance. |
| Loss of visibility into deployment correctness | Mitigated by Configuration Attestation, not eliminated |
| Support gap when Railroad team cannot restore service | Accepted; mitigated by documentation and recovery testing |
| Evidentiary weight of disposition records limited by clock trust | Requires trusted-time design (§5) |
| Misrepresentation from marketing/contract mismatch | **Fully controllable, and therefore inexcusable if it occurs** |

---

*Commercial and operational terms. Not legal advice. §4 and §5 require review by counsel in the relevant jurisdiction before execution. The product-liability analysis and any reliance on disclaimers must be confirmed locally.*

117	**The model is software maintenance, not operations support.** That is cleaner for both parties and it must be named that way in D06, because an ambiguous support clause will be read against the supplier.
118	
119	**The exposure this creates, stated plainly:** if the platform fails at 03:00 and the Railroad's team cannot restore it, the operational consequence is entirely theirs and they will feel it as our failure regardless of what the contract says. **Mitigation is documentation quality and recovery testing, not contractual language.** C01 (the self-deployment SOP, whose backup section requires the Railroad to test recovery) and F01 (site readiness, which establishes that the Railroad has the people and procedures to restore the system before we ever ship it) are load-bearing prerequisites of this model, not optional extras. **Both exist. 120

122	
123	**The largest liability in this entire model is not technical. It is the gap between how the product is described in a sales conversation and what the contract says.**
124	
125	If the platform is marketed as detecting failures 18–48 hours before they occur, and the contract disclaims any assurance of detection, then:
126	
127	- a misrepresentation claim becomes available independent of the contract;
128	- the disclaimer may be argued to be inconsistent with the express representations made to induce the purchase;
129	- and the Railroad's procurement record will contain both documents.
130	
131	**The resolution is not stronger disclaimers. It is identical language.**
132	
133	Every description of the product — website, deck, email, dossier, verbal — must say the same thing the contract says:
134

136	
137	Any material saying otherwise must be withdrawn. **This is enforceable discipline or it is nothing** — one slide that says "prevents derailments" undoes the whole structure.
138	
139	## 9. What this model requires from the Railroad
140	
141	Stated so that the obligation is mutual and visible:
142	
143	1. **Certified personnel.** Reviews performed only by individuals who have completed C02 certification and hold a current credential.
144	2. **Adequate resources.** Staffing sufficient to review advisories within the Railroad's own operational timeframes. An unreviewed advisory is worse than no advisory.

148	6. **Disposition discipline.** Recording a disposition for every advisory, positively or negatively, without exception. A ledger with gaps is not evidence.
149

151	
152	Accepted and documented rather than hidden:

155	|---|---|
156	| Product liability for design defects | **Retained.** Cannot be disclaimed away. Requires insurance. |
157	| Loss of visibility into deployment correctness | Mitigated by Configuration Attestation, not eliminated |
158	| Support gap when Railroad team cannot restore service | Accepted; mitigated by documentation and recovery testing |
159	| Evidentiary weight of disposition records limited by clock trust | Requires trusted-time design (§5) |
160	| Misrepresentation from marketing/contract mismatch | **Fully controllable, and therefore inexcusable if it occurs** |
161
